43888501.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了视频游戏中的作弊问题以及游戏公司如何打击作弊行为。随着网络竞技的发展，作弊已成为一个利润丰厚的产业，作弊者通过销售不公平的优势获利。为了应对这一问题，游戏开发商加强了反作弊团队，其中Riot Games开发的Vanguard反作弊系统尤为突出。Vanguard在操作系统内核层面运行，能够深入监控玩家的电脑，每天禁言大量作弊者。Riot利用Windows的安全功能，检查硬件驱动程序更新，防止作弊软件加载和执行代码。此外，Riot还通过渗透作弊社区、使用虚假身份获取作弊信息，并运用心理战术揭露和打击作弊者。尽管面临挑战，Riot的努力已见成效，其游戏《Valorant》中作弊行为比例已降至不到1%。
43888501.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：游戏反作弊系统，特别是内核级反作弊技术的使用及其隐私、安全和系统稳定性影响

不同观点：
• 反对内核级反作弊技术：
   - 认为内核级反作弊（如Riot的Vanguard）是对隐私的侵犯，可能被用于收集用户数据，尤其是与中国有关的公司时更加令人担忧（[prkl]）。
   - 这种技术类似于警察在每个人的房子里安装摄像头，本质上是不合适的（[prkl]）。
   - 内核级反作弊技术不稳定，可能导致系统崩溃和蓝屏（[snailmailman]，[OrvalWintermute]）。
   - 用户不愿意为玩游戏而让出系统的底层控制权，尤其是当这种技术可能带来安全隐患时（[shmerl]，[josephcsible]）。

• 支持内核级反作弊技术：
   - 一些玩家和开发者认为内核级反作弊是有效的对抗作弊手段，尤其是在免费游戏中，能够防止大多数作弊行为（[arh68]）。
   - 部分人认为玩家并没有对反作弊系统表现出明显的反感，且这种技术对游戏公平性有帮助（[arh68]）。

• 对反作弊技术的替代方案讨论：
   - 提出可以通过收费账户等方式减少作弊者，而不需要内核级反作弊技术（[oliwarner]）。
   - 未来可能通过Windows的安全功能实现用户级别的反作弊系统，减少内核级干预（[doikor]）。
   - 有人提出游戏流媒体服务可能是一种避免在本地硬件运行反作弊系统的方法（[to-too-two]）。

补充讨论：
• 反作弊技术对系统和多操作系统的干扰：
   - 安全启动（Secure Boot）可能影响双系统用户，尤其是那些使用非主流操作系统（如Haiku）的用户（[smallstepforman]）。
   
• 作弊问题和游戏公司的责任：
   - 有评论指出，一些游戏公司（如Valve）对作弊问题重视不够，可能因为作弊者与皮肤交易者有重叠，成为收入来源（[jokoon]）。

• 对内核级反作弊技术是否为“恶意软件”或“rootkit”的质疑：
   - 有用户直接称这种技术为“rootkit”或“恶意软件风格的访问”（[ziggure]，[shmerl]）。

争议焦点：内核级反作弊技术是否必要，及其对用户隐私和系统安全的潜在影响。

data.title: Reading Zanzibar
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
《Zanzibar：Google的全球一致授权系统》描述了一个用于授权的系统，支持灵活且可扩展的权限管理。Zanzibar被Google的多种应用程序使用，能够应对极大用户规模和全球分布的需求。该系统通过对象、用户、命名空间、用户组、用户组重写规则和元组等基本元素，实现灵活的授权规则设定。它避免了对ID格式或特定关系做出假设，具有高度抽象性。

Zanzibar基于分布式架构，利用Google的Spanner数据库实现高一致性，并通过独特的时钟技术（TrueTime）解决数据一致性问题。系统还通过多服务器架构和缓存方案解决扩展性和热点问题。

总结来说，Zanzibar提供了一个灵活的基于关系的访问控制模型，并能够在全球范围内为应用程序提供一致的授权服务。许多公司和开源项目都受到了Zanzibar的启发，展示了其广泛影响力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zanzibar作为权限管理系统的实现及其在分布式系统中的应用

不同观点：
• [whs的观点] 尝试修改Zanzibar以作为API网关而不是权限存储。他们希望权限验证由各服务自己处理，而不是集中存储在Zanzibar中。这种方法在分布式系统中存在挑战，例如在异步任务中用户权限被撤销时如何处理。Zanzibar依赖于其内部存储来进行权限变更通知，如果没有这个存储，权限变更的实时性会受到影响。此外，缓存失效也是一个问题。最终，[whs]认为这是一个职业失误。

• [jauntywundrkind的观点] 认为近年来实现Zanzibar的障碍已经减少，尤其是由于Google的Spanner数据库和其TrueTime技术使得时间戳排序更加精确。即使没有Spanner，像CockroachDB这样的数据库也在模仿Spanner的模型。此外，现代GPS和原子钟技术已经变得更加可负担和精确。对于大多数系统而言，极高精度的时间同步可能并非绝对必要，因为高级攻击很少见。此外，评论还提到了skip-lists数据结构在Zanzibar中的应用，并对其在统计学中的整合表示赞赏。

补充讨论：
• [whs]提到的具体实现问题：在异步任务中如何处理权限撤销，以及缓存失效和权限变更通知的问题。
• [jauntywundrkind]对时间同步问题的深入分析，以及现代技术如何降低实现高精度时间同步的成本和复杂性。
• 争议的焦点在于是否需要在权限验证系统中实现极高精度的时间同步，以及在没有内部存储的情况下如何有效处理权限变更和缓存失效问题。

通过以上分析，可以看出两位评论者从不同角度探讨了Zanzibar在实际应用中的挑战和解决方案，包括权限存储与验证、时间同步精度以及系统威胁分析等具体技术问题。

43878868.article_content:
Reading Zanzibar
Google published
Zanzibar: Google’s Consistent, Global Authorization System
in 2019. It describes a system for authorization – enforcing who can do what – which maxes out both flexibility and scalability. Google has lots of different apps that rely on Zanzibar, and bigger scale than practically any other company, so it needed Zanzibar.
The Zanzibar paper made quite a stir. There are at least four companies that advertise products as being inspired by or based on Zanzibar. It says a lot for everyone to loudly reference this paper on homepages and marketing materials: companies aren’t advertising their own innovation as much as simply saying they’re following the gospel.
A short list of companies & OSS products I found:
Companies
WorkOS
FGA
Authzed
auth0 FGA
Ory
Permify
Open source
Ory Keto
(Go)
Warrant
(Go) probably the basis for WorkOS FGA, since WorkOS acquired Warrant.
SpiceDB
(Go) the basis for Authzed.
Permify
(Go)
OpenFGA
(Go) the basis of auth0 FGA.
I read the paper, and have a few notes, but
the Google Zanzibar Paper, annotated by AuthZed
is the same thing from a real domain expert (albeit one who works for one of these companies), so read that too, or instead.
Features
My brief summary is that the Zanzibar paper describes the
features
of the system succinctly, and those features are really appealing. They’ve figured out a few primitives from which developers can build really flexible authorization rules for almost any kind of application. They avoid making assumptions about ID formats, or any particular relations, or how groups are set up. It’s abstract and beautiful.
The gist of the system is:
Objects: things in your data model, like documents
Users: needs no explanation
Namespaces: for isolating applications
Usersets: groups of users
Userset rewrite rules: allow usersets to inherit from each other or have other kinds of set relationships
Tuples, which are like
(object)#(relation)@(user)
, and are sort of the core ‘rule’ construct for saying who can access what
There’s then a neat configuration language which looks like this in an example:
name: "doc"
relation { name: "owner"}
relation {
name: "editor"
userset_rewrite {
union {
child { _this f } }
child { computed_userset { relation: "owner" } }
relation {
name: "viewer"
userset_rewrite {
union {
child {_this f} }
child { computed_userset & relation: "editor" 3 }
child { tuple_to_userset {
tupleset { relation: "parent" }
computed_userset {
object: $TUPLE_USERSET_OBJECT # parent folder
relation: "viewer"
} } }
} } }
It’s pretty neat. At this point in the paper I was sold on Zanzibar: I could see this as being a much nicer way to represent authorization than burying it in a bunch of queries.
Specifications & Implementation details
And then the paper discusses specifications: how much scale it can handle, and how it manages consistency. This is where it becomes much more noticeably Googley.
So, with Google’s scale and international footprint, all of their services need to be globally distributed. So Zanzibar is a distributed system, and it is also a system that needs good consistency guarantees so that it avoid the “new enemy” problem, nobody is able to access resources that they shouldn’t, and applications that are relying on Zanzibar can get a consistent view of its data.
Pages 5-11 are about this challenge, and it is a big one with a complex, high-end solution, and a lot of details that are very specific to Google. Most noticeably, Zanzibar is built with
Spanner
Google’s distributed database, and Spanner has the
ability to order timestamps using TrueTime
, which relies on atomic clocks and GPS antennae: this is not standard equipment for a server. Even CockroachDB, which is explicitly modeled off of Spanner,
can’t rely on having GPS & atomic clocks around
so it has to take a very different approach. But this time accuracy idea is pretty central to Zanzibar’s idea of
zookies
, which are sort of like tokens that get sent around in its API and indicate what time reference the client expects so that a follow-up response doesn’t accidentally include stale data.
To achieve scalability, Zanzibar is also a multi-server architecture: there are aclservers, watchservers, a Leopard indexing system that creates compressed
skip list
-based representations of usersets. There’s also a clever solution to the caching & hot-spot problem, in which certain objects or tuples will get lots of requests all at once so their database shard gets overwhelmed.
Conclusions
Zanzibar is two things:
A flexible, relationship-based access control model
A system to provide that model to applications at enormous scale and with consistency guarantees
My impressions of these things match with AuthZed’s writeup so I’ll just quote & link them:
There seems to be a lot of confusion about Zanzibar. Some people think all relationship-based access control is “Zanzibar”. This section really brings to light that the ReBAC concepts have already been explored in depth, and that Za

data.title: Why Flatpak apps use so much disk space on Linux
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Linux 包管理工具（如 Flatpak、Snap）的优缺点，尤其是在存储空间、时间和资源消耗方面的影响。

不同观点：
• [loloquwowndueo] 认为包管理工具（特别是 Snap）不尊重用户的计算机资源，导致系统和人的时间成本增加，尤其是在更新时会严重拖慢系统。
• [INTPenis] 表示 Flatpak 在其日常使用中影响不大，虽然占用一定空间，但因为使用不多，所以可以接受，特别是其容器化的优点。
• [qbane] 关注 Flatpak 存储空间无限制增长的问题，引用多个社区和问题报告来说明该问题的普遍性。
• [massysett] 以幽默的方式指出 Flatpak 与 IKEA 平包的对比，指出 Flatpak 实际上增加了空间占用，而不是减少。
• [mcv] 建议允许不同版本的库共存，而不是打包所有依赖，以减少空间占用，类似于 npm 的做法。
• [jasonpeacock] 对 Flatpak 不适合服务器使用的观点提出疑问，想知道具体是哪些桌面特性导致这一问题。
• [Havoc] 以讽刺的方式表达对“在我的电脑上能运行，我们就发布我的电脑”这种做法的不满。
• [account-5] 比较了 Windows 的便携式应用程序和 Linux 的 Flatpak，质疑为什么 Linux 的解决方案会如此不同。
• [_Soulou] 关注 Flatpak 的内存使用问题，认为多次加载相同库的不同版本会增加内存消耗。
• [butz] 提出通过选择相同运行时版本来减少 Flatpak 的磁盘空间占用，并讨论了运行时版本过渡期间可能导致的多版本问题。
• [wltr] 对原文内容的低质量表示不满，认为评论比文章本身更有价值。
• [haunter] 质疑 Flatpak 比 Appimage 更流行的原因，认为 Appimage 更便携。
• [ReptileMan] 批评不断尝试重新发明静态链接器，认为这是在重复 Windows 的 DLL 地狱问题。
• [gjsman-1000] 对比了 Linux 桌面和任天堂的 Horizon 操作系统，认为现代操作系统设计应该更简洁和高效。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于 Flatpak 和 Snap 等包管理工具在存储空间和资源消耗上的影响，尤其是它们是否对用户计算机造成了不必要的负担。
• 不同用户对 Flatpak 的体验和看法各异，有的用户认为其影响不大，而有的用户则认为问题严重。
• 对如何有效管理库版本和减少空间占用提出了多种建议和比较，包括与 Windows 的 npm 等工具的对比。
• 对 Flatpak 和 Appimage 的流行程度和优劣也有一定的讨论和不同看法。
• 部分用户对现代 Linux 桌面环境的复杂性和效率提出了批评和反思。

• [gjsman-1000] 对比了 Linux 桌面和任天堂的 Horizon 操作系统，认为现代操作系统设计应该更简洁和高效。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于 Flatpak 和 Snap 等包管理工具在存储空间和资源消耗上的影响，尤其是它们是否对用户计算机造成了不必要的负担。
• 不同用户对 Flatpak 的体验和看法各异，有的用户认为其影响不大，而有的用户则认为问题严重。
• 对如何有效管理库版本和减少空间占用提出了多种建议和比较，包括与 Windows 的 npm 等工具的对比。
• 对 Flatpak 和 Appimage 的流行程度和优劣也有一定的讨论和不同看法。
• 部分用户对现代 Linux 桌面环境的复杂性和效率提出了批评和反思。

data.title: AI code is legacy code?
data.author: krrishd
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI对编程和代码维护的影响，尤其是对遗留代码和LLM（大语言模型）生成代码的讨论。

不同观点：
• [kachapopopow] 认为未来可能完全不需要人类编程，所有的代码和系统都可以由AI自动生成，甚至硬件规格也可以由AI决定，最终可能只需要一个“魔法盒子”来处理所有输入和输出。
• [peteforde] 强调使用AI工具（如Cursor）生成代码的过程需要谨慎，编码者应保持批判性思维，不应盲目接受AI的建议。他认为AI可以帮助程序员在未知领域快速上手，但程序员仍需对代码负责。
• [dang] 引用了Peter Naur的“编程作为理论构建”的观点，讨论了LLM是否能够构建或需要“理论”。他提出，如果程序是由AI生成的，那么AI可能拥有该理论，而人类则不一定。
• [gregwebs] 认为AI在编写测试和文档方面表现出色，可以帮助确保高质量的代码。他强调测试对于防止代码快速变为遗留代码的重要性。
• [lacker] 指出AI在处理不同复杂程度的编码任务时表现不同，简单的任务如创建前端界面和复杂的任务如重构代码有显著差异。
• [nialv7] 认为LLM虽然没有隐藏状态（如人类程序员），但可以通过对话日志重现其内部输出，这在某种程度上比人类更可靠。
• [mrweasel] 分享了使用AI编码可能有助于处理技术债务的经验，特别是在存储提示和生成代码的关联方面，可以帮助理解代码的背景。
• [OnlyMortal] 认为所有代码从诞生起就是遗留代码，因为业务需求总是在变化，AI工具如Copilot在处理模板代码方面表现尚可，但在解决问题方面则不尽如人意。
• [DevKoala] 表示AI生成的代码非常成功，只需提供需求和系统设计，AI可以生成通常需要外包的代码，但仍需人工审查和测试生成的代码。
• [ozim] 强调了AI生成代码的版权问题，指出如果公司依赖AI生成的代码，可能在版权纠纷中处于不利地位。
• [hollerith] 担心未来的AI将不得不维护遗留代码，这将是一个巨大的挑战。
• [closewith] 指出遗留代码往往是企业盈利最高的代码，因此在说服管理层不使用AI编码工具时，这不是一个有力的角度。
• [colesantiago] 认为AI生成代码将带来新的工作机会，AI工具的使用将创造更多就业机会。
• [rufius] 认为代码从第一天起就是遗留代码。
• [BSOhealth] 展望了未来的“有机、自愈代码”，认为当前的持续集成和持续交付（CICD）方法将显得非常幼稚。

补充讨论：
• AI是否能够构建或需要“理论”是讨论的核心之一，涉及AI生成代码的质量和可维护性。
• 版权问题和AI生成代码的法律地位也是一个值得关注的讨论点。
• 遗留代码的定义和处理技术债务的方法在讨论中被多次提及，显示出其在软件开发中的重要性。
• 对AI在编程中角色的不同看法，从完全替代人类到辅助工具，反映了对技术发展的不同预期。

data.title: Distributed Continuous GPU Profiling
data.author: tdullien
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一款由zystem.io推出的分布式GPU性能分析工具——zymtrace，旨在解决GPU利用率低下的问题。许多企业投入巨资购买和运行GPU集群，但由于缺乏有效的性能监控，GPU常常处于闲置或低效状态，导致训练时间长、推理成本高和能源浪费。zymtrace通过提供轻量级、无摩擦的连续性能分析，帮助AI/ML工程师精确定位CUDA内核中的性能瓶颈，优化推理批次大小，并消除空闲GPU周期。该工具能够将GPU性能问题直接追溯到PyTorch代码、CUDA内核或调度线程，并与CPU代码路径相关联，提供全面的工作负载可视化。这使得GPU优化变得更加简单高效，现已在多个企业环境中成功部署并公开推出。

data.title: Why can't HTML alone do includes?
data.author: susam
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了为何HTML本身不支持"包含"功能（includes），即在多个页面重复使用同一段HTML代码。作者指出，虽然有许多解决方案，如JavaScript、静态站点生成器、模板语言和后端语言等，但这些都不是纯HTML的原生方式。作者质疑为何CSS和JavaScript可以导入自身的文件，而HTML却不支持类似的功能，并探讨了可能的原因，包括性能问题、异步加载、复杂性、嵌套包含的处理等。评论中有人认为这是因为HTML已成为"死亡标准"，不再有重大版本更新，而开发者不得不依赖其他工具实现所需功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：HTML是否需要原生的"includes"功能，以简化网页开发中的重复内容问题。

不同观点：
• dwheeler：HTML历史上是SGML的应用，而SGML支持"includes"功能。随着HTML的简化，这一功能被舍弃。
• dimal：支持原生客户端"includes"方法，认为iframes和服务器端解决方案都不理想。
• throwup238：提到HTML Imports提案，因缺乏厂商支持而被废弃，指出Google曾在Blink中实现该提案。
• Lammy：提到Netscape 4中的<ILAYER>标签，可以实现类似的功能。
• Null-Set：将此功能称为transclusion，并提到其在Project Xanadu和mediawiki中的应用。
• Linux-Fan：认为framesets可以解决此问题，但因设计上的局限性和移动端的兼容性问题而被淘汰。
• rchaud：认为"includes"功能应由服务器端处理，HTML是展示格式，需结合CSS和JS使用。
• socalgal2：指出HTML include可能导致链接和结构上的复杂性，认为生成页面时不需要浏览器支持include。
• uallo：提到WHATWG有一个关于客户端include功能的开放问题。
• austin-cheney：认为frames曾提供类似功能，但因安全性和可访问性问题而失去青睐。
• Kuyawa：提供了一种使用JavaScript实现include功能的变通方法。
• simonjgreen：提到SSI（服务器端包含）在过去提供了有效的缓存解决方案。
• rorylaitila：认为尽管服务器端渲染解决了此问题，但有些情况下不希望运行服务器或静态站点生成器，希望有简单的HTML includes功能。
• 1718627440：从语义角度解释HTML文档和节点组合的区别，认为HTML文档是完整的传输单元。
• kyledrake：批评HTML规范制定者在设计时未充分考虑手写HTML的需求，提到<xmp>标签的废弃问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到多种历史技术，如SGML、framesets、<ILAYER>标签和HTML Imports，显示了在不同阶段解决同样问题的多种尝试。
• 争议的焦点在于是否需要在HTML中重新引入类似"includes"的功能，以及这种功能应在客户端还是服务器端实现。
• 不同意见还涉及到技术实现的复杂性、安全性和可访问性问题，以及现代网页开发中对简化流程的需求。
• 有提到当前的变通方法，如JavaScript和服务器端解决方案，但这些方法在不同场景中各有优缺点。

• throwup238：提到HTML Imports提案，因缺乏厂商支持而被废弃，指出Google曾在Blink中实现该提案。
• Lammy：提到Netscape 4中的<ILAYER>标签，可以实现类似的功能。
• Null-Set：将此功能称为transclusion，并提到其在Project Xanadu和mediawiki中的应用。
• Linux-Fan：认为framesets可以解决此问题，但因设计上的局限性和移动端的兼容性问题而被淘汰。
• rchaud：认为"includes"功能应由服务器端处理，HTML是展示格式，需结合CSS和JS使用。
• socalgal2：指出HTML include可能导致链接和结构上的复杂性，认为生成页面时不需要浏览器支持include。
• uallo：提到WHATWG有一个关于客户端include功能的开放问题。
• austin-cheney：认为frames曾提供类似功能，但因安全性和可访问性问题而失去青睐。
• Kuyawa：提供了一种使用JavaScript实现include功能的变通方法。
• simonjgreen：提到SSI（服务器端包含）在过去提供了有效的缓存解决方案。
• rorylaitila：认为尽管服务器端渲染解决了此问题，但有些情况下不希望运行服务器或静态站点生成器，希望有简单的HTML includes功能。
• 1718627440：从语义角度解释HTML文档和节点组合的区别，认为HTML文档是完整的传输单元。
• kyledrake：批评HTML规范制定者在设计时未充分考虑手写HTML的需求，提到<xmp>标签的废弃问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到多种历史技术，如SGML、framesets、<ILAYER>标签和HTML Imports，显示了在不同阶段解决同样问题的多种尝试。
• 争议的焦点在于是否需要在HTML中重新引入类似"includes"的功能，以及这种功能应在客户端还是服务器端实现。
• 不同意见还涉及到技术实现的复杂性、安全性和可访问性问题，以及现代网页开发中对简化流程的需求。
• 有提到当前的变通方法，如JavaScript和服务器端解决方案，但这些方法在不同场景中各有优缺点。

data.author: Lammy
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了CORBA（公共对象请求代理架构）的历史、功能、优势及实际应用，并讨论了Netscape计划如何在其产品线中集成CORBA，以支持企业内部网、外部网及互联网的下一代应用程序。CORBA通过对象请求代理（ORB）连接客户端和分布式对象，无需考虑操作系统和编程语言的差异。它具有平台和语言独立性，支持软件组件的重用和共享，降低开发成本和复杂性。CORBA结合Java，支持跨平台对象互操作，提供了诸如事务、安全、命名等丰富服务，为开发人员和企业IT部门带来了选择灵活性和互操作性优势。

CORBA: C
ATCHING THE
N
EXT
W
AVE
June 5, 1997
This white paper presents CORBA - its history, features and benefits, and
practical applications. It also describes Netscape's plans to integrate
CORBA across its product line, enabling the next generation of applications
for intranets, extranets, and the Internet.
C
ONTENTS
What is CORBA?
CORBA Everywhere
How CORBA Works
CORBA in Action
The Netscape Advantage
Competition
Conclusion
Further Reading
back to top
W
HAT IS
CORBA?
Distributed objects are the next wave in Internet innovation. CORBA, the
Common Object Request Broker Architecture defined by the Object Management
Group (OMG), specifies how software objects distributed over a network
can work together without regard to client and server operating systems
and programming languages.
CORBA is a complete distributed object platform. It extends applications
across networks, languages, component boundaries, and operating systems.
A CORBA Object Request Broker (ORB) connects a client application with
the objects it wishes to use. The client application does not need to know
whether the object resides on the same computer or on a remote computer
elsewhere on the network. The client application needs to know only two
pieces of information: the object's name and how to use the object's interface.
The ORB takes care of the details of locating the object, routing the request,
and returning the result.
H
ISTORY
As CORBA grew, three influential trends were taking shape:
The software development community realized the importance of
object-oriented
programming
techniques, even though they'd been around for the better
part of two decades.
Industry leaders-including IBM, Microsoft, and Apple-were advocating new
application models based on small,
task-specific components
. Because
they are smaller than general-purpose applications, components are easier
to write and update. Developers can, conveniently and cheaply, upgrade
only those parts of their software that are out of date, and users don't
have to purchase new versions of the entire package. Also, small components
can be distributed over a network more easily than their monolithic ancestors.
With component architectures comes the promise of a cross-platform future
where components running on different systems work together seamlessly.
Just after the release of CORBA 2.0 in early 1995, the
Java programming
language
burst forth, as if to validate the concepts underlying the
vision of an object-oriented, component-based future. Java provided an
object-oriented development environment for producing small software components
that could run on any operating system with a Java virtual machine. And
the components could be used over the Internet, which by then was surging
in popularity.
CORBA fits the component-based and Internet-based approaches to building
and using software. It defines a way to divide application logic among
objects distributed over a network, some on clients, others on a variety
of servers. It also defines a way for those objects to communicate and
use each others' services. CORBA supplements Java with a rich set of services
that includes introspection, dynamic discovery, transactions, security,
naming, and more. CORBA links the Java mobile code environment and the
world of interoperable objects.
F
EATURES AND
B
ENEFITS
CORBA defines an object-oriented approach to creating software components
that you can reuse and share between applications. Each object encapsulates
the details of its inner workings and presents a well-defined interface,
reducing application complexity. The CORBA approach also reduces development
costs, because once an object is implemented and tested, it can be used
over and over again. CORBA's platform independence lets you run and invoke
the object from any platform; you can run an object from the platform that
makes the most sense for that object. CORBA's language independence lets
you reuse existing code and leverage your existing programming skills.
Netscape envisions a near-term future in which software objects with
defined interfaces interoperate across corporate intranets and across the
Internet. The benefits for application developers and information technology
(IT) organizations are significant:
Choice
. CORBA is based on an open, published specification. It
is implemented on and supported by numerous hardware and operating system
platforms. CORBA Java objects are portable. You can build objects on one
platform and deploy them on any other supported platform.
Interoperability
. CORBA objects are fully interoperable because
they communicate using the Internet Inter-ORB Protocol (IIOP). An enterprise
IT organization need consider only its functional needs when selecting
an ORB, CORBA services, and software objects, even when they are developed
by different vendors. In addition, software bridges enable communications
between CORBA objects and objects developed using Microsoft's DCOM technology.

主要讨论点：对新闻中字体排版的批评，特别是字母间距（kerning）问题

不同观点：
• [jocoda] 认为新闻中的字母间距问题很明显，属于糟糕的设计，应该被指出。虽然自己不是设计师，但意识到 kerning 是一个专业问题。同时，认为大多数人在问题被指出之前可能不会注意到。现在问题被指出，他好奇纽约时报是否会修正。

• [LorenDB] 通过分享一个相关的 XKCD 漫画（#1015），幽默地指出了字体排版和设计问题在普通人与设计师眼中的不同重要性。

补充讨论：
• [jocoda] 的评论中提到了普通观众对设计细节的不敏感，暗示设计问题往往需要被指出才能被大众注意到。

data.title: We fell out of love with Next.js and back in love with Ruby on Rails
data.author: mike1o1
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Hardcover从Next.js迁移回Ruby on Rails和Inertia.js的经历。最初，团队因SEO需求选择了Next.js，利用其服务端渲染（SSR）和增量静态再生功能。然而，随着应用增长，客户端数据获取导致性能下降，且无法有效缓存。2022年，Next.js推出App Router，团队尝试迁移以改善性能，但仍遇到一些集成问题。最终，团队决定回归Ruby on Rails，结合Inertia.js，实现了更高效的开发和性能优化。这一转变使他们重新爱上了Rails的开发体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：服务器端渲染（SSR）与客户端渲染（CSR）的优劣比较，以及不同技术栈在实际项目中的适用性

不同观点：
• **支持服务器端渲染**：thembones 认为，服务器端渲染从未真正消失，如今因首屏绘制和SEO的优势重新受到重视。现代框架如Rails + Turbo、HTMX、Phoenix LiveView和React Server Components都将SSR作为基准。复杂性成本是关键驱动因素，减少客户端JS的依赖可以同时提升性能和安全性。"HTML by default, JS only where needed"是新兴模式。

• **质疑复杂性**：3sbi 指出，某些项目如书追踪应用不需要GraphQL或复杂的前端框架，使用Ruby on Rails的单体应用即可满足需求。对复杂性的渴望可能源于对技术潮流的追随，而非实际需求。

• **NextJS的局限性**：twodave 分享了使用NextJS的经验，指出其在认证、代理请求、文档和云服务依赖方面的不足，并提到维护者支持不力。这些因素导致其团队决定逐步淘汰NextJS。

• **用户体验问题**：petetnt 强调，尽管技术选择对开发者有利，但用户体验不应被忽视。在使用NextJS的项目中出现了明显的延迟问题，影响了用户体验。

• **全栈开发的挑战**：t-writescode 讨论了前后端开发者沟通不畅的问题，并指出JavaScript全栈开发虽然提高了开发效率，但也带来了新的复杂性和技术债务。

• **技术栈选择的两难**：madethemcry 认为，选择JavaScript全栈（前端和后端）涉及ORM和数据库的复杂性。尽管个人偏好Ruby on Rails，但由于市场需求和团队技能限制，选择JavaScript和Java更为现实。

• **技术栈的成本效益**：austin-cheney 质疑许多技术文章和讨论中对技术栈成本和时间效益的实际考量，指出缺乏具体数据支持。

• **框架对比**：ummonk 和 qq99 分别对NextJS和Ruby on Rails以及Phoenix LiveView进行了对比，提出技术选择可能受个人舒适度和项目需求影响。

补充讨论：
• **对未来技术的展望**：chagel 对LLM/AI技术在Web开发中的潜力表示关注，并强调对基础设施、协议、数据库和API的掌握。

• **对技术潮流的反思**：swyx 幽默地指出了使用NextJS时成本增长的问题，并提出开发者可能需要考虑框架开发者的决策背景和企业客户需求。

争议焦点：
• **技术复杂性与实际需求之间的矛盾**：部分评论者认为现代Web开发中过度依赖复杂的技术栈，而实际项目需求可能不需要如此复杂的解决方案。
• **NextJS的适用性**：对NextJS在不同项目中的适用性存在争议，部分开发者认为其在某些场景下增加了不必要的复杂性和成本。

Part 1: How We Fell Out of Love with Next.js and Back in Love with Ruby on Rails & Inertia.js
Adam Fortuna
By
Adam Fortuna
Fri, 02 May 2025 00:00:00 +0000
·
20
min read
This is
part 1
of a series documenting
Hardcover’s Alexandria release
. We recently migrated our codebase from Next.js to Ruby on Rails, and it’s been amazing so far! It was a learning experience, and I’m excited to share some of our takeaways. I’ll link each article here as it’s written.
Introducing Alexandria: Faster, Smoother, Smarter
Part 1: How we fell out of love with Next.js and back in love with Ruby on Rails & Inertia.js
Part 2: Moving from the Cloud to the Server – Google & AWS to Digital Ocean and Kamal
Part 3: How we use Puppeteer to generate OpenGraph images
Part 4: Speeding up Ruby on Rails with Solid Cache, server side rendering, Sidekiq, and Brick
Part 5: Securing and Speeding up our API Server
Today’s focus is on the main reason for the move from Next.js to Ruby on Rails. This is the first question anyone asks, and the most important one. So let’s dive into it.
Just a side note: this is going to be a software development related post, not a book related posts. If you’re here for the Book Vibes, I’d encourage you read about the
release first
.
How We Got Here
When Hardcover started, I was primarily a Ruby on Rails developer. I had experience with JS frontends, but Rails was my
jam
. I’ve been building things in it since before Rails 1.0, worked at multiple startups that use it, built courses to teach it, spoken at meetups about it, and been to conferences.
I’ve been
all in
with Rails for a while.
In the late 2010s, single page applications broke out as an alternative way to create applications. It was the JavaScript framework Cambrian Explosion – with jQuery as the common ancestor (in spirit at least).
We had Backbone.js, Ember.js, Angular.js, Vue.js, React.js and many more. I’ve shipped code in each of these frameworks that have been seen by millions people (which is easier than it sounds! I’ve heard you can just
do stuff
– especially on the Internet).
The biggest point of friction with these frameworks was always how they would integrate with Ruby on Rails. Rails has gone down a different route for it’s sanctioned front-end path – using
Islands Architecture
, Stimulus Controllers and other solutions (which are all preferred to Rails previous .rjs syntax).
I’ll be honest: I haven’t spent the time to fully learn this architecture. I can’t criticize it, other than that the code looks
weird
to me. It does have advantages over JS frameworks, but you’re still writing JS either way.
For most of the past decade, using these popular frameworks in Rails has meant giving up
Server Side Rendering
. In 2021 when I started Hardcover, that one fact alone meant it was out. We knew we’d need to rely on SEO to find new readers and I didn’t want to sacrifice that.
Enter Next.js
Right as I was deciding on what framework to use that would allow for SEO + JavaScript, Next.js announced version 9.5  – adding incremental static regeneration and other features that would allow us to render pages with SSR and expire the cache. It sounded perfect.
I setup the initial architecture of Hardcover using Next.js with the pages router, hitting a GraphQL API (Hasura) for getting data, and caching as much as possible using Incremental Static Revalidation. The first load was often a bit slow, but caching helped.
One decision I made during this phase would come back to haunt me:
cache facts on the server, fetch user data in the browser
.
For instance, if you’re viewing a Readers profile,
everything
we show there would be fetched client-side from our GraphQL API. Our API returns different results depending on your relationship with the reader you’re viewing. Someone can mark a book, list or goal as public, private or only people you follow – which all determine what other readers can see.
This approach left that logic to the API, allowing the front-end to be dumb and just show whatever was returned. It
worked
.
Behind the scenes we were still using Ruby on Rails for the entire backend. This is what the architecture looked like at the time.
From 2021 to 2022 we continued on building like this. Some pages were getting slower, but we were able to ship fast. We continued innovating, but the app kept getting slower. As more readers joined, we were hitting our API servers
hard
, and we couldn’t cache anything at that level. If we wanted server side caching, we needed to move that to the server.
An Wild App Router Appears
In mid-2022, Next.js launched the App Router – a new way to server side render Next.js apps. I loved the idea. It felt more like Rails which I was used to. We immediately starting migrating Hardcover to this approach.
We switched to fetching all data about facts and users to be fetched on the server using the app directory and React Server Components. This went surprisingly smooth! There were some rough days with next-auth and Apollo to get everything

主要讨论点：服务器端渲染（SSR）与客户端渲染（CSR）的优劣比较，以及不同技术栈在实际项目中的适用性

不同观点：
• **支持服务器端渲染**：thembones 认为，服务器端渲染从未真正消失，如今因首屏绘制和SEO的优势重新受到重视。现代框架如Rails + Turbo、HTMX、Phoenix LiveView和React Server Components都将SSR作为基准。复杂性成本是关键驱动因素，减少客户端JS的依赖可以同时提升性能和安全性。"HTML by default, JS only where needed"是新兴模式。

• **质疑复杂性**：3sbi 指出，某些项目如书追踪应用不需要GraphQL或复杂的前端框架，使用Ruby on Rails的单体应用即可满足需求。对复杂性的渴望可能源于对技术潮流的追随，而非实际需求。

• **NextJS的局限性**：twodave 分享了使用NextJS的经验，指出其在认证、代理请求、文档和云服务依赖方面的不足，并提到维护者支持不力。这些因素导致其团队决定逐步淘汰NextJS。

• **用户体验问题**：petetnt 强调，尽管技术选择对开发者有利，但用户体验不应被忽视。在使用NextJS的项目中出现了明显的延迟问题，影响了用户体验。

• **全栈开发的挑战**：t-writescode 讨论了前后端开发者沟通不畅的问题，并指出JavaScript全栈开发虽然提高了开发效率，但也带来了新的复杂性和技术债务。

• **技术栈选择的两难**：madethemcry 认为，选择JavaScript全栈（前端和后端）涉及ORM和数据库的复杂性。尽管个人偏好Ruby on Rails，但由于市场需求和团队技能限制，选择JavaScript和Java更为现实。

• **技术栈的成本效益**：austin-cheney 质疑许多技术文章和讨论中对技术栈成本和时间效益的实际考量，指出缺乏具体数据支持。

• **框架对比**：ummonk 和 qq99 分别对NextJS和Ruby on Rails以及Phoenix LiveView进行了对比，提出技术选择可能受个人舒适度和项目需求影响。

补充讨论：
• **对未来技术的展望**：chagel 对LLM/AI技术在Web开发中的潜力表示关注，并强调对基础设施、协议、数据库和API的掌握。

• **对技术潮流的反思**：swyx 幽默地指出了使用NextJS时成本增长的问题，并提出开发者可能需要考虑框架开发者的决策背景和企业客户需求。

争议焦点：
• **技术复杂性与实际需求之间的矛盾**：部分评论者认为现代Web开发中过度依赖复杂的技术栈，而实际项目需求可能不需要如此复杂的解决方案。
• **NextJS的适用性**：对NextJS在不同项目中的适用性存在争议，部分开发者认为其在某些场景下增加了不必要的复杂性和成本。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对存档网页服务的评价与使用体验

不同观点：
• **支持存档网页服务的观点**：
  - 存档网页服务（如archive.is）能够有效保存网页内容，防止因网站关闭或内容被删除而丢失重要信息。
  - 用户提到，该服务在保存有价值的新闻文章、研究资料和论坛讨论方面非常有用，特别是在内容可能被修改或删除的情况下。
  - 例子：有用户提到在学术研究中使用存档网页服务来保存参考文献和数据，确保引用的稳定性和可靠性。

• **对存档网页服务的质疑和批评**：
  - 存档网页可能涉及侵犯版权问题，因为未经原网站所有者同意保存和提供内容。
  - 用户担心存档服务可能被滥用，例如用于传播虚假信息或恶意内容，因为存档内容可能不再反映当前的真实情况。
  - 例子：有用户指出一些存档网页可能包含过时或误导性的信息，影响公众的理解和判断。

• **对具体存档服务（archive.is）的技术和功能评价**：
  - 有用户认为archive.is的界面友好，操作简单，适合非技术用户使用。
  - 但也有用户指出archive.is在处理动态网页和复杂JavaScript内容时存在不足，导致存档页面显示不完整或不准确。
  - 例子：有用户提到某些包含交互式图表或动态加载图片的网页在存档后无法正常显示内容。

补充讨论：
- **隐私问题**：有用户关注存档网页服务在抓取网页时是否会尊重robots.txt协议和隐私声明，避免抓取不应公开或敏感的信息。
- **存档网页的长期可用性**：有用户关心存档服务的长期维护和稳定性，担心服务关闭会导致已存档内容的丢失。
- **争议焦点**：存档网页服务的合法性、准确性和隐私问题是讨论的核心争议点。用户在使用存档服务时需要权衡其带来的便利与潜在的法律和信息准确性风险。

data.title: 'Dangerous nonsense': AI-authored books about ADHD for sale on Amazon
data.author: n1b0m
data.article_summary: 亚马逊正在销售一些自称提供专业建议的ADHD管理书籍，但这些书似乎是由ChatGPT等聊天机器人撰写的。这些书籍包括《Navigating ADHD in Men: Thriving with a Late Diagnosis》等，经检测确认100%由人工智能生成。专家警告，这些AI生成的内容可能包含有害或误导的信息，特别是在健康和医疗领域，可能导致误诊或加重病情。计算机科学研究员Michael Cook指出，生成型AI可能会提供危险建议，例如涉及有毒物质或忽略健康指南。亚马逊通过销售这些书籍获利，无论内容是否可信。目前，尚无立法要求AI撰写书籍必须标注，这导致市场如“狂野西部”般混乱。专家呼吁亚马逊有道德责任防止伤害顾客。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容对信息质量和传播的影响，以及如何应对低质量内容的增加。

不同观点：
• **fritzo的观点**：认为当前AI生成内容带来的问题并不是AI独有的，而是随着内容制作和传播成本降低，低质量内容增多的一般性问题。这种现象在博客、电子书、自出版等领域早已存在，因此AI并不是问题的根本原因，核心在于需要更强的过滤机制。

• **TrackerFF的观点**：通过挪威某市 council 使用LLM生成错误报告的实例，指出AI生成内容的现实危害，尤其是在不当使用时可能引发严重后果。同时提到在数学Facebook群组中发现大量看似合法的AI生成科学书籍，担忧这些内容误导读者。

• **gedy的观点**：过去出版编辑、书店和图书馆员在过滤低质量内容方面发挥了重要作用。当前通过亚马逊等平台直接向读者发布内容虽然提高了效率，但平台应承担责任，付费聘请人工审核过滤低质量的AI生成内容。

• **pengaru的观点**：认为当前AI生成内容充斥着无意义的废话，不仅在工作环境中（如GH评论、JIRA tickets）造成困扰，还可能导致更严重的后果。对AI生成内容的泛滥表示强烈担忧，甚至以幽默的方式表达对未来职业选择的迷茫。

• **pureagave的观点**：指出类似的问题不仅存在于AI生成内容领域，还涉及其他行业（如ADHD诊断中心、辅导中心等）的“伪科学”现象。认为这些行业本质上是巨大的“金钱印刷机”，呼吁关注这些领域的乱象。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：AI生成内容问题的独特性以及责任归属。fritzo认为这并非AI独有问题，而是内容生成成本下降带来的普遍问题。而TrackerFF和pengaru则通过实例强调AI带来的具体危害，gedy则关注平台责任，提出应由平台付费进行内容审核。

• **现实影响**：TrackerFF的实例显示AI生成内容在现实中已产生不良后果，如挪威市 council 的错误报告事件。pengaru则提到工作环境中AI生成内容对效率和质量的负面影响。

• **解决方案的讨论**：gedy提出通过平台付费进行人工审核的建议，但未深入讨论具体操作和可行性。此外，fritzo强调需要更强的过滤机制，但未具体说明这些机制应如何设计和实施。

Richard Wordsworth was given a book bought off Amazon after receiving an adult ADHD diagnosis.
Photograph: Martin Godwin/The Guardian
View image in fullscreen
Richard Wordsworth was given a book bought off Amazon after receiving an adult ADHD diagnosis.
Photograph: Martin Godwin/The Guardian
Artificial intelligence (AI)
‘Dangerous nonsense’: AI-authored books about ADHD for sale on Amazon
Experts say online retailer has ethical responsibility to guard against chatbot-generated work on sensitive topics
Rachel Hall
Sun 4 May 2025 10.50 EDT
Last modified on Sun 4 May 2025 16.03 EDT
Share
Amazon is selling books marketed at people seeking techniques to manage their ADHD that claim to offer expert advice yet appear to be authored by a chatbot such as ChatGPT.
Amazon’s marketplace has been deluged with works produced by artificial intelligence that are easy and cheap to publish but include unhelpful or dangerous misinformation, such as
shoddy travel guidebooks
and mushroom foraging books that
encourage risky tasting
.
A number of books have appeared on the online retailer’s site offering guides to ADHD that also seem to be written by chatbots. The titles include
Navigating ADHD in Men: Thriving with a Late Diagnosis
,
Men with Adult ADHD: Highly Effective Techniques for Mastering Focus, Time Management and Overcoming Anxiety
and Men with Adult ADHD Diet & Fitness.
Samples from eight books were examined for the Guardian by Originality.ai, a US company that detects content produced by artificial intelligence. The company said each had a rating of 100% on its AI detection score, meaning its systems were highly confident that the books were written by a chatbot.
Experts said online marketplaces were a “wild west” owing to the lack of regulation around AI-produced work – and dangerous misinformation risked spreading as a result.
Michael Cook, a computer science researcher at King’s College London, said generative AI systems were known to give dangerous advice, for example around ingesting toxic substances, mixing together dangerous chemicals or ignoring health guidelines.
As such, it was “frustrating and depressing to see AI-authored books increasingly popping up on digital marketplaces” particularly on health and medical topics, which could result in misdiagnosis or worsen conditions, he said.
“Generative AI systems like ChatGPT may have been trained on a lot of medical textbooks and articles, but they’ve also been trained on pseudoscience, conspiracy theories and fiction,” said Cook.
“They also can’t be relied on to critically analyse or reliably reproduce the knowledge they’ve previously read – it’s not as simple as having the AI ‘remember’ things that they’ve seen in their training data. Generative AI systems should not be allowed to deal with sensitive or dangerous topics without the oversight of an expert,” he added.
Yet Cook noted Amazon’s business model incentivised this type of practice, as it made “money every time” people bought a book, whether the work was “trustworthy or not”, while the generative AI companies that created the products were not held accountable.
Prof Shannon Vallor, the director of the University of Edinburgh’s Centre for Technomoral Futures, said Amazon had “an ethical responsibility to not knowingly facilitate harm to their customers and to society”, although it would be “absurd” to make a bookseller responsible for the contents of all its books.
Problems were arising because the guardrails previously deployed in the publishing industry – such as reputational concerns and the vetting of authors and manuscripts – had been completely transformed by AI, she noted.
This was compounded by a “wild west” regulatory environment in which there were no “meaningful consequences for those who enable harms”, fuelling a “race to the bottom”, Vallor said.
At present, there is no legislation that requires AI-authored books to be labelled as such. Copyright law only applies if a specific author’s content has been reproduced, although Vallor noted that tort law should impose “basic duties of care and due diligence”.
The Advertising Standards Agency said AI-authored books cannot be advertised to give a misleading impression that they were written by a human, enabling people who had seen such books to submit a
complaint
.
Richard Wordsworth was hoping to learn about his recent adult ADHD diagnosis when his father recommended a book he found on Amazon after searching “ADHD adult men”.
When Wordsworth sat down to read it, “immediately, it sounded strange”, he said. The book opened with a quote from the
conservative psychologist Jordan Petersen
and then contained a string of random anecdotes, as well as historical inaccuracies.
Some advice was actively harmful, Wordsworth observed. For example, one chapter discussing emotional dysregulation warned that friends and family did not “forgive the emotional damage you inflict. The pain and hurt caused by impulsive anger leave lasting scars.”

data.title: Redis is open source again
data.author: antirez
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Redis 许可证变更及其对社区和用户的影响

不同观点：
• [c0l0] 认为 Redis 公司因将许可证变更为 SSPL 而失去了用户的信任，即使现在改回 AGPL，社区可能仍不会信任 Redis。作为贡献者，他感觉自己被背叛，并选择继续使用 Redis 的分支版本（如 redict）。
• [simonw] 对 Redis 改回开源许可证表示欢迎，认为这是社区希望看到的结果，并对 Redis 团队表示感谢。他还提到，这次变更可能会激励其他公司也做出类似的决定。
• [placatedmayhem] 提到社区可能不会轻易再信任 Redis 公司，尤其是一些大公司的法律部门可能仍然对 AGPL 持谨慎态度，因此 Valkey 可能更具吸引力。
• [kamranjon] 强调 Redis 的技术优势和 API 设计的优越性，认为 Redis 一直推动技术进步，并对 Redis 团队的努力表示赞赏。
• [aftbit] 质疑 Redis 公司将“让大公司 fork 他们的软件”作为目标是否合适，并指出 AGPL 许可证可能让一些用户转向由大公司维护的更宽松许可的替代品。
• [md3911027514] 表示其公司已切换到 Valkey 并投入大量资源，因此不会考虑再切换回 Redis，尤其在 Redis 有可能再次变更许可证的情况下。
• [rustc] 指出 Redis 仍然要求贡献者签署 CLA（贡献者许可协议），这使得未来再次变更许可证的可能性依然存在。
• [theturtletalks] 引用了 Antirez 离开 Redis 时的一篇博客，认为 Antirez 回归并继续推动 Redis 的美学和技术进步是一件值得高兴的事。
• [bradgessler] 提到曾因 Redis 公司过于严苛的商标政策而对其失去兴趣，但对此次许可证变更表示欢迎，希望 Redis 能修复之前的信任问题。
• [otterley] 认为，改变开源许可证会导致信任的永久性丧失，即使 Redis 恢复了原来的许可证，社区的信任也很难完全恢复。
• [remram] 表示对 Redis 的失望，尤其在其对社区的伤害之后，认为 Valkey 提供了更好的选择，且 Redis 团队之前的行为不可原谅。
• [redbell] 提到 Redis 的许可证变更如同 Elasticsearch 之前一样，最终还是恢复了开源，并对 Redis 团队的努力表示感谢。
• [DetroitThrow] 认为 Redis 改回 AGPL 是一个好的开始，但短期内难以恢复社区的信任，需要时间来重建与开源社区的关系。
• [rdtsc] 对新出现的许可证（如 SSPL）持怀疑态度，认为传统的 GPL 许可证更为明确和可靠，且法律团队更容易理解和接受。

补充讨论：
• 许可证变更对社区和大公司法律部门的影响是讨论的焦点之一。
• 社区对 Redis 公司信任的丧失以及如何重建信任是另一个核心议题。
• Redis 的技术优势和 API 设计的优越性被一些用户高度评价，即使在许可证争议的背景下，这些技术因素仍然被视为 Redis 的核心竞争力。
• 讨论中多次提到 Valkey 作为一个更具吸引力的替代方案，尤其是在大公司和社区对 Redis 失去信任的情况下。
• 贡献者协议（CLA）和未来可能的再次许可证变更也是用户关注的重点。

data.title: The future of solar doesn't track the sun
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了东西固定太阳能阵列是否比单轴跟踪阵列更具经济性。尽管单轴跟踪阵列在每块面板的能量产出上仍占优势，且能应对严重冰雹天气，但东西阵列安装更简单、快速，所需材料和土地更少。随着光伏组件价格下降，东西阵列的经济效益愈发明显。如果仅考虑每瓦交付价格，东西阵列在大多数地方是更优选择，但某些地区仍需更具弹性的面板技术支持。文章总结，尽管跟踪技术曾因提高效率而主导市场，但如今更便宜的光伏组件使东西阵列成为更具成本效益的选择。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太阳能板的固定与追踪系统的优缺点，以及不同配置方案的经济性和技术可行性。

不同观点：
• weinzierl：认为追踪系统的可靠性是主要问题，尤其是如果面板方向错误，效果可能比固定位置更差。他们通过模拟发现，任何移动方案都会影响利润，因此选择了简单的机械齿轮设计，而不是复杂的电子设备。
• adamcharnock：基于离网生活经验，认为固定阵列在日出或日落时提供额外电力的能力有限，曾考虑增加东西方向的阵列，但因复杂性而放弃。
• mchannon：拥有丰富太阳能行业经验，指出东西方向阵列是一种新的拓扑结构，与传统的固定倾斜或追踪系统不同，强调其新颖性。
• tgsovlerkhgsel：指出追踪阵列可能在早晨和傍晚提供电力，但在太阳能占总体发电量大比例的情况下，固定阵列可以通过增加安装功率来补偿追踪阵列的优势。
• tzs：提出使用DMD设备，让小型太阳能板有两个位置，通过机械结构实现部分追踪，以提高可靠性。
• edent：拥有东西向屋顶太阳能经验，认为效率低于纯南向，但能平滑发电，提供更多傍晚电力。
• rini17：建议垂直安装面板以减少冰雹和雪的影响，并最大化早晨和傍晚的生产。
• dgfl：建议通过大卷面板实现低成本安装，采用锯齿形图案和地面支撑，以快速部署东西方向配置。
• csr86：以自然界为例，指出树木不追踪太阳，暗示固定位置可能更自然和可靠。
• xphos：指出单轴追踪系统可以正常化每块板的生产曲线，认为更多固定面板可能在规模上正常化生产。
• carpdiem：回顾过去的工作经验，认为随着面板价格下降，大规模安装成为可能，见证了“墙纸化”的实现。
• wyldfire：关注住宅安装成本，质疑劳动力成本是否开始主导成本。
• tmjdev：对太阳能成本下降的数据来源表示疑问，希望了解消费者层面的成本。
• nbadg：提出防冰雹网作为保护追踪系统的中庸方案，建议自动化部署以减少损害。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的方案包括东西方向阵列、DMD设备、垂直安装、大卷面板和防冰雹网等，展示了多种技术可能性。
• 争议的焦点在于追踪系统与固定系统的可靠性和经济性，以及不同配置方案在实际应用中的复杂性和成本效益。
• 多个评论者提到了面板价格下降对系统设计和安装方式的影响，反映了行业趋势对技术选择的影响。

43861253.article_content:
PV modules are cheap enough today that the simple fixed East-West arrays are cheaper and faster to install than the industry’s darling, the single-axis tracked array.
Xavier Dedenbach, Terraform Power Electronics Engineer
Originally posted
on April 20, 2025.
Summary
This article takes you on a journey to explore whether East-West fixed solar arrays are now more economical than the dominant variant, single-axis tracked arrays. If you just want the answer, feel free to jump to the end or read this summary. But if you have 15 minutes to follow along, the juice is worth the squeeze.
We’re
hiring at Terraform
!
💡
Today’s Claim
PV modules are cheap enough today that the simple fixed East-West arrays are cheaper and faster to install than the industry’s darling, the single-axis tracked array.
Arguments Against
Single-axis tracked arrays still significantly outperform East-West fixed arrays in energy production on a per-panel basis.
There is one weather pattern (severe hail) so destructive that I would choose the more expensive single-axis tracked array if I experienced it regularly.
Arguments For
East-West arrays require less material and labor to install.
East-West arrays use substantially less land for the same power output.
As PV modules become cheaper, the economic benefits of East-West arrays get even better.
Conclusion
If price per watt delivered were the only important factor, East-West arrays would be the clear choice everywhere.
However, nature is metal, and in some regions, we currently lack sufficiently resilient panel technology to support East-West arrays.
Introduction
Like many technologies, photovoltaic (PV) cells, which convert sunlight into usable energy, started out expensive and uncompetitive. They had to compete in one of the most competitive industrial sectors: the energy sector, which is filled with behemoths like coal, natural gas, and hydropower. On top of that, photovoltaic technology was handicapped by limited daylight hours and an above-average vulnerability to weather conditions.
PV systems did not have it easy, but a collective push from green energy companies, governments, and their citizens willed them into existence. They shared in the renewable energy promise to build an economy powered by sunlight, wind, water, and atoms.
So began the decades-long push to improve module efficiency in every way imaginable: new materials, new
PV cell architectures that convert more photons to electrons
, and tracking systems that keep modules aligned with the Sun’s position. These trackers gained industry dominance by offsetting their costs through improved efficiency of the PV modules.
Today’s story examines what happens when the very components being optimized, the PV modules themselves, become cheaper than the technologies designed to improve their efficiency.
Figure 1:
Choose your characters. The incumbent tracking solution vs the simple East-West solution.
Tracking technologies are moderately complex, requiring actuators, sensors, stronger structures, and additional energy storage. These technologies fall into two camps: single-axis and dual-axis systems. Single-axis trackers handle intra-day solar movements, following the Sun as it rises in the East and sets in the West. Dual-axis trackers adjust for the array’s latitude, the Sun’s intra-day movement, and inter-day movement, due to Earth’s orbit
1
. Unlike single-axis trackers, dual-axis solutions haven’t seen mass adoption due to more complicated mechanisms and increased spacing requirements between rows to prevent shading. For this reason, we’ll focus solely on the costs and benefits of the single-axis tracker, the current king, if you will, and its relation to its much simpler cousin, Earl. Ugh… I mean the East-West array.
The Rapid Decline in PV Module Prices
Why ask this question? When I took over the solar and power systems at Terraform Industries, I was asked to architect a photovoltaic system that capitalized on one of the most remarkable learning curves in modern history: a 44% cost reduction for every doubling of cumulative PV module production. The East-West array was a clear winner, despite not being highly adopted in the United States. I began to investigate why, and this article is a byproduct of this effort.
Starting with PV module costs, PV benefited from the trifecta of expanding economies of scale, increased competition as more suppliers rushed into the market, and increased supply as high-grade silicon became abundant due to the demand for PV modules and integrated circuits, aka chips. That level of cost reduction is hard to compete with. In the 2010s, the cost of PV modules fell by 85%, and so far this decade, they have fallen an additional 58%. All this in the face of the worldwide epidemic of increased inflation in recent years.
Table 1:
Module Price Reduction 2010-2025
Over the last decade, trackers rose to dominance, and by 2015, they accounted for more than 50% of the cumulative installed capacity for photovoltaic syst

data.title: Best Practices for User Authentication and Authorization in Web Applications
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary:
本文探讨了现代web应用程序中安全认证和授权机制的框架，强调了在面对日益复杂的网络威胁时，加强身份和访问管理的重要性。文章从七个关键领域进行分析：密码存储、多因素认证、OAuth与联合认证、会话管理、授权模型、基础设施安全和监控。通过实施文中所推荐的实践，组织可以显著提升安全性，同时保持良好的用户体验。

密码存储部分强调了使用强适应性哈希算法（如Argon2、bcrypt、PBKDF2）来保护密码，防止暴力破解攻击。多因素认证虽未充分使用，但其有效性已被证明。OAuth和联合认证提供了更安全的授权方式，而现代授权模型允许细粒度的控制。基础设施安全和监控则是整体安全性的重要组成部分。

本文为安全专业人士、开发人员和系统架构师提供了实用的指导，帮助构建抵御当前威胁的系统，并适应不断变化的安全环境。

43888274.article_content:
Identity & Access
Security Bloggers Network
by
Deepak Gupta - Tech Entrepreneur, Cybersecurity Author
on
May 2, 2025
Your authentication system isn't just a door—it's the fortress protecting everything you value. This research paper presents a comprehensive framework for implementing secure authentication and authorization mechanisms in modern web applications. The increasing sophistication of cyber threats necessitates robust security practices for managing user identity and access privileges.
It examines current industry standards and emerging technologies across seven critical domains: password storage, multi-factor authentication, OAuth and federation, session management, authorization models, infrastructure security, and monitoring. By implementing the recommended practices outlined in this research, organizations can significantly enhance their security posture while maintaining positive user experiences.
The research synthesizes technical expertise, industry standards, and practical implementation guidance to provide a valuable resource for security professionals, developers, and system architects responsible for designing and maintaining secure web applications.
1. Introduction
Imagine waking up to discover that your company's entire customer database has been exposed, your proprietary code stolen, and your CEO's account used to authorize fraudulent transactions—all because of a single compromised password. This nightmare scenario plays out with alarming frequency across organizations of every size and industry.
In 2023 alone, credential-based attacks resulted in over $5 billion in losses, with the average data breach costing companies $4.45 million. Behind these staggering numbers lie simple truths: authentication systems are both your most critical security control and your most vulnerable attack surface.
"
The password was supposed to die years ago
," says security expert Troy Hunt, "yet most breaches still trace back to credential mismanagement." While headlines focus on sophisticated zero-day exploits and nation-state hackers, the uncomfortable reality is that most successful attacks exploit fundamental flaws in how we verify user identity and manage access permissions.
This is not merely a technical problem—it's an existential business risk. When authentication fails, everything fails.
The good news? With proper implementation of modern authentication and authorization frameworks, you can transform this vulnerability into a competitive advantage. Organizations with mature identity practices experience 50% fewer security incidents and recover from breaches three times faster than their counterparts.
This paper cuts through the complexity of identity security to provide actionable guidance across seven critical domains. We'll explore how password storage techniques have evolved beyond simple hashing, why multi-factor authentication remains underutilized despite its proven effectiveness, and how modern authorization models enable granular control without sacrificing user experience.
Whether you're securing a simple web application or implementing enterprise-wide identity governance, the practices outlined here will help you build systems that are resilient against current threats while adapting to the evolving security landscape.
The stakes have never been higher, but neither has our understanding of how to get identity security right. Let's begin.
2. Password Storage: Beyond the Basics
2.1 The Fundamentals of Secure Password Storage
Despite predictions of their demise, passwords remain the most common authentication mechanism. However, they also represent a significant security vulnerability if not properly implemented and stored. The cardinal rule of password storage is simple: never store passwords in plaintext. Instead,
passwords should be protected using cryptographic techniques
that transform the original password into a form that cannot be reversed to reveal the original input.
2.2 Modern Hashing Algorithms
Passwords should be stored using
strong adaptive hashing algorithms
specifically designed for password storage. These algorithms include:
Argon2
: The winner of the Password Hashing Competition in 2015,
Argon2 provides strong resistance
against various attacks, including those leveraging specialized hardware. Argon2 allows for tuning of memory, CPU, and parallelism parameters, making it adaptable to different security requirements and hardware environments.
bcrypt
: Designed in 1999, bcrypt remains a strong choice for password hashing. It includes a built-in salt and a configurable work factor that allows the computational cost to be increased as hardware becomes more powerful.
PBKDF2

data.title: N8n – Flexible AI workflow automation for technical teams
data.author: XCSme
data.article_summary: n8n是一个灵活的工作流自动化平台，专为技术团队设计，结合了代码的精确性和拖放式操作的速度。它允许用户构建多步骤的AI代理并集成各种应用，具有高度自由。平台支持本地或云端部署，适用于IT、安全、开发和销售等多个部门。用户可以通过Docker部署，访问GitHub上的源代码，或使用托管版本。n8n提供1700多个模板，支持JavaScript或Python编写，并允许添加npm或Python库。平台还具备快速反馈、调试、重运行单步等功能，提升了效率。案例显示，企业使用n8n能显著节省时间并提高工作效率，同时平台提供全面的安全和协作功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：n8n工具的优缺点及其使用体验

不同观点：
• **安全性问题**：_pdp_认为n8n在安全性上存在隐患，尤其是提示注入漏洞，因为用户经常将外部数据直接插入系统提示中，可能导致恶意使用。虽然其他工具也存在类似问题，但n8n似乎缺乏对此问题的认识。
• **功能和易用性**：jasongill指出n8n作为自托管的Zapier替代品，虽然价格合适且具备不少内置集成，但在创建自定义应用时体验不佳，需要手动操作和编写JavaScript模块，且缺乏专业的管理界面。
• **性能和成本**：photon_garden认为n8n在可观察性、非技术人员使用方面表现出色，但并行执行、版本控制和定价方面存在不足，尤其对于有工程能力团队来说，直接写后端代码可能更简单、成本更低。
• **定制化与扩展性**：fzysingularity分享了他们使用n8n进行自动化任务的成功案例，包括自定义节点用于ETL任务，展示了n8n在特定场景下的强大扩展性。

补充讨论：
• **使用案例**：ChrisGammell提到使用n8n快速原型化外部计算，而preya2k则推荐Windmill作为n8n的替代开源方案。
• **代码 vs 可视化工具**：hypefi认为直接使用代码进行自动化比n8n更优，但承认n8n的可视化节点在某些场景下有趣。SansGuidon也有类似看法，最终选择脚本和cron jobs替代n8n。
• **开源争议**：kfogel提到n8n曾因错误使用“开源”一词引发讨论，最终n8n停止使用该标签。
• **名称和发音**：Jefro118关注如何将网页抓取整合到工作流中，而behnamoh则询问n8n的名称发音及其在教育领域的适用性。

争议焦点：
• **安全性问题**：n8n在处理外部数据和系统提示方面的潜在漏洞是主要争议点，尤其是在提示注入攻击的易用性上。
• **自定义应用的复杂性**：jasongill和photon_garden都提到自定义应用的复杂性和管理界面的缺乏，这增加了使用难度。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **低代码/无代码工具在教育中的应用**：behnamoh关注n8n及其他工具在教育领域的适用性，尤其是对计算机科学背景较少的学生而言。
• **抽象层次和范式转换**：MattDaEskimo指出no-code工具在抽象层次和应对新范式方面的不足，这可能是其在复杂场景下表现不佳的原因。

总结：n8n作为一个自托管、低代码/无代码工具，在价格和集成性上获得了一定好评，但在安全性、自定义复杂性和性能方面存在不足。用户在选择n8n时需要权衡其易用性与潜在的技术债务和复杂性。

data.title: ePub-utils: A Python library and CLI tool for inspecting ePub from the terminal
data.author: ernstgnzlz
data.article_summary: "epub-utils" 是一个用于处理 EPUB 文件的 Python 命令行工具和实用库。它可以解析和验证 EPUB 文件的容器及包文件，提取元数据（如标题、作者、标识符），并提供命令行界面用于快速检查文件。主要功能包括显示 `container.xml` 和 `package.opf` 内容、查看目录等。用户可以通过 pip 安装该工具，并在命令行或 Python 代码中使用它来处理 EPUB 文件。该项目基于 Apache-2.0 许可证，拥有 152 个星标和 2 个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：EPUB阅读器工具的比较与功能扩展

不同观点：
• Flex247A 分享了一个自己开发的EPUB阅读器（Qitab），该工具使用系统Webview渲染EPUB文档，但没有详细说明其相对于其他工具的独特之处。

• kanodiaashu 对该项目表示兴趣，并询问其相对于 ebooklib（一个Python的EPUB处理包）有哪些关键改进。这表明读者关心新工具相较于现有解决方案的创新点和优势。

• sigwinch 认为 mupdf 可能已经能够满足类似的功能，并且可能提供更多功能，暗示 Qitab 可能与现有工具在功能上存在重叠，且未必有显著优势。

• lupusreal 提到 Calibre 工具集，尤其是其命令行工具（如 ebook-meta 和 ebook-convert），指出这些工具在处理电子书元数据和格式转换方面的实用性，但也指出其图形界面可能不符合所有人的喜好。

• Dromadie 对 Qitab 表示兴趣，并询问其是否支持 EPUB3 系列以及是否有计划增加写入元数据的功能，表明用户对更高级的EPUB3支持和元数据处理功能有需求。

• ryen 询问 Qitab 是否提供API以支持分页以及提取文本和图像，这反映出对EPUB内容解析和处理的进一步技术需求。

补充讨论：
• 用户对新工具的功能改进和独特性表示关注，尤其是相对于现有工具如 ebooklib、mupdf 和 Calibre 的优势。
• 用户对EPUB3支持、元数据写入以及API功能表现出具体需求，这可能为 Qitab 的后续开发提供方向。
• 讨论中提到的现有工具如 mupdf 和 Calibre 提供了参考基准，帮助评估 Qitab 的潜在价值和市场定位。

争议焦点：目前讨论中尚未出现明显争议，但有潜在的功能重叠和工具比较，可能会引发对 Qitab 独特性和竞争力的进一步探讨。

data.title: Bloom Filters
data.author: mfrw
data.article_summary:
Bloom filters是Burton Bloom于1970年提出的一种概率数据结构，用于高效地进行集合成员检查，通过牺牲一定的准确性（可能出现假阳性）来大幅减少时间和空间开销。其主要特点是：如果Bloom filter判断某个键不在文件中，则可以100%确定不需要读取该文件；但如果判断键存在，则可能出现假阳性。

Bloom filter由一个位数组和多个哈希函数组成。插入元素时，元素经过k个哈希函数计算出k个位置，并将这些位置的比特设为1。查询时，若所有对应位置均为1，则可能存在（可能假阳性）；若有任何一个位置为0，则确定不存在。

这种结构非常适合大多数查询结果为否定的场景，能够显著加速系统并节省空间。假阳性率和空间使用可通过调整位数组大小和哈希函数数量来控制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Bloom滤波器及其变体（如紧凑近似器）的应用、优化及实际使用场景

不同观点：
• Jeffparsons分享了他对"紧凑近似器"的发现和使用体验，指出它们可以用于隐式缓存失效处理。与Bloom滤波器不同，紧凑近似器提供与键相关联的值的下界，并且不会像Bloom滤波器那样"填满"，旧数据只会逐渐变差。这使得在某些用例中可以持续使用同一个结构。

43866001.article_content:
The original motivation for the creation of Bloom filters is efficient set
membership, using a probabilistic approach to significantly reduce the time and
space required to reject items that are not members in a certain set.
The data structure was proposed by Burton Bloom in
a 1970 paper
titled "Space/Time
Trade-offs in Hash Coding with Allowable Errors". It's a good paper that's
worth reading.
Why Bloom filters?
Suppose that we store some information on disk and want to check if a certain
file contains a certain entry. Reading from disk is time consuming, so we want
to minimize it as much as possible. A Bloom filter is a data structure that
implements a cache with probabilistic properties:
If the cache says the key is not present in a specific file, then it's
100% certain we should not be reading the file.
If the cache says the key
is
present in the file, there's a small chance
this is a false positive (and in fact the key isn't there). In this case
we just read the file as usual.
In a scenario where the majority of queries "is this key in that file?" have a
negative answer, a Bloom filter can significantly speed up the system
[1]
.
Moreover, the probabilistic nature (the existence of false positives) allows
Bloom filters to be extremely fast and occupy very little space. Here's a quote
from the Bloom paper:
The new hash-coding methods to be introduced are
suggested for applications in which the great majority of
messages to be tested will not belong to the given set. For
these applications, it is appropriate to consider as a unit of
time (called
reject time
) the average time required to
classify a test message as a nonmember of the given set.
How a Bloom filter works
A Bloom filter is a special kind of a
hash table with open addressing
.
It's an array of bits (the length is typically denoted
m
), and some fixed
number (
k
) of hash functions. We'll assume each hash function can take an
arbitrary sequence of bytes and hash it into an integer in the inclusive range
[0,
m-1]
. A Bloom filter supports two operations:
Insert an item
: the item is hashed using each of the
k
hash functions, and the
appropriate bits in the underlying array are set to 1.
Test if an item is a member
: the item is hashed using each of the
k
hash
functions. If any of the bits indicated by their results is 0, we return "false"
with certainty. If all the bits are 1, we return "true" - and there's a small
chance of false positives.
Here's how the Bloom paper describes it:
The hash area is considered as N individual addressable bits, with addresses 0
through N - 1. It is assumed that all bits in the hash area are first set to 0.
Next, each message in the set to be stored is hash coded into a number of
distinct bit addresses, say a1, a2, . . . , ad. Finally, all d bits addressed by
a1 through ad are set to 1.
To test a new message a sequence of d bit addresses,
say a'1, a'2, ... a'd, is generated in the same manner as for storing a message.
If all d bits are 1, the new message is accepted. If any of these bits is zero,
the message is rejected.
Hopefully it's clear why this data structure is probabilistic in nature: it's
possible that different items hash to the same number, and therefore when
we test some X, all its hashes point to bits turned on by the hashing of other
data. Read the Math appendix for the math behind Bloom filters and how to
calculate (and design for a specific) the false positive rate.
Here's an example:
We start with an empty bloom filter with
m=16
and
k=3
. All bits
are initialized to 0.
Insertion of "x". The three hashes return indices 1, 6, 15, so these bits
in the array are set to 1.
Insertion of "y". Hashing returns indices 6, 9 and 13, so these
bits in the array are set to 1. Note that bit 6 is set for both "x" and "y",
and that's fine.
Next, let's look at some membership tests:
Test "x". Hashing returns 1, 6, 15; all these bits are 1 in the
array, so the answer is "true". This is a true positive.
Test "w". Hashing returns 3, 9, 13. Since the bit at position 3 is 0, the
answer is "false".
Test "v". Hashing returns 9, 13, 15; all these bits are 1 in the array,
so the answer is "true". This is a false positive.
Note that it's trivial to prove (by the law of contraposition) that all "false"
answers from a Bloom filter's test operation are true negatives.
Implementation
Here's a simple implementation of a Bloom filter in Go:

// You can calculate m and k from the number of elements you expect the
// filter to hold and the desired error rate using CalculateParams.
func
New
(
m
uint64
,
k
uint64
)
*
BloomFilter
{
return
&
BloomFilter
{
m
:
m
,
k
:
k
,
bitset
:
newBitset
(
m
),
seed1
:
maphash
.
MakeSeed
(),
seed2
:
maphash
.
MakeSeed
(),
}
}
type
BloomFilter
struct
{
m
uint64
k
uint64
bitset
[]
uint64
// seeds for the double hashing scheme.
seed1
,
seed2
maphash
.
Seed
}
// Insert a data item into the bloom filter.
func
(
bf

BloomFilter

43866001.article_summary:
Bloom filters是Burton Bloom于1970年提出的一种概率数据结构，用于高效地进行集合成员检查，通过牺牲一定的准确性（可能出现假阳性）来大幅减少时间和空间开销。其主要特点是：如果Bloom filter判断某个键不在文件中，则可以100%确定不需要读取该文件；但如果判断键存在，则可能出现假阳性。

Bloom filter由一个位数组和多个哈希函数组成。插入元素时，元素经过k个哈希函数计算出k个位置，并将这些位置的比特设为1。查询时，若所有对应位置均为1，则可能存在（可能假阳性）；若有任何一个位置为0，则确定不存在。

这种结构非常适合大多数查询结果为否定的场景，能够显著加速系统并节省空间。假阳性率和空间使用可通过调整位数组大小和哈希函数数量来控制。

data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者喜欢深夜穿轮滑探索城市，特别是在波士顿和纽约。在夜间，城市街道变得空旷，垃圾车、维修工人等开始工作，使城市为新一天做好准备。作者通过轮滑以不同速度感受城市的细节与整体。作者还介绍了一个名为"Stickdar"的实验项目，利用2D LiDAR扫描仪记录城市环境，并将其可视化。后来，作者尝试将LiDAR安装在头盔上，结合手机的6自由度追踪功能，构建了一个名为"Helmdar"的系统，通过手机和LiDAR的结合，实时绘制出周围环境的3D点云地图。这一项目被视为一种"奇特相机"，通过不完全精确的成像系统进行创意表达。作者详细描述了硬件和软件的实现方式，并通过照片展示了实际效果。

43889875.article_content:
One of my favorite joys is exploring a city late at night on rollerblades. I’ve been doing it fairly regularly for about
10 years now, first in Boston and then in NYC. Every time day turns to night and back again a city takes a breath. At
night people flow out or huddle up in buildings, leaving the streets clear for the people and machines that reset
the urban environment for the next day. Garbage trucks lumber about, workers unload fresh stock at stores, repairs
happen in subway tunnels and on roads. Without all the people it’s easier to see the naked form of the streets,
buildings, and infrastructure.
When you’re moving slow you spend more time taking in the details. When you’re moving fast the world becomes a blur. The
world around you is a brush that paints into your perception, and the speed of the brush strokes helps set the style of
the painting. I like rollerblading in particular because it gives those perceptual brush strokes a lot of range. You can
quickly stop and soak in a detail, change direction, occupy a tight space, or fly downhill in a long straight line.
Stickdar
Some years ago I picked up a 2D LiDAR scanner (RPLidar A1) without a particular purpose in mind. As it spins it tells
you its current angle and the distance to the environment in the direction it’s pointing. They’re often used in robot
vacuums to map walls and other obstacles. One night in 2021 I put it on the end of a stick and carried it around with my
laptop recording timestamped measurements from it. By putting each scan sweep on its own layer I could make
visualizations like this:
Taken outside my apartment at the time during heavy snowfall. You can see the path cut through the snow on the
sidewalk, the apartment building wall, windows, cars along the sidewalk, and points on a tree.
Walking along the perimeter wall outside New Lab. Just behind the character is scaffolding. There are rectangles from
windows. And if I remember right there was snow on the ground at that time too. This one is much more distorted because
I wasn’t so careful to keep the sensor stable while moving.
I think about devices like this as “weird cameras” - imperfect leaky imaging systems that don’t faithfully reproduce
a precise representation of what they are pointed at. Instead they mix in side channels that the user or environment can
affect, and that frees them up for more interesting creative expression.
Helmdar
While I was experimenting with the stickdar I had the idea that it would be fun to make maps on a larger scale by
carrying it around while I was rollerblading. But when I tried that out the maps were very chaotic because it was harder
to keep it steady. I moved onto other projects, but then the other week this project thread popped back into mind.
Over the years I’ve done various projects which needed 6 DoF tracking through space (i.e. machine needs to know where it
is and where it is pointing). A very convenient way to achieve this nowadays for something quick and dirty is to use
mobile phones, because they come with AR frameworks that know how to use the sensors and cameras onboard to do very good
“inside-out” (no external sensors) 6 DoF tracking. On Android that’s even exposed to web browsers via the WebXR API so
you can bash together a web app to access that data, no app development required (hot tip: works on the Quest VR
headsets too, including hand tracking, which I’ve
had fun using for projects in the past
).
So when the stickdar popped back into mind I started thinking about attaching the LiDAR to a phone to track its position
and orientation in space. Then I could work out the position of all the points returned by the sensor in 3D world space,
building up a point cloud map of the world as I moved through it. In general doing this is a problem known as
simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM)
, and
nowadays there are plenty of very good ways to solve it. But in the spirit of weird cameras, because I was curious about
how well this would work, and for fun I decided to try it this way.
Here’s what I came up with:
I built a frame out of aluminum extrusion and attached the phone (a Pixel 6) and the LiDAR to the front with some laser
cut and 3D printed brackets. I affixed this to the helmet using flexible brackets printed in TPU and VHB double-stick
tape, with some white duct tape for insurance. The LiDAR plugs into the phone’s USB-C jack via a USB-to-serial adapter
for data and power. The squares on the side are AprilTags, which are visual tracking markers that I wanted to try using
for tracking the helmet in space to do some VFX experiments. They’re unrelated to the mapping. The whole thing felt
surprisingly sturdy but was pretty front-heavy so I added a power bank on the back purely as a counterweight.
(Photo credit: Sally)
On the software side, I wrote an Android app that implements a driver for the LiDAR. This wasn’t a big challenge because
of this nice
usb-serial-for-android
library and
an existing python library
I used as refe

data.title: Graceful Shutdown in Go: Practical Patterns
data.author: mkl95
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Go应用中的优雅关闭模式，主要包括三个核心步骤：关闭请求入口、等待正在处理的请求完成、释放关键资源。优雅关闭首先需要捕获操作系统信号（如SIGTERM、SIGINT、SIGHUP），Go运行时默认处理这些信号，但可以通过`os/signal`包注册自定义信号处理函数来实现优雅关闭。使用带缓冲的通道（容量为1）可以确保信号不会丢失，Go会在收到指定信号时将其发送到通道，开发者可以手动处理这些信号并执行自定义的关闭逻辑。通过这种方式，应用可以在接收到终止信号时从容地完成资源释放和清理工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应用程序的优雅关闭和相关问题，尤其是在Kubernetes和分布式系统中的处理方式

不同观点：
• karel-3d指出，使用`log.Fatal`不会执行`defer`语句，因为`log.Fatal`调用了`os.Exit`，立即终止程序。相比之下，`panic`会执行`defer`语句。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是如何在分布式系统中实现优雅关闭，特别是在Kubernetes环境下，如何确保在pod终止时不丢失连接和数据。
• 另一个值得注意的点是不同工具和语言对进程关闭的处理方式不同，例如Go中的`log.Fatal`和`panic`，以及Elixir中的进程管理。
• 实践中，很多人通过增加延迟（如preStop钩子的睡眠时间）和使用特定的设计模式（如waitgroup和context）来解决优雅关闭的问题。

by
Phuong Le
on
May 2, 2025
13 Minutes Read

Graceful Shutdown in Go: Practical Patterns
Graceful shutdown in any application generally satisfies three minimum conditions:
Close the entry point by stopping new requests or messages from sources like HTTP, pub/sub systems, etc. However, keep outgoing connections to third-party services like databases or caches active.
Wait for all ongoing requests to finish. If a request takes too long, respond with a graceful error.
Release critical resources such as database connections, file locks, or network listeners. Do any final cleanup.
This article focuses on HTTP servers and containerized applications, but the core ideas apply to all types of applications.
1. Catching the Signal
#
Before we handle graceful shutdown, we first need to catch termination signals. These signals tell our application it’s time to exit and begin the shutdown process.
So, what are signals?
In Unix-like systems, signals are software interrupts. They notify a process that something has happened and it should take action. When a signal is sent, the operating system interrupts the normal flow of the process to deliver the notification.
Here are a few possible behaviors:
Signal handler
: A process can register a handler (a function) for a specific signal. This function runs when that signal is received.
Default action
: If no handler is registered, the process follows the default behavior for that signal. This might mean terminating, stopping, continuing, or ignoring the process.
Unblockable signals
: Some signals, like
SIGKILL
(signal number 9), cannot be caught or ignored. They may terminate the process.
When your Go application starts, even before your
main
function runs, the Go runtime automatically registers signal handlers for many signals (
SIGTERM
,
SIGQUIT
,
SIGILL
,
SIGTRAP
, and others). However, for graceful shutdown, only three termination signals are typically important:
SIGTERM
(Termination): A standard and polite way to ask a process to terminate. It does not force the process to stop. Kubernetes sends this signal when it wants your application to exit before it forcibly kills it.
SIGINT
(Interrupt): Sent when the user wants to stop a process from the terminal, usually by pressing
Ctrl+C
.
SIGHUP
(Hang up): Originally used when a terminal disconnected. Now, it is often repurposed to signal an application to reload its configuration.
People mostly care about
SIGTERM
and
SIGINT
.
SIGHUP
is less used today for shutdown and more for reloading configs. You can find more about this in
SIGHUP Signal for Configuration Reloads
.
By default, when your application receives a
SIGTERM
,
SIGINT
, or
SIGHUP
, the Go runtime will terminate the application.
Insight: How Go Terminates Your Application
When your Go app gets a
SIGTERM
, the runtime first catches it using a built-in handler. It checks if a custom handler is registered. If not, the runtime disables its own handler temporarily, and sends the same signal (
SIGTERM
) to the application again. This time, the OS handles it using the default behavior, which is to terminate the process.
You can override this by registering your own signal handler using the
os/signal
package.
func
main
()
{
signalChan
:=
make
(
chan
os
.
Signal
,
1
)
signal
.
Notify
(
signalChan
,
syscall
.
SIGINT
,
syscall
.
SIGTERM
)
// Setup work here
<-
signalChan
fmt
.
Println
(
"Received termination signal, shutting down..."
)
}
Graceful shutdown begins with signal setup
signal.Notify
tells the Go runtime to deliver specified signals to a channel instead of using the default behavior. This allows you to handle them manually and prevents the application from terminating automatically.
A buffered channel with a capacity of 1 is a good choice for reliable signal handling. Internally, Go sends signals to this channel using a
select
statement with a default case:
select
{
case
c
<-
sig
:
default
:
}
This is different from the usual
select
used with receiving channels. When used for sending:
If the buffer has space, the signal is sent and the code continues.
If the buffer is full, the signal is discarded, and the
default
case runs. If you’re using an unbuffered channel and no goroutine is actively receiving, the signal will be missed.
Even though it can only hold one signal, this buffered channel helps avoid missing that first signal while your app is still initializing and not yet listening.
You can call
Notify
multiple times for the same signal. Go will send that signal to all registered channels.
When you press
Ctrl+C
more than once, it doesn’t automatically kill the app. The first
Ctrl+C
sends a
SIGINT
to the foreground process. Pressing it again usually sends another
SIGINT
, not
SIGKILL
. Most terminals, like bash or other Linux shells, do not escalate the signal automatically. If you want to force a stop, you must send
SIGKILL
manually using
kill -9
.

data.title: Thunderscope update: My take: Why open source is better
data.author: ChuckMcM
data.article_summary: ThunderScope是一款全新类型的示波器，具备高速、灵活和完全开放的特点，目前已开放预订。项目更新报告提到，团队正在全力推进Rev. 5的PCB设计，特别注重将ADC、时钟生成器、FPGA及其电源供应全部安装在散热片下，并增加了弹簧夹使散热片兼具屏蔽功能。设计中对四个前端做了细微差别处理，以测试接地和切口对衰减器电路的影响，并通过脚本改进了KiCad的长度匹配功能以实现延迟匹配。由于新设计和个人原因，产品将延期交付。接下来的步骤包括手动构建和测试Rev. 5，组装开发版PCB，制作测试夹具，并预计在9月前完成发货。项目进展将通过GitHub Issues公开跟踪。

43852217.article_content:
ThunderScope
A new type of oscilloscope that’s fast, flexible, and completely open
Available for pre-order
View Purchasing Options
Apr 30, 2025
Project update
11 of 11
Revving Up for Production
by
Aleksa B
Hi all,
I’ve spent the last month-and-a-half heads down on the PCB layout for Rev. 5…
I didn’t expect it to take that long, but then again this is the most effort I’ve ever put into a PCB design - it just had to be perfect!
High effort silkscreen aside, I’m especially proud of fitting the ADC, Clock Generator, FPGA and all their power supplies under the heatsink. I added spring clips so the heatsink can function as a shield for the whole acquisition section as well. Here’s some work-in-progress pictures from when I first placed everything (left) and at some point into the layout (right).
I also made the four front ends ever so slightly different from one another to test how the cutouts and grounding affect the elusive attenuator circuit. CH1 has a solid pour to all the components, while the other channels do not. CH3 and CH4 have progressively fewer ground plane cutouts than CH2. I’ve also via stitched the front end as I think that may have caused the wobbliness in the frequency response as dropping down a few layers causes the ground reference to change and, without vias nearby, the return current will have a hard time making it there.
The other change in the front end is the (re)addition of a trim cap (C1059). Since the buffer’s capacitance can vary from part to part, we want to trim it to a known level. This capacitance is about 2.4 pF, while variation in it will be sub 1 pF. This wasn’t much compared to the >100pF lower leg of the attenuator in previous designs, but with this new improved design we need to worry about it again. Trade-offs, trade-offs everywhere!
Teaching KiCad a New Trick - Matching Delays
At time of writing, KiCad only understands the length of traces and pins. When length matching, it takes length as a single number added up across every layer. This leads to delay mismatches, as the signals on the inner layers are slower than the signals on the outer layers. When assigning pin lengths, you need to arbitrarily choose a layer to convert a delay value (given by the manufacturer), to a length. This also results in delay mismatches.
I wanted to do this right, just like Altium does, but I didn’t want to have to calculate and add up all the delay values by hand in a spreadsheet. So I made a script to rewrite custom design rules to try to get KiCad’s length matching to be delay matching (including pad delays).
It was only slightly off from KiCad’s reported lengths, so not bad, as we just need consistency from trace to trace, not absolute accuracy. But then, as soon as I added a curved tuning pattern, it all fell apart.
I found out it was miscounting certain segments because of a small math error (normalizing the angle to [0,2*pi] when it should be [0,pi]) and got it working again! Below is the output of the script when tuning the skews on the PCIe lanes.
The rewriting design rules bit doesn’t work all that well given the slight discrepancy with the KiCad reported lengths and the whole delay-to-length conversion just assuming top layer for everything. However, if you just look at the delay deltas, then it’s pretty usable for tuning! In fact, I did all the delay matching on TS with this tool. If you want to try it yourself, I’ve put the script up in its
own separate repo
.
Next Steps, Accountability, and New Shipping Estimates
Now to address the elephant in the room, we won’t be shipping on time. The new interposer design, the switch to KiCad, and some personal issues all contributed to this. I take full responsibility and am committed to getting this done as quickly as possible while still holding myself and the project to the highest standards. So first things first, what are the next steps?
Hand Build Rev. 5:
Boards arrive at the end of April and I expect to get them built within a day or two of receiving them.
Test Rev. 5:
This should take no longer than two weeks.
Once these are done, I can roll any minor changes into a Rev 5.1. If there are any major changes needed, however unlikely, I will repeat the above process with a new rev.
Next up,
Get Dev. Edition PCBs Assembled:
send the design to a CM and wait a month or so.
Build Test Fixtures and Assembly Jigs:
use the time the CM is working on the PCBAs.
Test and Ship Dev. Edition units:
these should reach backers in July.
A month after shipping Dev. Edition units (to give time for any last bugs to be reported), we’ll do the same process as above for the rest of the units. We can improve our fixtures and jigs while the boards are out for fab and assembly, and then we should be able to ship in September.
To keep myself accountable, I will be using
GitHub Issues
to publicly track the tasks left before shipping, so check those out if you’re ever wondering how things are going between updates. Or, you can ask me directly through the project qu

data.title: On Not Carrying a Camera – Cultivating memories instead of snapshots
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 这篇文章的作者讲述了一次在北卡罗来纳州格林斯伯勒的回顾展上，一位摄影师问他为什么很少拍摄家乡 Chapel Hill 的照片。作者解释说，自己住在 Chapel Hill 时不带相机，因为无法同时做两件事——生活和拍摄。他回忆起1972年儿子出生时，自己因专注于拍照而未能全然在场，这让他意识到摄影让他与现实产生距离。从那以后，他决定与朋友相处时不再随时携带相机，以免错过生活中的真实瞬间。作者强调，被美的瞬间震撼是人类独特的礼物，而摄影往往是后来的事。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：拍摄照片的价值与平衡，特别是在重要时刻或生活经历中的拍摄行为。

不同观点：
• 有些人认为拍摄大量照片是必要的，因为最终可能只有一两张照片值得保留。这种观点强调了拍摄数量与质量的关系，以及对事后挑选出好照片的预期。([makeitdouble])

43890525.article_content:
Last summer, in Greensboro, North Carolina, at a retrospective exhibition of my work, a photographer introduced himself and asked a question no one had ever asked me. I assumed he was a photographer because he carried a camera bag, its pockets bulging with lenses. I thought he might ask if I preferred using a digital or a film camera, or if I preferred color to black-and-white film. But no, his question was different. He said he’d noticed that out of a hundred plus photographs in the exhibit, only one was titled “Chapel Hill.” “There must have been others, right? You’re from Chapel Hill.”
I told him that I seldom photographed in Chapel Hill.
“But why?” he asked.
I said, “Because I live there. I can’t do two things at once.”
I think he laughed. At least I hope he did, because I didn’t intend to be rude.
But I was serious.
I don’t carry a camera in my hometown of Chapel Hill, and even though my cellphone contains a camera, I use it only for snapshots. Naturally, there were moments when I wished I had a camera with me. Once, while walking in my neighborhood at twilight, I felt a strange rush of energy in the air, and, suddenly, no more than twenty feet away, a majestically antlered whitetail buck soared over a garden fence and hurtled down the dimming street. Yet even as it was happening—this unexpectedly preternatural moment—I tried to imagine it as a
photograph
. That’s how we’ve been taught to think. “Oh, I wish I’d had a camera!” But that presumes I would have been
prepared
to capture the moment—instead of being startled by it. Yet being startled by beauty is a uniquely, and all too rare, human gift. The photograph comes later, when I journey back from astonishment and begin to fiddle with my camera.
Well, I don’t carry a camera in town, and here’s the reason: In 1972, on the day my son was born, I was in the hospital room with my wife Susan, trying to be of assistance. I was there to remind her of certain breathing patterns we’d learned in our natural-childbirth classes, and to offer her encouragement during contractions. I was also there to photograph the birth of our child—my camera loaded with Tri-X film and fitted with a 50-mm lens.
Everything was going pretty well. We sang “Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band” to help regulate her breathing. However, when Susan was wheeled into the delivery room, I sensed a tension in the air. Doctors and nurses were rushing about, and, since the baby was arriving three weeks early, a small incubator stood on a gleaming aluminum cart in the corner. At that moment, even in the world of modern medicine, questions of life and death were not beside the point. A few minutes earlier, I’d taken out my camera and checked my light meter. Good, the room was bright enough. I could shoot at one-one-hundred-twenty-fifth of a second. Not much blur. I looked around for the proper angle from which to photograph the birth. Unfortunately, the doctors and nurses, who were moving quickly, even urgently, kept getting in my way. I moved here and there. What if a nurse blocked my view? I couldn’t say “Move,” but I wanted to. My frustration mounted. Nobody paid any attention to me. Then, looking through the viewfinder—there, within the rectangle of a potential photograph—I saw my wife’s face contract in pain. Multiple emotions flooded through me, but the one I identified first was the photographer’s “Yes!,” and I immediately pressed the shutter. Then, a minute later, when the doctor held a wriggling infant in the air, I pressed it again.
Over the next few days, I thought about my son’s birth. I was in the room when it happened, but was I really there, or had I been hiding behind my camera? I wanted the doctors to do whatever was necessary to bring my child safely into the world, but I also wanted them—and this was of equal importance—not to spoil my photograph. If something had gone wrong and Susan had desperately looked around the room for me, she would have seen a man holding a black box in front of his eyes. That image stayed with me, emblematically.
This was all a long time ago. I was learning how to use a camera. Walking with a friend, I’d interrupt a good conversation to frame something up. I couldn’t help myself. I hadn’t yet developed an inner point of view, my own way of seeing things, so
everything
seemed visually plausible. I also hadn’t yet realized that a good conversation—of which there would be fewer as time went by—was more important than an interesting symmetry seen out of the corner of my eye. Still, my friends made allowances for my “artistry,” for my sudden vacancies. It wasn’t until my son was born that I began to measure the size of the empty space I left behind when I’d raise my camera to my eyes and focus on something in the distance. It was this distance I eliminated on the day I stopped carrying my camera with me whenever I spent time with friends. As I said to the photographer who questioned me at the retrospective, “I can’t do two things at once.”

data.author: CGMthrowaway
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一篇数学论文的讨论，该论文涉及通过一系列解和组合数学来解决多项式问题，尤其是超卡塔兰数（Hypercatalan numbers）在多项式根的无穷级数中的应用。

不同观点：
• [throwaway81523] 认为该论文很简洁，并指出每个单变量多项式都有一个系数来自复杂组合数学的级数解，但找到论文的PDF下载链接存在困难。
• [v64] 提到论文的亮点在于超卡塔兰数的发展，这些数字是多项式无穷级数根的系数。他还指出，过去对卡塔兰数和根的特殊情况有部分研究成果，但论文中称为“Geode”的结构使之前的发现得以推广。
• [keepamovin] 对论文表示赞赏，认为其深度和创造性值得称道，尽管它并不是最终答案，只是通向更多理解的一步。还提到了作者的YouTube频道和博客。
• [emmelaich] 提供了一个新闻链接，指出该论文代表了一种解决高次多项式方程的新方法，并再次提到作者的博客和YouTube频道。
• [CGMthrowaway] 提供了一个通俗文章链接，帮助普通读者理解论文内容，并指引读者查看维基百科上关于卡塔兰数的条目以了解多边形分割。
• [vpribish] 以幽默的语气表示对“Hyper-Catan”的初步误解，但总体上对内容表示认可。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到作者的YouTube频道和博客，显示出对作者其他作品的关注。
• 提供了多个外部链接，帮助读者更方便地访问相关资源和背景信息。
• 争议的焦点可能在于对该论文是否为最终解决方案的看法，部分评论认为它只是理解更深层次问题的步骤之一。

data.article_summary: 文章讲述了Kat和她丈夫在婚后因AI使用问题导致关系破裂的故事。她的丈夫最初使用AI分析他们的关系，后来逐渐沉迷于向AI提出哲学问题，试图通过AI寻找“真相”。他声称AI帮助他恢复了幼年时被保姆试图溺亡的记忆，并认为自己是“世上最幸运的人”和“救世主”。Kat最终与他离婚，并在之后发现网上有类似情况的人，他们的伴侣因使用ChatGPT而陷入宗教或超自然妄想。一名匿名教师分享她的伴侣在几周内被ChatGPT迷惑，认为它是“宇宙的答案”，甚至自称是“上帝”。这些案例显示出人们对AI的过度依赖和由此引发的精神问题。
