data.title: Show HN: Free, in-browser PDF editor
data.author: philjohnson
data.article_summary: Breeze PDF是一款免费、强大的PDF编辑工具，完全在浏览器中离线运行，确保100%隐私。用户可以在PDF文档中添加文本、图片、签名，创建填表字段，合并或删除页面，以及加密保护文件，无需上传文件至服务器。该工具无需安装，适用于桌面和移动设备，文件处理均在本地完成，保障用户数据安全。Breeze PDF完全免费，无文件使用限制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PDF工具的功能、隐私性、技术实现及用户体验

不同观点：
• throwanem认为该工具在处理嵌入字体方面需要改进，但对工具整体表示认可，并提到希望能有一个单文件的HTML版本以便离线使用。他强调嵌入字体在PDF文档中一直是个难题，并对工具的发展表示期待。
• speerer赞赏该工具，分享了自己在处理PDF方面的经验，并提出了两个技术建议：使用WASM编译的MuPDF和选择不同分支的pdf-lib（他选择了cantoo fork，而作者使用了pdf-lib-plus-encrypt），询问作者的选择理由。
• denfromufa分享了自己创建的pdfmini工具，强调其开源、客户端运行、保护隐私的特点，并提供了工具链接和源码。
• kevinlinxc推荐使用stirling-pdf，这是一个可以通过Docker本地运行的PDF工具，并认为原作者应该尝试。
• kengoa从隐私角度讨论了自己维护的浏览器内数据可视化工具，提到很难说服用户相信数据不会被发送出去，并建议可能通过桌面版应用解决这一问题。
• Saris和afranchuk提到Firefox浏览器内置的PDF工具已经具备很多类似功能，质疑该工具的独特性。
• chfritz支持该项目，但提出浏览器缺乏“离线模式”的保证，建议提供Electron或Docker版本以确保离线使用。
• tbarbe分享了自己在疫情期间创建的类似离线工具，并提供了开源链接，虽然UI设计不太好。
• stefnotch指出该工具在保留PDF内链接方面存在问题，并提供了一个相关的GitHub issue链接，建议使用不同PDF库或手动实现该功能。
• nestorD表示将尝试该工具，但个人更倾向于使用本地工具Xournal++进行PDF编辑，同时寻求一种有效清理扫描PDF的方法。
• cbracketdash提供了详细的用户体验反馈，包括滚动问题、模态框关闭方式、字体编辑功能不足、文本框选择不清晰、删除页面确认模态烦人等问题，并建议增加撤销功能和缩放功能。
• behnamoh指出该工具不能真正“编辑”PDF文本，只能添加更多内容。
• afranchuk提醒不要在描述专有软件时使用“free”一词，以免引起混淆。
• jsomedon询问是否有可能开源该工具并允许私有部署。

补充讨论：
• 关于PDF工具的功能，用户对嵌入字体处理、链接保留、文本编辑等方面的技术问题进行了深入讨论，并提出了使用不同PDF库或分支的建议。
• 关于隐私和离线使用，用户对浏览器内工具的隐私保护表示关注，并提出了对离线使用模式的需求，建议开发桌面版或Docker版本。
• 关于用户体验，cbracketdash提供了详细的UI和功能改进建议，强调了与现有流行PDF工具（如ilovepdf.com或smallpdf.com）在质量上的差距。
• 开源和私有部署问题也被提及，有用户希望工具能开源并允许私有部署。

data.title: Closures in Tcl
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了Tcl编程语言中闭包的概念以及如何模拟实现闭包。作者首先解释了闭包的定义，并以C++代码为例说明了闭包的基本功能，即捕获和修改外部变量。然而，作者指出，在Tcl中实现闭包并不直接，因为Tcl缺乏对闭包的原生支持。文章进一步探讨了如何在Tcl中模拟闭包，并提到在Tcl/Tk 9.0发布后，社区对如何实现闭包展开了讨论。作者分享了自己对闭包的理解，并展示了在Tcl中模拟闭包的一种方法。文章还涉及了Tcl中环境变量的捕获和作用域问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Tcl作为多范式编程语言的能力及其与其他语言（如C++、Rust）在闭包和变量捕获方面的比较

不同观点：
• **[thesz]** 认为Tcl可以作为多范式编程语言使用，并通过SQL-like查询和回调函数来收集项目。他还提到自己在Tcl中实现了模式匹配，并应用于代数类型值。他提供了具体的参考链接，展示了Tcl在函数式编程中的潜力。

• **[RHSeeger]** 讨论了闭包在对象编程中的应用，指出闭包可以用于返回一组方法，这些方法作用于同一组变量，类似于对象的行为。这暗示了闭包在面向对象编程中的作用。

• 讨论中涉及了多种编程语言（Lisp、Tcl、C++、Rust）在不同编程范式（函数式、面向对象、多范式）中的应用和比较。

data.title: Modern Latex
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 《Modern LaTeX》是一份简明的LaTeX指南，旨在帮助用户快速上手，同时避免过时的复杂操作。LaTeX是一种优秀的排版工具，但许多指南已不再适用。该书介绍了如何使用LuaLaTeX（一个现代、支持Unicode的LaTeX版本）来构建文档，并推荐了一些字体如Garamond Premier和Neue Haas Grotesk等。构建书籍时需使用`latexmk`命令，若无法使用，可手动调用`lualatex`。该书源码和最新版本可从指定网址获取，并欢迎用户提出反馈和贡献。

不同观点：

• BlackFly提出的LaTeX现代化问题值得关注，特别是在响应式布局和在线阅读日益普及的背景下。

Modern LaTeX
LaTeX is a tool for creating beautiful writing, or a torture device that drives
users to the brink of madness every time they see bad spacing for the rest
of their lives. One of the two. Despite origins that can be traced back four
decades, it remains one of the best typesetting programs around. Many of its
guides, however, haven't aged as well. This short book will get you started with
LaTeX without bogging you down in arcana that lost its relevance back in the 90s.
Where do I get it?
An up-to-date version should be available at
https://assets.bitbashing.io/modern-latex.pdf
How do I build it?
Install LuaLaTeX, a modern, Unicode-aware version of LaTeX.
On Linux, this is usually as simple as installing your distro's TeX Live
package, e.g.,
texlive-base
or
texlive-core
.
The same package should also provide the
latexmk
script.
(See below)
Check out the
online
branch of the source repository,
which is optimized for digital display instead of a printed book.
Changes include even margins, centered page numbers, a lack of blank pages
between chapters, and so on.
Change the fonts as-needed.
The official version of this book is typeset with Garamond Premier,
Neue Haas Grotesk, URW Futura, Drive Mono, Noto, and (of course) Latin Modern.
In the likely case that you don't have all of these typefaces,
change the
fontspec
commands (e.g.,
setmainfont
, etc.) appropriately,
then modify or remove the colophon at the back of the book.
Build the book using
latexmk -lualatex -latexoption=-halt-on-error modern-latex.tex
Note that
latexmk
will run LuaLaTeX multiple times, since
TeX generates cross references in one pass, then links them in a second.
If you can't use
latexmk
for some reason, you can manually invoke
lualatex -halt-on-error -shell-escape modern-latex.tex
until it no longer warns,
"Label(s) may have changed. Rerun to get cross-references right."
Feedback
...is welcome!
Please issue pull requests on this book's Github page,
or contact the author via matt <at> bitbashing.io
Enjoy!

data.title: AI Meets WinDBG
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了将AI技术应用于崩溃分析的未来，重点介绍了如何利用AI改造传统的WinDBG调试工具。尽管软件开发的其他领域迅速发展，崩溃转储分析仍然依赖过时的命令行工具和手动操作。作者提出了一种全新的方法，通过与调试器进行对话来完成分析工作，取代手动输入复杂命令和解析输出。借助AI助手（如GitHub Copilot），工程师可以简单地问“应用程序为什么崩溃”，AI会自动分析崩溃转储，识别问题并提出修复建议。这种方法极大提高了效率，适用于多个崩溃转储文件的分析，并能处理复杂的调试任务。技术上，作者通过将WinDBG与AI连接，使用CDB进行可编程调试会话，并借助Anthropic开发的模型上下文协议服务器（MCP）实现AI与工具的交互。这一创新不仅帮助开发人员，也对支持和QA团队产生深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在调试工具中的应用，特别是ChatDBG和其他类似项目在调试过程中的作用和效果。

不同观点：
• **ChatDBG的先进性与实用性**：
   - emeryberger认为ChatDBG项目在通过LLM驱动调试过程方面走得更远，尤其是在与lldb/gdb和pdb的集成上，并且提供了API来充分利用调试器的功能。
   - ChatDBG自2023年以来已经下载超过8万次，并在FSE会议上发表了技术论文，显示其在解决许多问题上的有效性。

• **对AI调试工具的隐私与安全性担忧**：
   - lowleveldesign指出，在使用AI调试工具时，需要小心处理发送到外部服务器的数据，因为进程内存可能包含敏感信息。

The Future of Crash Analysis: AI Meets WinDBG
Posted on
2025-05-04
Old Meets New: Bringing Crash Analysis into 2025
Let's face it - while the rest of software development has evolved at warp speed, crash dump analysis feels like it's been preserved in digital amber for decades. We've got self-driving cars and pocket-sized supercomputers, yet here we are, still pecking away at command prompts like it's the dawn of the internet. Why is debugging the only area where we cling to tools that look like they belong in a computer history museum?
Picture this: You, a professional software engineer in 2025, hunched over a terminal, manually typing arcane commands like
!analyze -v
and
.ecxr
, squinting at hexadecimal memory addresses, and mentally translating stack traces. All while your friends in other industries are delegating their work to AI assistants that can write entire documents, create art, or automate complex workflows.
Something's wrong with this picture, right?
What if I told you we can throw that ancient workflow into the dustbin of computing history?
That's exactly what I've done. And I'm not talking about slightly better syntax highlighting or prettier UI for WinDBG. I'm talking about a fundamental transformation where you simply have a conversation with your debugger.
When Inspiration Strikes
During a debugging session at work, I had one of those lightning bolt moments. What if - and stick with me here - we could apply the same AI-assisted "vibe coding" approach to crash dump analysis?
Picture this: instead of manually slogging through memory dumps and command outputs, you simply ask, "Hey, why did this application crash?" and get an intelligent, contextual answer that actually helps you solve the problem.
The idea was too compelling not to pursue. So I built it.
See It In Action: AI-Powered Crash Analysis
Before diving into the technical details, let me show you what this looks like in practice. I have prepared a demo application to showcase two different use cases:
Video 1: Crash Analysis and Automated Bugfix
In this video, I show how Copilot can analyze a crash dump, identify the bug and auto-fix the issue.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
As you can see in the video, instead of manually running WinDBG commands and interpreting the cryptic output, I'm having a natural conversation with GitHub Copilot. The AI quickly identifies that the application crashed, explains which specific conditions led to the crash, and suggests a fix.
Video 2: Automated Crash Dump Analysis of multiple crash dump files
This video demonstrates a different capability: analyzing multiple crash dump files at once. It shows how the tool can quickly identify which dumps belong to your application and which don't.
Your browser does not support the video tag.
Worth noting, it takes just a few seconds until you get your first useful answer. I've played around with this for many hours and let me tell you one thing: You can really go deep. If you ask the right questions, the AI runs WinDBG/CDB commands that I haven't seen in all these years of debugging, and that is simply amazing.
How can this help the industry?
I believe this is one of the really good examples of how AI can boost productivity. Analyzing crash dumps is a very tedious task. It begins with quickly checking and identifying whether crashes are the same or different, and often requires very advanced knowledge when a crash is challenging - really challenging.
Copilot can help here tremendously; it knows how to:
Interpret assembly code (without you having to remember what EAX stands for)
Check memory contents (so you don't have to count hex bytes on your fingers)
Traverse structures with symbols (goodbye to manual pointer arithmetic!)
And so much more
This is a game changer - not just for engineers, but also for support, QA, and everyone involved with crash dumps. It's like going from hunting with a stone spear to using a guided missile.
How did I build this?
If you've ever worked with WinDBG, you know the drill: cryptic commands, obscure syntax, and endless scrolling through memory addresses and stack traces that make your eyes glaze over. It's the kind of specialized knowledge that takes years to master and feels like speaking an alien language even when you do.
The trick here is connecting WinDBG with AI. To do that, you first need to programmatically control a debugging session, right? There are plenty of options on how to do this. I prefer to keep things simple, so I have chosen
CDB
, which is Microsoft's Console Debugger. It operates on standard input and output, and that's so much more fun to deal with than setting up COM APIs or similar approaches.
The second part is "connecting with AI." That's where Model Context Protocol Servers come into the game.
Understanding Model Context Protocol Servers
MCP is an open standard developed by Anthropic, released in November 2024. This protocol allows AI models to interact with external tools and data sources - thi
43892096.article_summary: 本文探讨了将AI技术应用于崩溃分析的未来，重点介绍了如何利用AI改造传统的WinDBG调试工具。尽管软件开发的其他领域迅速发展，崩溃转储分析仍然依赖过时的命令行工具和手动操作。作者提出了一种全新的方法，通过与调试器进行对话来完成分析工作，取代手动输入复杂命令和解析输出。借助AI助手（如GitHub Copilot），工程师可以简单地问“应用程序为什么崩溃”，AI会自动分析崩溃转储，识别问题并提出修复建议。这种方法极大提高了效率，适用于多个崩溃转储文件的分析，并能处理复杂的调试任务。技术上，作者通过将WinDBG与AI连接，使用CDB进行可编程调试会话，并借助Anthropic开发的模型上下文协议服务器（MCP）实现AI与工具的交互。这一创新不仅帮助开发人员，也对支持和QA团队产生深远影响。

data.title: Semantic unit testing: test code without executing it
data.author: alexmolas
data.article_summary: 《Semantic Unit Testing》一文介绍了一种新的测试方法——语义单元测试。这种方法利用大型语言模型（LLM）分析函数的实现和文档说明（docstring），判断代码是否符合预期行为，而不仅依赖传统的输入输出对比。语义单元测试通过评估函数的描述和实现是否一致来发现潜在错误，无需实际运行代码。文章介绍了一个名为`suite`的Python库，它利用LLM自动检测代码中的问题。具体操作包括读取函数的实现和文档，提取相关信息并递归分析内部调用的方法，最终生成一个提示交给LLM判断。文章通过一个发牌函数的例子展示了该库的工作流程和使用方法。`suite`库通过这种智能分析方式，提高了代码审查的效率和准确性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在软件开发和代码验证中的应用及局限

不同观点：
• **LLM生成的代码需要严格的验证**：[vouwfietsman] 认为LLM可以用于辅助编写代码，但每行代码仍需经过验证，确保没有逻辑和推理上的问题。LLM本身不应负责验证，因为这可能会加剧问题。
• **对LLM接管工程的怀疑**：[RainyDayTmrw] 对LLM主导设计持怀疑态度，特别是考虑到现有代码库中不确定性（如测试不稳定）已经是一个问题。如果需要不确定性，已有更成熟的基于属性的测试方法。
• **LLM用于文档和代码比对的潜力与风险**：[lgiordano_notte] 认为LLM可以通过比对文档字符串和代码来发现问题，但需要小心过度依赖不充分的文档。
• **LLM代码审查而非测试**：[dragonwriter] 指出，LLM更多是用于代码审查，而非测试。将其称为测试是误导性的。
• **静态类型语言与动态类型语言的比较**：[jonathanlydall] 认为在静态类型语言中，很多验证工作在编译时完成，而在动态类型语言中则需要额外的测试，这可能使得LLM工具在动态类型语言中更有用。
• **AI辅助代码审查而非单元测试**：[jmull] 认为将LLM用于代码审查更合适，而不是单元测试。即使可以自动化运行测试，也需要手动审查结果。
• **LLM作为linter工具的潜力**：[brap] 认为LLM更适合作为linter规则，提供100%覆盖率，但需要选择性使用。

补充讨论：
• **LLM工具的有效性分析**：[yuliyp] 指出需要对LLM工具的有效性进行分析，包括其在实际代码库中的应用效果、误报率和漏报率。
• **代码正确性的证明与尝试**：[evanb] 引用Donald Knuth的话提醒大家，即使代码被证明正确，仍需实际尝试。
• **LLM在代码语义比对和安全审查中的应用**：[JanSchu] 分享了使用LLM进行语义比对的经验，包括其在发现代码与文档不一致、安全风险和不安全调用方面的潜力，同时提醒注意模型提示的压力和错误信心问题。
• **LLM与传统测试方法的比较**：[masklinn] 认为LLM更像是“气氛审查”，而不是证明代码正确性的工具，传统测试方法如属性测试和符号执行仍然不可或缺。
• **LLM在函数式编程中的潜力**：[simianwords] 提出LLM可能在纯函数式编程中更有用，因其无副作用和明确参数传递的特性。
• **LLM测试的随机性问题**：[rollulus] 担心LLM的随机性可能导致测试结果的不稳定。
• **LLM用于文档验证的潜力**：[cerpins] 认为LLM可能适合用于验证文档与代码的一致性，而不需要在代码和文档未改变时重新运行测试。

争议焦点：
• LLM在代码验证和测试中的角色和有效性：一方认为LLM可以有效辅助代码审查和文档比对，另一方则担心其不确定性和潜在误报问题。
• LLM工具的实际应用效果和覆盖率：对LLM工具在实际代码库中的应用效果和误报率、漏报率的分析需求。

总结：讨论围绕LLM在软件开发中的应用展开，主要争议点在于其验证代码的有效性和不确定性问题，同时对其在文档比对和代码审查中的潜力给予了一定认可。

Semantic Unit Testing
April 09, 2025 ·
18 mins · 3350 words
Left
Wallapop
a couple of weeks ago, heading to
RevenueCat
soon. In that classic ‘between jobs’ hacking window, I built
suite
: a Python library for semantic unit testing. What’s semantic unit testing? Think unit tests that understand context and meaning, not just
assert obj == expected
. Sound interesting? I’ll break down what semantic unit testing is, how suite works under the hood, and how you can integrate it.
What’s semantic unit testing?
Semantic unit testing is a testing approach that evaluates whether a function’s implementation aligns with its documented behavior. The code is analyzed using LLMs to assess if the implementation matches the expected behavior described in the docstring. It’s basically having an AI review your code and documentation together to spot discrepancies or bugs, without running the code.
This is, instead of writing classic unit tests with pairs of
(input, output)
, the testing responsibility is passed to an LLM. The hypothesis is that a powerful model, with good enough context, should be able to detect bugs without having to run the code. The idea is that an LLM can analyze the code and its documentation much like a human developer would -carefully reading and thinking hard about it- but much more quickly.
I wrote a package for doing semantic testing called
suite
(Semantic UnIt TEsting). You can install it using
uv
as
1
uv pip
install
suite
Here’s an example of how to perform a basic semantic test with
suite
from
suite
import
suite
tester
=
suite
(
model_name
=
"openai/o3-mini"
)

multiply
(
x
:
int
,
y
:
int
)
->
int
:
"""Multiplies x by y
Args:
x (int): value
y (int): value
Returns:
int: value
"""
return
x
+
y
result
=
tester
(
multiply
)
print
(
result
)
# {'reasoning': "The function's docstring states that it should multiply x by y.
#   However, the implementation returns x + y, which is addition instead of multiplication.
#   Therefore, the implementation does not correctly fulfill what is described in the docstring.",
# 'passed': False}
Basically, we have a
multiply
function that we want to test. To do so we create a
tester
instance that will use
o3-mini
as a judge. Then, we pass the method
multiply
to the
tester
, which internally will build a prompt containing all the information about it. Finally, the LLM will decide if the method is correctly implemented or contains a bug.
How does it work?
I’ve had this project on my todo list for a long time and I never had enough time and motivation to start it, however, some weeks ago
Vincent
released
smartfunc
(a library to turn docstrings into LLM-functions), and motivated me to start the project -and to be honest I borrowed some design choices from Vincent’s code. I also used
llm
library by
Simon Willison
to access different LLM providers easily.
The
suite
library does the following.
Receives a callable
func
as input.
Reads
func
implementation and docstring (using
inspect
library).
Analyzes the implementation of
func
to identify and extract any functions or methods that it calls internally.
Recursively applies steps 1, 2 and 3 to
func
inner methods (up to some
max_depth
).
Builds a
FunctionInfo
object with all the information about
func
we need.
Uses
FunctionInfo
to write a prompt which is passed to an LLM.
The LLM returns a structured output like
{"reasoning": str, "passed" bool}

• **AI辅助代码审查而非单元测试**：[jmull] 认为将LLM用于代码审查更合适，而不是单元测试。即使可以自动化运行测试，也需要手动审查结果。
• **LLM作为linter工具的潜力**：[brap] 认为LLM更适合作为linter规则，提供100%覆盖率，但需要选择性使用。

补充讨论：
• **LLM工具的有效性分析**：[yuliyp] 指出需要对LLM工具的有效性进行分析，包括其在实际代码库中的应用效果、误报率和漏报率。
• **代码正确性的证明与尝试**：[evanb] 引用Donald Knuth的话提醒大家，即使代码被证明正确，仍需实际尝试。
• **LLM在代码语义比对和安全审查中的应用**：[JanSchu] 分享了使用LLM进行语义比对的经验，包括其在发现代码与文档不一致、安全风险和不安全调用方面的潜力，同时提醒注意模型提示的压力和错误信心问题。
• **LLM与传统测试方法的比较**：[masklinn] 认为LLM更像是“气氛审查”，而不是证明代码正确性的工具，传统测试方法如属性测试和符号执行仍然不可或缺。
• **LLM在函数式编程中的潜力**：[simianwords] 提出LLM可能在纯函数式编程中更有用，因其无副作用和明确参数传递的特性。
• **LLM测试的随机性问题**：[rollulus] 担心LLM的随机性可能导致测试结果的不稳定。
• **LLM用于文档验证的潜力**：[cerpins] 认为LLM可能适合用于验证文档与代码的一致性，而不需要在代码和文档未改变时重新运行测试。

争议焦点：
• LLM在代码验证和测试中的角色和有效性：一方认为LLM可以有效辅助代码审查和文档比对，另一方则担心其不确定性和潜在误报问题。
• LLM工具的实际应用效果和覆盖率：对LLM工具在实际代码库中的应用效果和误报率、漏报率的分析需求。

总结：讨论围绕LLM在软件开发中的应用展开，主要争议点在于其验证代码的有效性和不确定性问题，同时对其在文档比对和代码审查中的潜力给予了一定认可。

data.author: misonic
data.article_summary: 本文由Fabien Sanglard撰写，探讨了学习编程语言与掌握编译工具之间的差距。作者回顾了自己学习C和C++语言的愉快经历，得益于许多优秀的教材。然而，学习如何将代码转化为可执行文件的过程却充满挑战，缺乏相关文献。大多数编程书籍仅介绍“Hello World”示例，而未深入讲解编译器使用。本文系列旨在填补这一空白，不教授语言或编写编译器，而是解释如何超越单文件示例，理解可执行文件的创建过程。内容涵盖编译器驱动、预处理、编译、链接和加载五个部分，通过具体步骤和工具帮助读者构建知识体系。本文例子基于Linux平台，但概念适用于其他操作系统。

43891398.article_content:
Driving Compilers
By
Fabien Sanglard
May 3rd, 2023
Mistake - Suggestion
Feedback
Introduction
←
→
I remember how pleasant it was to learn to program in C. There were so many good books explaining not only the language but also the standard library. I devoured both
The C Programming Language (K&R)
by Kernighan/Ritchie and
The Standard C Library
by P.J. Plauger. Then came
Expert C Programming
by Van der Linden and finally
C: A Reference Manual
by Harbison and Steele.
It was an equally enjoyable experience when I took on C++. I found myself unable to put down the
Effective C++
series by Scott Meyers. I loved the simple layout and the astute usage of red text for emphasis. I must have read half the first volume while standing in
Toronto World's Biggest Bookstore
before I left with the complete series under my arm. I remember power walking to my place to keep on reading.
A contrasting experience was to learn how to use the tools to turn my programs into executable. It was a painfully slow and deeply unpleasant process where knowledge was gathered here and there after trial, errors, and a lot of time spent on search engines. It felt like acquiring the same level of comfort to use a compiler took significantly more than learning the language.
I blame this experience on the lack of literature on the topic. Most language books start with a "Hello World" code sample. In the case of K&R, it would be
hello.c
.
#include <stdio.h>
int main()
{
printf("hello, world\n");
}
The reader is given the command to convert that text file into an executable and it is the last time they will hear about how to use the compiler.
$
cc hello.c
$
./a.out
hello, world
This is the gap this series attempts to fill. It won't teach about a language, its libraries, or an SDK. It won't teach how to write a compiler or a linker either. These articles are meant to ease leaving the world of one-file examples. It is a pot-pourri of the things I wish I had known when I was pulling my hair over mysterious
LNK2019
and other
LNK4002
errors.
Here will be explained the core concepts associated with the creation of an executable. As much as possible claims will be backed up with reproducible steps relying on
bintools
and driver verbose mode (
-v
). The goal is to provide the readers with both the tools and a mental map to explore beyond the charted territories of these pages.
Note:
Some liberties were taken with command invocation outputs for typesetting purposes. Commands such as
clang -v
generate a lot more than what is actually printed here. The uninteresting parts were removed to only keep what is relevant to the topic at hand. Rest assured that no command-line tools were hurt during the making of this text.
Environment
The examples assume a Linux platform. Depending on which illustrate the topic better,
gcc
or
clang
compiler drivers are used. If you are using Mac OS X or Windows, the ideas and concepts should be similar. Here is a table of equivalencies.
Platform
Driver
Object format
Dynamic library
Static library
Executable
Linux
gcc
elf
library.so
library.a
elf
Mac OS X
clang
macho
library.dylib
library.a
macho
Windows
CL.EXE
COFF
library.dll
library.lib
PE
The platform / toolchain association is the one most often encountered but they may vary. For example,
clang
is available on all platforms and
gcc
is available on Windows via cygwin.
Structure
1. driver
2. cpp
3. cc
4. ld
5. loader
This series is divided into five parts. First is explained the component which rules them all, the compiler driver
(1)
. Then we drill into the three stages of the compilation pipeline, detailing their inputs/outputs. The pre-processor
(2)
,
cpp
, converts source code files into translation units (TU), is covered first. Then comes the compiler
cc
(3)
, which ingests TUs and outputs relocatable (object) files. Then we look at the element combining all objects together into and executable, the linker
ld
(4)
.
In the fifth and final part we take a look at the linux loader (also called
ld
)
(5)
to further understand the linker output.
Next
The Compiler Driver (1/5)
*

data.title: Unparalleled Misalignments
data.author: ChadNauseam
data.article_summary: 这篇文章列出了一系列“无与伦比的不对齐”（Unparalleled Misalignments），即每对短语中的单词互为同义词，但整个短语的含义不同。例如，“Butt dial”和“Booty call”等。该列表自2018年起由Brian Smiley维护，并接受他人投稿。示例包括：“Home schooled”和“House trained”，“Manual labor”和“Hand job”等。这些短语通过幽默和文字游戏展示了语言的复杂性和多义性。列表中还标注了部分短语的贡献者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文字游戏和双关语的理解与自动化生成

不同观点：
• 有人认为应该为这些文字游戏提供解释，尤其是对非母语者。myflash13建议使用ChatGPT进行快速生成，并提出可以建立一个社交网络来评选最佳解释。（[myflash13]）
• 有人分享了自己在学习外语过程中遇到的类似困难，并幽默地提到了自己曾误用词语的经历。（[ben_w]）
• 有人从中找到了乐趣，并建议可以以此创作说唱歌词。（[flufluflufluffy]）
• 有人从技术角度提出，这可以作为一个机器学习项目，结合bigram语料库、词嵌入和NSFW文本分类器，但需要处理多义词的问题。（[gwern]）
• 有人认为这些文字游戏可能是有意为之，类似于一种“地下”创作，试图在审查中加入双重含义。（[roenxi]）
• 有人提议可以将这种文字游戏与Cockney Slang结合，增加难度和趣味。（[PeterStuer]）
• 有人对某些配对词语的合理性提出质疑，认为有些配对过于牵强。（[krisoft]）
• 有人进一步指出，这些配对更像是“概念上相邻”而不是真正的同义词。（[chabska]）
• 有人简单地表示这种文字游戏中的understatement是可以理解的。（[investa]）
• 有人提到Hacker News或Tweaker Buzz这样的技术社区可能对这种文字游戏感兴趣。（[jl6]）
• 有人承认自己需要时间才能理解其中一些双关语。（[saagarjha]）
• 有人对这种文字游戏表示高度赞赏，认为其非常天才。（[keeganpoppen]）

补充讨论：
评论中涉及了对双关语和文字游戏的理解难度、创作乐趣、技术实现可能性以及对某些配对合理性的质疑。争议的焦点在于某些词语配对是否合理，以及这些配对是真正的同义词还是概念上相邻。此外，还有人提出了扩展这种文字游戏的创意，如结合Cockney Slang。

data.title: MathML with Pandoc
data.author: goranmoomin
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了作者从MathJax转向使用MathML渲染方程的过程中，尝试了多种工具，最终发现Pandoc是最便捷的解决方案。Pandoc能有效处理LaTeX到MathML的转换，尤其在多行方程和矩阵处理上表现优异。然而，作者也发现Pandoc在处理某些复杂公式（如包含求和和极限的公式）时存在一个小bug，即极限符号的格式不正确。通过分析MathML代码，作者找出了问题所在，并计划向Pandoc的开发者John McFarlane反馈此问题。总体而言，Pandoc在大多数情况下是一个可靠且易用的工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pandoc及其在数学公式处理方面的功能和问题，包括MathML的支持、渲染方案的选择以及Pandoc在实际应用中的优缺点。

不同观点：
• [fiddlosopher] 作为Pandoc的开发者，指出了Pandoc使用texmath库处理公式转换，并提供了两个编译选项（`-fexecutable`和`-fserver`）。他还解释了有关空`<mo></mo>`标签的误解，指出其中包含不可见的U+2061字符，并承诺修复相关问题。

• [seanhunter] 认为评论中提到的极限格式问题并不是Pandoc的bug，而是LaTeX书写不明确所致。他解释说LaTeX会自行决定将极限格式化为行内样式或在其下方，如果希望强制在下方显示，需要使用`\lim\limits`。

• [bArray] 分享了自己在2021年遇到的MathML在Chrome等浏览器中支持不佳的问题，并选择了Preet的一个小实现方案。他提到当前解决方案要么是过度复杂的LaTeX包装器，要么是其他奇怪的方法，并表示可能编写一个解析器来解决这些问题。他还对JS的未来表示担忧，认为其可能会像Flash一样被淘汰。

• [satgo1546] 支持在Markdown源文件中保留MathML，而不是LaTeX，并提到自己编写了一个AutoHotkey脚本来处理Markdown到HTML的转换，计划用Pandoc替换其中的后端以支持MathML。

• [ayhanfuat] 提到GitHub最近也切换到了MathML，认为这是一个不错的回归。

• [huijzer] 询问是否有其他类似的转换工具，表示虽然喜欢Pandoc，但在生产环境中运行并不理想，但未具体说明原因。

• 关于MathML的支持情况，不同浏览器（如Chrome和Firefox）的表现差异。

• 对JS未来发展的看法，以及可能替代现有渲染方案的未来技术趋势。
• Pandoc在实际应用中的局限性及可能的其他替代工具。

And now it’s all this I just said what I said and it was wrong Or was taken wrong Previous post MathML with Pandoc May 3, 2025 at 11:25 AM by Dr. Drang Since switching from MathJax to MathML to render equations here on ANIAT, I’ve tried several approaches to generate the MathML. There are many utilities and libraries that claim to do the conversion, but I’ve found all of them to be limited in one way or another. For a while, I was even writing MathML directly, albeit with the help of some Typinator abbreviations, because I couldn’t trust the converters to generate the correct characters or even understand some LaTeX commands I use regularly. Recently, I began using what I should have started out with: Pandoc . It’s not that I wasn’t aware of Pandoc. Its famous in the Markdown/HTML/LaTeX world, and I probably first heard of it shortly after its release. But I’ve always thought of it as a document converter, not an equation converter. I was wrong. It’s very easy to use with a single equation. pandoc --mathml <<<'$$T = \frac{1}{2} v_x^2$$' produces

T = 12 vx2 T = \frac{1}{2} v_x^2

where I’ve added linebreaks and indentation to the output to make it easier to read. Because it’s delimited by double dollar signs, the equation is rendered in block mode, like this: T = 1 2 v x 2 Single dollar signs would generate MathML with a display="inline" attribute. (If you look at the source code for this page, you’ll see that I usually delete some of the code Pandoc generates—we’ll get to that later.) All the converters handled simple equations, like v 0 2 , well, but more complicated stuff can be troublesome. One of the problems other converters have is dealing with multiline equations, something Pandoc handles with ease. For example, this piecewise function definition, $$ f(x) = \left\{ \begin{array} {rcl} -1 & : & x<0 \\ 0 & : & x=0 \\ +1 & : & x>0 \end{array} $$ is rendered exactly as expected: f ( x ) = { − 1 : x < 0 0 : x = 0 + 1 : x > 0 Well, perhaps not exactly as expected. If you’re reading this in Chrome (and, presumably, other Chrome-based browsers), all the cells in the array are aligned left, which puts the zero in the wrong spot, not vertically aligned with the ones. But that’s Chrome’s fault, not Pandoc’s. Since Pandoc understands the \begin{array} command, it can do matrices, too: k = E A L [ 1 − 1 − 1 1 ] So far, I’ve found only one small bug in Pandoc’s conversion from LaTeX to MathML. Here’s a simple formula that includes both a summation and a limit: $$ e^x = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{x^n}{n!} = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left( 1+ \frac{x}{n} \right)^n $$ This is what it should look like, a screenshot of the equation as rendered by LaTeX itself: But here’s how it comes out after passing the equation to Pandoc: e x = ∑ n = 0 ∞ x n n ! = lim ⁡ n → ∞ ( 1 + x n ) n The summation is fine, but the limit is formatted incorrectly. The n → ∞ part should be under the lim , not off to the side like a subscript. That subscript-like formatting is what you’d use for an inline equation, not a block equation. Let’s see what happened. Here’s the MathML produced by Pandoc: xml: 1: 2: 3: 4: ex 5: = 6: 7: ∑ 8: n=0 9: ∞ 10: 11: 12: xn 13: n! 14: 15: = 16: 17: lim⁡ 18: n→∞ 19: 20: 21: 22: ( 23: 1+ 24: xn 25: ) 26: 27: n 28: 29: 30: 31: e^x 32: = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{x^n}{n!} 33: = \lim_{n\to\infty} \left( 1+ \frac{x}{n} \right)^n 34: 35: 36: The problem with the rendering of the limit is in Line 17. There’s an empty ⁡ element after the lim element. That’s what’s messing up the formatting. If we remove that empty element, the limit gets formatted the way it should: e x = ∑ n = 0 ∞ x n n ! = lim n → ∞ ( 1 + x n ) n Obviously, I’m not going to try to fix Pandoc; I have no idea how to program in Haskell. data.title: Towards the Cutest Neural Network
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
文章主要讲述了作者尝试在微控制器上使用神经网络来估算物体姿态的过程。由于传感器读数是非线性且相互耦合的，无法通过解析方法解决，作者决定使用简单的神经网络进行近似。具体步骤包括：通过正向模拟生成训练数据，训练一个小型神经网络来学习从传感器读数到姿态的映射，并将该网络部署到微控制器上进行推理。

作者遇到了几个挑战，尤其是在微控制器上进行整数运算推理，因为该设备不支持浮点运算。尽管发现了许多关于“量化”的文献，但大多数库和工具都过于复杂且依赖浮点运算。最终，作者使用了TensorFlow进行量化感知训练，并使用Rust的microflow-rs库进行推理，但仍需解决浮点运算问题以实现纯整数运算。

文章总结了神经网络的基本原理，强调了量化的概念，并希望找到更简洁的解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在嵌入式系统上实现小型神经网络的最佳方法，包括训练、量化、推理和代码实现等方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• [gwern] 认为在特定硬件上训练小型整数神经网络时，随机搜索或进化算法（如CMA-ES）是简单有效的方法，因为这些方法易于理解和实现，且不需要外部库。
• [JanSchu] 分享了在Cortex-M0和M3板上进行传感器融合的经验，建议使用固定点运算和CMSIS-NN库来避免浮点运算，并详细描述了从PyTorch原型到C代码实现的工作流程。
• [QuadmasterXLII] 支持JanSchu的观点，并提到使用C++和Eigen进行推理，以及从Python生成C++代码的方法。
• [jasonjmcghee] 提出考虑使用贝叶斯状态估计器，如无迹卡尔曼滤波器，作为另一种方法。
• [mattdesl] 讨论了BitNet（三值权重）在受限硬件上的潜力，并提到固定点运算的精度和性能问题，建议根据具体需求选择浮点或固定点表示。
• [imtringued] 批评原文作者在没有特殊情况下选择原生训练量化神经网络，认为这是不必要的复杂化，并建议使用固定点量化感知训练（QAT）和现有框架。
• [light_hue_1] 认为原文作者在没有系统学习和实验的情况下尝试复杂的方法是错误的，建议从PyTorch等现有框架开始，逐步优化网络和实现。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到了具体的工具和资源，如"A Neural Network in 11 lines of Python"教程和BitNet论文及其实现。
• 对于量化方法，有讨论提到训练后静态量化和量化感知训练（QAT）的区别和适用场景。
• 关于硬件优化，有评论提到需要注意指令生成、对齐和填充等问题，以提高性能。
• 对于不同神经网络架构的适用性，有评论提到梯度提升树在某些问题上的优越性能。

争议焦点：
• 是否应该使用现有框架（如PyTorch、TensorFlow）还是手动实现量化神经网络。
• 量化神经网络的训练方法和数据需求，特别是QAT是否需要大量数据。
• 在嵌入式系统上实现神经网络时，选择浮点还是固定点运算的性能和精度权衡。

43861297.article_content:
Towards the cutest neural network ← Back to Kevin's homepage Published: 2025 April 28 I recently needed to use a microcontroller to estimate the pose (translation and orientation) of an object using readings from six different sensors. Since the readings were non-linear and coupled with each other, an explicit analytical solution was out of the question. I figured I’d have a go at using a simple neural network to approximate it: generate training data (on my computer) using a forward simulation (pose to sensor readings) train a lil’ neural network (a few dense layers, 100’s of parameters, tops) to approximate the inverse mapping function (sensor readings to pose) deploy this network on my microcontroller (Cortex-M0, 16 kB RAM, 32 kB flash) to actually do the inference Since neural networks have been around since the 1980’s, I figured it’d be straightforward. A quick background search uncovered lots of promising leads too, especially regarding “quantization”, which I wanted to do as my microcontroller doesn’t have hardware support for floating point operations. However, this turned out to be much more difficult than I’d anticipated. It seems like my use case — end-to-end training of a simple dense neural network with integer-only inference — is quite uncommon. The vast majority of papers and software libraries I found turned out to be complex, heavyweight (in terms of inference code size), and have lots of unstated assumptions and background requirements. To make a web design analogy: It felt like I kept falling into npm create-react-app rabbit holes rather than what I wanted: The moral equivalent of opening index.html with notepad.exe and typing

Welcome to my Homepage

. I’m writing up my notes to: checkpoint my understanding of the space and current best solution help anyone else who simply wants a wholesome lil’ universal function approximator with low conceptual and hardware overhead solicit “why don’t you just …” emails from experienced practitioners who can point me to the library/tutorial I’ve been missing =D (see the alternatives-considered down the page for what I struck out on) tl;dr, how to do it? use TensorFlow to do quantization-aware training and save the resulting model out to a .tflite flatbuffer file use the microflow-rs crate for inference — it’s basically a proc macro that reads tflite file and generates straightforward Rust code that uses nalgebra to multiply matrices Props to Matteo for being seemingly the only person in this space who can put a clear “hello world” inference example in their README.md: use microflow :: model ; #[model( "path/to/model.tflite" )] struct MyModel ; fn main () { let prediction = MyModel :: predict ( input_data ); } It should be cuter. Unfortunately, MicroFlow (and TensorFlow’s out-of-the-box quantization routines, from what I can tell) require floating point operations for inference. While I could use software floating point, I want to make the cutest possible neural network, which means integer arithmetic operations only. (The code size and speed of software floating point depends on the routines used. qfplib-m0-full has a good overview and shows that, e.g., the GCC compiler software floating point multiplication takes 166 cycles.) On the MicroFlow side, removing floating point operations would require a big redesign, as: they’re baked into the API ( predict assumes f32 inputs and outputs). the internals themselves rely on floating point the MicroFlow proc macro reads the .tflite flatbuffer ( source ) when reading a fully-connected layer it combines the various quantization scale factors and zero points into f32 constants these constants are then used during inference at runtime On the TensorFlow side, I can’t find any documentation/options about whether the quantization-aware training routines use floating point activation scaling or if they can model quantized multipliers. But I’m getting ahead of myself — let’s first review the mathematics of neural networks and meaning of “quantization”. Neural network overview The basic idea of neural networks you have a bunch of training data: $x$, the input data you have (in my case, readings from six sensors) $y$, the output value you are trying to predict (the object pose) Since you have no idea how to go from $x$ to $y$ yourself, you throw together $n$ general equations (“layers”) like: \begin{align} a_1 &= \sigma(W_1 x + b_1) \newline a_2 &= \sigma(W_2 a_1 + b_2) \newline \vdots \newline \hat{y} &= \sigma(W_{n} a_{n-1} + b_n) \end{align} These equations take your input $x$ and make a prediction $\hat{y}$ which, hopefully, is close to $y$. The equations require: free parameters $W$ and $b$ (the “weights” and “biases”, respectively); in our case these are a matrix and vector rather than scalar values, since our input data $x$ comes from multiple sensors and the the output pose $y$ has six components (three spatial positions and three spatial rotations) $\sigma$, some nonlinear “activation” function (traditio

• [JanSchu] 分享了在Cortex-M0和M3板上进行传感器融合的经验，建议使用固定点运算和CMSIS-NN库来避免浮点运算，并详细描述了从PyTorch原型到C代码实现的工作流程。
• [QuadmasterXLII] 支持JanSchu的观点，并提到使用C++和Eigen进行推理，以及从Python生成C++代码的方法。
• [jasonjmcghee] 提出考虑使用贝叶斯状态估计器，如无迹卡尔曼滤波器，作为另一种方法。
• [mattdesl] 讨论了BitNet（三值权重）在受限硬件上的潜力，并提到固定点运算的精度和性能问题，建议根据具体需求选择浮点或固定点表示。
• [imtringued] 批评原文作者在没有特殊情况下选择原生训练量化神经网络，认为这是不必要的复杂化，并建议使用固定点量化感知训练（QAT）和现有框架。
• [light_hue_1] 认为原文作者在没有系统学习和实验的情况下尝试复杂的方法是错误的，建议从PyTorch等现有框架开始，逐步优化网络和实现。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到了具体的工具和资源，如"A Neural Network in 11 lines of Python"教程和BitNet论文及其实现。
• 对于量化方法，有讨论提到训练后静态量化和量化感知训练（QAT）的区别和适用场景。
• 关于硬件优化，有评论提到需要注意指令生成、对齐和填充等问题，以提高性能。
• 对于不同神经网络架构的适用性，有评论提到梯度提升树在某些问题上的优越性能。

争议焦点：
• 是否应该使用现有框架（如PyTorch、TensorFlow）还是手动实现量化神经网络。
• 量化神经网络的训练方法和数据需求，特别是QAT是否需要大量数据。
• 在嵌入式系统上实现神经网络时，选择浮点还是固定点运算的性能和精度权衡。

data.title: Space Invaders on your wrist: the glory years of Casio video game watches
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了卡西欧在20世纪80年代推出的带有游戏功能的电子表，尤其是1981年发布的CA-90/CA-901表，它结合了计算器和太空射击游戏。卡西欧高管Yuichi Masuda表示，公司认为手表不仅是看时间的工具，还可以具备多种功能，如电话号码存储和音乐闹钟。虽然当时任天堂的Game & Watch系列也推出了类似的手持游戏，但卡西欧称其灵感来源于自身技术发展，而非任天堂。在1980到1985年间，卡西欧研发了多种不同类型的游戏手表，尽管受限于当时的LCD显示技术，这些游戏仍展现了丰富的创意，包括赛车、射击和平台跳跃游戏等。这些手表在80年代的学校孩子中非常受欢迎，如今也成为了收藏品。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Casio手表与现代智能手表的对比及其功能和怀旧情感

不同观点：
• [curiosity42] 认为Casio手表尽管功能简单，但相比Apple Watch和Android手表更受其儿子的青睐，突显了Casio的持久吸引力，尤其是对年轻用户。
• [forinti] 对Casio手表的内部机制和技术细节表示好奇，但发现相关信息很少，尤其是控制器方面的细节，暗示了Casio在技术保密上的成功。
• [throwanem] 提出可以将Casio的简单功能与现代可编程智能手表结合，比如使用"digital crown"来适配某些游戏，探索了传统与现代技术结合的可能性。
• [JSR_FDED] 通过分享自己童年时长时间玩Casio计算器手表游戏的经历，强调了Casio手表的娱乐性和持久吸引力，类似于任天堂Wii，尽管图形简单，但游戏性强。
• [dlachausse] 提到Atari最近发布的可以玩游戏的手表，链接了Casio手表与现代游戏手表的联系，指出旧技术和现代技术之间的循环和复兴。
• [timewizard] 分享了自己对Timex Datalink手表的怀旧情感，尤其是其"太空认证"的特性，并对比了旧款和新款手表的魅力和功能，强调了某些经典款式的不可替代性。
• [aa-jv] 分享了自己从80年代至今对LCD手表的喜爱，尤其是Casio手表的游戏功能，并表达了希望在现代开源手表（如PineTime和Watchy）上开发Casio风格表盘和应用程序的愿望，探索了将怀旧情感与现代技术结合的可行性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Casio手表为何能在功能简单的情况下依然受到青睐。一部分人认为是其娱乐性和简单性，另一部分人则对其技术保密和持久吸引力表示好奇。
• 重要论据和例子：
  - curiosity42的儿子更喜欢Casio手表，尽管他有更先进的智能手表。
  - forinti对Casio手表技术细节的好奇和信息缺乏。
  - JSR_FDED分享了自己童年长时间玩Casio手表游戏的经历。
  - dlachausse提到了Atari最近发布的游戏手表，指出了旧技术和现代技术的复兴。
  - timewizard对Timex Datalink手表的怀旧情感和对经典款式的喜爱。
  - aa-jv希望在现代开源手表上开发Casio风格表盘和应用程序，探索怀旧情感与现代技术结合的可能性。

这些观点共同构成了关于Casio手表与现代智能手表的对比及其功能和怀旧情感的丰富讨论。

Space Invaders on your wrist: the glory years of Casio video game watches
Their tech may have been primitive, but for 80s schoolchildren of a certain kind they had a glamour to equal any modern iPhone
Keith Stuart
Fri 2 May 2025 04.00 EDT
Last modified on Fri 2 May 2025 23.43 EDT

ver the last couple of weeks I have been tidying our attic, and while the general aim has been to prevent its contents from collapsing through the ceiling, I have a side-mission. My most valued possession when I was twelve was a Casio GD-8 Car Race watch – a digital timepiece that included a built-in racing game on its tiny monochrome LCD display. Two big buttons on the front let you steer left and right to avoid incoming vehicles and your aim was to stay alive as long as possible. I lost count of the number of times it was confiscated by teachers at my school. I used to lend it to the hardest boys in the year, thereby guaranteeing me protection against bullies. As a socially inept nerd, this was invaluable to my survival. I’m pretty sure I still have the watch somewhere, and my determination to find it has been augmented by a recent discovery: these things are valuable now.
Casio started making digital watches in the mid-1970s, using technology it had developed in the calculator market to compete on price, but as the decade drew to a close, the market became saturated and the company started to explore new ways to entice buyers.
Speaking to Polygon in 2015
, Yuichi Masuda, senior executive managing officer and Casio board member, explained, “Casio went back to its original thinking when it first entered the watch market; that is, ‘a watch is not a mere tool to tell the time.’ We started talking about a multifunction [approach], time display plus other things, such as telephone number memory and music alarms.”
View image in fullscreen
Taking off … children playing Space Invaders in 1980.
Photograph: Eugene Adebari/REX/Shutterstock
At the time, Taito’s arcade game Space Invaders was a phenomenon in Japan. And so in 1981 Casio launched the CA-90/CA-901, a chunky calculator watch that included a sort of space shoot-’em-up but with numbers rather than alien spaceships advancing down the screen. “We wanted to create a new lifestyle of enjoying the game anywhere at any time,” said Masuda.
But wasn’t Casio also inspired by Nintendo’s Game & Watch series? After all, this iconic range of handheld electronic games started in 1980 with the juggling and catching sim Ball, and its success led to a vast array of titles, including the famed two-screen Donkey Kong that inspired the Nintendo DS. Shinji Saito, general manager and chief producer at the product planning department of Casio’s timepiece business unit, says not. “In 1980, the year before Casio launched the CA-90, Casio launched the MG-880, a game calculator that allowed users to enjoy digital invaders. Nintendo’s Game & Watch was also launched in 1980,” he says. “In developing the CA-90, Casio utilised the development assets of its MG-880 game calculator, but the starting point for the idea was Casio’s development philosophy of creating a new culture using light, thin, short and low-power technology. We were
not
inspired by Nintendo’s Game & Watch.”
Indeed, Casio was developing a wide array of innovative features at the time including databanks, thermometers and pulse checkers. “Their entire watch range in the 80s was huge,” says watch enthusiast Andy Bagley. “I have been collecting for years and even now I will still come across a model I haven’t seen before; there were many hundreds. I only recently discovered Casio made a range of touch screen watches in the 80s – way ahead of their time!”
View image in fullscreen
Times past … Casio Gaming watch page from Vintage Casio catalogue
Photograph: Casio
Whatever the case, the CA-90 was such a success that it inspired a period of rampant creativity in the Casio R&D department. Between 1980 and 1985 the company produced dozens of different game watches – an incredible feat considering the limitations of LCD displays at the time, which couldn’t produce computer graphics or animation and simply relied on matrices of pre-set shapes that would switch on and off to suggest movement. There were several different racing games, there were shoot-’em-ups such as Heli-Fighter and Zoomnzap, and there were very rudimentary platformers including Jungle Star, where you play a Tarzan character leaping out of the way of rampaging panthers, and Hungry Mouse, where you are the mouse leaping over incoming cats.

data.title: Apple Shortcuts is falling into "the automation gap"
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Mac上Shortcuts功能的进展缓慢问题。作者John Voorhees回顾了三年前对AppleScript通过Shortcuts集成的质疑，指出如果Shortcuts要成为Mac上自动化任务的主要方式，需要每年稳步进展。然而，Shortcuts在Mac上的发展并不稳定，作者通过复杂的多工具自动化实例（如Stream Deck、Keyboard Maestro、JavaScript、AppleScript等）展示了目前Shortcuts的不足。尽管Apple希望通过App Intents改进Shortcuts，但其功能仍显不足，尤其是在条件语句等方面。作者认为，Apple宣称的“多年过程”已过去近四年，改进空间有限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple的Shortcuts功能在实用性、功能限制、用户体验等方面的不同观点和争议

不同观点：
• jtrn认为Shortcuts功能限制过多，尤其是无法实现如键盘快捷键、SMS触发等功能，认为这些限制更多是苹果的哲学或政治考量，而非技术问题。
• rcarmo指出Shortcuts在iOS上勉强可用，但在macOS上几乎无用，因为有更强大的Automator和AppleScript。同时批评苹果在自动化技术上的投资不足。
• hn_throw2025对Shortcuts持积极态度，分享了其在家庭自动化中的实际应用，如通过SSH命令控制设备，认为其功能满足了自己的需求。
• walterbell提供了Shortcuts在iOS 18中的一些新功能和应用示例，如通过SSH脚本或API执行外部任务，展示了Shortcuts的潜力。
• sholladay详细描述了自己在创建简单报警功能时遇到的多个问题，包括设备间不一致、HomePod功能限制、音量控制问题等，表达了对Shortcuts的复杂情感，倾向于不满。
• jbverschoor认为Shortcuts对程序员和非程序员都不友好，原因在于不了解其用户群体。
• aucisson_masque指出Shortcuts是iPhone的一大卖点，但大多数普通用户并不关心其存在。认为苹果更关注大众功能而非小众需求。
• dawnerd希望实现简单的车载热点自动化，但经常失败，表达了对通知无法关闭的不满。
• oneeyedpigeon认为Shortcuts在macOS上缺乏Automator的功能，但作为入门任务（如切换深色模式）还是有用的。
• mrtksn认为Shortcuts的UI冗长且功能神秘，建议采用类似Swift的编码方式来简化使用。
• ErneX认为尽管Shortcuts功能有限，但仍很有用，分享了通过Shortcuts下载视频和运行Python脚本的实际应用。
• jfernandezr仅使用Shortcuts记录车辆里程，认为由于集成的应用不足，找不到其他有用功能。
• citizenkeen对文章标题中未解释的术语“automation gap”表示不满。
• internet_points分享了通过Shortcuts实现拔掉充电器时自动开启省电模式的实用功能，对此感到满意。
• jen20作为macOS的资深用户，首次尝试Shortcuts以自动化电视应用，但因应用未提供所需功能而取消订阅，表达了对应用开发者的失望。

补充讨论：
• Shortcuts功能在iOS和macOS上的表现差异显著，用户对苹果在自动化技术上的投资和优先级存在质疑。
• 用户对Shortcuts的功能限制（如触发条件、音量控制、设备间不一致等）表达了不满，但也有用户通过创造性应用找到了实际价值。
• 对Shortcuts的UI设计和使用体验存在争议，部分用户认为其冗长复杂，建议采用更直接的编码方式。
• 普通用户和高级用户对Shortcuts的需求和期望不同，普通用户可能不关心或不需要复杂的自动化功能，而高级用户则希望有更多自定义和控制选项。

by Jason Snell
March 28, 2025 1:46 PM

Shortcuts is falling into “the automation gap”
John Voorhees,
writing on Club MacStories
(subscription required):
Nearly three years ago, I wrote
AppleScript: Shortcuts Bridge or Crutch?
, questioning whether accessing AppleScript via Shortcuts on the Mac was a feature to be celebrated or a red flag, fearing that Apple would use the integration to postpone or never release many of the system-level actions that were missing from Shortcuts’ debut on the Mac.
As I put it then, “if Shortcuts is to become the default way to automate tasks on the Mac, there needs to be steady, yearly progress to make macOS and its default system apps as Shortcuts-friendly as possible. There’s a role for AppleScript to play in Shortcuts that won’t go away anytime soon, but not as a way to fill the potholes left by missing Shortcuts actions.”
Shortcuts’ progress on the Mac has been anything but steady and yearly.
A few days ago, while writing my
Podcast Notes update
, I realized that I had (inadvertently?) created an automation that begins with a Stream Deck keypress that executes a Keyboard Maestro macro that kicks off a JavaScript script in Audio Hijack that runs an AppleScript applet that executes a Shortcuts shortcut. In recent days I’ve also edited shortcuts that run Python and AppleScript scripts, including some where the shortcut is really nothing more than a Mac UI-friendly wrapper around a bare script, much in the same way you can use Automator as a simple wrapper around AppleScript scripts.
That all these things are possible on the Mac is amazing, and it’s a testament to how flexible and powerful the Mac can be. But it also says something quite profound about how little progress Apple has made with Shortcuts on the Mac (or in general) in the last few years. (And of course, all these workarounds fail on iOS entirely.)
Maybe the drive toward App Intents will help make Shortcuts more powerful and less reliant on tools like AppleScript, Keyboard Maestro, and the rest. But even that isn’t enough, since the Shortcuts app is way too rickety and limited. Just the other day, Dan Moren said to me, “I was working on a shortcut and I needed an if-else-if statement,” and we both began laughing because conditionals are just
so bad
in Shortcuts.
Apple gave itself a lot of leeway by declaring that Shortcuts was the “beginning of a years-long process” to make Shortcuts the “future of automation on the Mac.” But that was almost four years ago. There’s not a lot of leeway left for me to give.

• aucisson_masque指出Shortcuts是iPhone的一大卖点，但大多数普通用户并不关心其存在。认为苹果更关注大众功能而非小众需求。
• dawnerd希望实现简单的车载热点自动化，但经常失败，表达了对通知无法关闭的不满。
• oneeyedpigeon认为Shortcuts在macOS上缺乏Automator的功能，但作为入门任务（如切换深色模式）还是有用的。
• mrtksn认为Shortcuts的UI冗长且功能神秘，建议采用类似Swift的编码方式来简化使用。
• ErneX认为尽管Shortcuts功能有限，但仍很有用，分享了通过Shortcuts下载视频和运行Python脚本的实际应用。
• jfernandezr仅使用Shortcuts记录车辆里程，认为由于集成的应用不足，找不到其他有用功能。
• citizenkeen对文章标题中未解释的术语“automation gap”表示不满。
• internet_points分享了通过Shortcuts实现拔掉充电器时自动开启省电模式的实用功能，对此感到满意。
• jen20作为macOS的资深用户，首次尝试Shortcuts以自动化电视应用，但因应用未提供所需功能而取消订阅，表达了对应用开发者的失望。

补充讨论：
• Shortcuts功能在iOS和macOS上的表现差异显著，用户对苹果在自动化技术上的投资和优先级存在质疑。
• 用户对Shortcuts的功能限制（如触发条件、音量控制、设备间不一致等）表达了不满，但也有用户通过创造性应用找到了实际价值。
• 对Shortcuts的UI设计和使用体验存在争议，部分用户认为其冗长复杂，建议采用更直接的编码方式。
• 普通用户和高级用户对Shortcuts的需求和期望不同，普通用户可能不关心或不需要复杂的自动化功能，而高级用户则希望有更多自定义和控制选项。

data.title: Visualising home sun exposure with Rhino
data.author: ostwilkens
data.article_summary: 本文是一位屋主对房屋日照情况的回顾和可视化过程的分享，而非指导指南。作者在房屋 renovation 时意识到日照对不同区域的重要性，尤其是避免在缺乏日照的阳台浪费资金。为了更好地理解日照情况，作者使用Rhino 3D软件及其插件Grasshopper和Ladybug进行了日照模拟。通过这些模拟，作者发现早晨地面阴影处适合户外早餐，院子和可接近的较低屋顶适合午餐，而西向阳台由于日照不足不适合晚餐。最终，作者决定取消对西阳台的原计划，从而节省开支。此外，通过模拟发现屋顶仍适合安装太阳能板，未来可能会考虑使用太阳能。

43856208.article_content:
Visualising sun exposure for our house
Disclaimer: this is not a guide, but a retrospective surface-level documentation of what I achieved
We're doing a lot of renovations right now. I've been thinking about how our house is used, but also how it could change in the future. One thing I didn't give much thought when initially looking at the house is how it relates to the cardinal directions. Well, we've been living here 4 years now, and I'm just now realizing we don't have a lot of evening sun.
When considering how much attention and money to allocate to different areas, I realized sun exposure is really important. I don't want to spend tons of money on a balcony that never sees the sun. And so I thought, this must be possible to visualize with software.
My conversation on TypingMind
I had no idea where to begin, so I asked ChatGPT. It suggested trying the following:
Sketchup with extensions
Rhino with Ladybug
Autodesk Revit
Going with Rhino 3D
Rhino has a month-long trial version which works on MacOS, and also seemed powerful enough to do what I want.
It took some getting used to, searching the documentation, and following youtube tutorials. But after (quite) a few hours, I had a somewhat precise model of my building and the surrounding area. I utilized old drawings of our house, and made some measurements by hand. Working with Rhino feels like a very peculiar mix of CAD and 3d modeling software like Blender.
Bear with me, there are some names to keep track of.
Rhino is the main software.
Grasshopper is a visual programming interface (with a Python backend)
Ladybug is an extension to Grasshopper, which allows for sun calculations.
There are some great tutorials for Ladybug on youtube, which will help you achieve the same things as me.
Simulation results
I wanted to determine which areas are fitting for a nice summer lunch, or dinner. I ran the following simulations:
The sun is intense in the morning. Most likely, if we're looking for a nice outdoor breakfast, we'll do it in a shade on the ground level.
It looks like the yard on ground level is a good fit for lunch as well. The lower roof would also be a good fit, if we were to make it accessible.
As suspected, evening sun is looking grim. What I learned is: if we plan in advance, we can get a few hours of sun for a nice dinner on our west-facing balcony.
Main takeaway: We had some plans for the west balcony. Seeing as it doesn't get much sun at all, we're scrapping those plans, and just doing the minimum. Money saved!
Solar surprise
A bonus simulation: Incident Radiation. Because we barely experience the sun from the south, I expected solar panels to be a bad pick for us. Turns out, our roof actually has a different experience! Seeing this, we might actually consider solar energy in the future.
Written 2025-04-16

data.title: DotnetSnes: Library allowing to use C# to create SNES ROMs
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: DotnetSnes 是一个允许使用 .NET 语言创建真实 SNES ROM 的库。它通过 DotnetSnes.Core 库将 C# 代码转译为 C，再利用 PvSnesLib SDK 工具链编译成 SNES ROM。由于 SNES 的限制，开发中需注意系统级类型支持、无动态内存分配、最小化堆栈变量和指针追踪等。开发环境建议使用 Linux 或 WSL，需安装相关依赖如 cmake、g++ 和 dotnet-sdk-8.0。开发者可通过克隆仓库、初始化子模块并运行 make 命令来准备环境和构建项目。示例项目包括简单的 "Hello World" 和 "LikeMario" 游戏，展示了基本游戏逻辑、地图、音频和输入管理。创建新项目需新建 .NET 类库，引用相关库并定义入口函数，最后编写 Makefile 进行构建。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过Fable将F#转换为Rust的可行性及其实际限制

不同观点：
• reverseblade2认为，可以通过Fable工具将F#代码转换为Rust代码，并提供了一个GitHub链接（fable-raytracer）作为示例，表明这种转换是可行的。
• SideburnsOfDoom则指出，这种方法存在严重限制，特别是缺乏对动态内存分配的支持，这意味着无法使用引用类型和类实例。这将从根本上改变语言的特性，限制其实用性。

补充讨论：
• rawling提到了在Hacker News上三周前有过相关讨论，表明该话题已经引起了一些关注，可能有进一步的讨论和不同的见解。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于通过Fable将F#转换为Rust的可行性和实际应用中的限制。具体而言，是否能够克服不支持动态内存分配等限制，从而在实际项目中有效使用这种转换方法。

总结：
评论中主要讨论了通过Fable工具将F#转换为Rust的可能性及其限制。一方认为这种方法可行并提供了示例，而另一方则强调了其在实际应用中的严重限制，特别是对动态内存分配和类实例的支持缺乏。此外，该话题之前已有讨论，表明其具有一定的关注度。

DotnetSnes
Allows using .net languages to create real working SNES roms!
How Does It Work?
Getting Started
Dependencies needed to install on WSL Ubuntu for make
Preparing the Repo and SDKs
Hello World Example
LikeMario Game Example
Creating a New Project
How Does It Work?
This works by providing a .net library that abstracts functions and globals used in creating SNES games. Once a
project using the
DotnetSnes.Core
library is compiled, the resulting DLL is transpiled to C using the
Dotnet To C transpiler (dntc)
. The game's C code is then compiled against
the
PvSnesLib SDK
toolchain to create a working rom.
Due to the limitations of the SNES, it is not always possible to write idiomatic C# for a working rom. For example:
Minimal
System
level type support
No dynamic allocations are supported (thus no reference type support)
Minimizing variables on the stack is important
Pointer/address tracking is common to save memory
Even with these limitations, it is still possible to create real SNES games, though there might be instances where
it may be necessary to go to a lower level than C# supports.
Note:
The dntc transpiler has its own limitations on what MSIL operations it supports and doesn't yet support, so
it's possible to hit code that should work but the transpiler does not yet have support for.
Getting Started
There are several things to be aware of before getting started
The PVSnesLib SDK works best under Linux. If developing on windows, you'll want to do the final compilation of the
SNES rom under WSL, but obviously you can use windows emulators to test the resulting rom.
This repository should be cloned using
ssh
credentials. This is because all submodules (and submodules within
submodules) are using
git@
addresses and I have not yet figured out a good way to allow them to be mixed. See the
Github SSH key docs
for help.
Make sure to do a full recursive submodule update after cloning (e.g.
git submodule update --init --recursive
)
Dependencies needed to install on WSL Ubuntu for make
export PVSNESLIB_HOME=(yourpath)/DotnetSnes/pvsneslib
sudo apt-get update
(if needed)
sudo apt-get install cmake
sudo apt-get install g++
sudo apt-get install dotnet-sdk-8.0
Preparing the Repo and SDKs
Clone the DotnetSnes repository
Do a recursive submodule initialization on the clone to get dependent projects
git submodule update --init --recursive
cd
into the
pvsneslib/
directory and run
make
This will make sure the pvsneslib toolchain is now built
Hello World Example
The Hello World is a basic example that shows a bare minimum SNES rom that prints text to the screen.
cd
into
src/DotnetSnes.Example.HellowWorld/
run
make
You should see
Build finished successfully !
and a
HelloWorld.sfc
should now exist in your
bin/Release/net8.0
folder. This is your SNES rom that you can load into an emulator, or save to flash cart.
LikeMario Game Example
mario.mp4
This is a C# port of the
PVSnesLib LikeMario example
, which
demonstrates how to manage objects, tmx tile maps, audio, and game pad input.
Important classes are:
Globals.cs
contains assembly labels for where content exists in the
baked in rom.
Game.cs
contains the logic for initializing the game
Mario.cs
contains the logic for showing and controlling the mario object
To build:
cd
into [src/DotnetSnes.Example.LikeMario]
run 'make'
The
LikeMario.sfc
rom file should now exist in the
bin/Release/net8.0
folder.
Creating a New Project
To start a brand-new project:
Create a new .net class library project
Reference the
DotnetSnes.Core
library
This provides core functionality needed by SNES roms
Reference the
Dntc.Attributes
library
This provides pretty important attributes thatare useful for the transpilation process
Create a
public static int Main()
function declaration to declare your rom's entry point
Add the
[CustomFunctionName("main")]
attribute to your
Main()
function, to force it to have
main
as the
function name after transpiling to C. This allows the SDK to know it's the entry point.
Create a file named
Makefile
with the following contents:
.SUFFIXES
:
SNES_NAME
?= HelloWorld
#
Replace with the name you want your rom to have
SNES_DLL ?=
$(
ARTIFACTS_ROOT
)
/DotnetSnes.Example.HelloWorld.dll
#
Replace with the DLL your csproj will generate
ARTIFACTS_ROOT ?=
$(
abspath
bin/Release/net8.0)
DNSNES_CORE_DIR
?=
$(
abspath
../DotnetSnes.Core)
#

data.title: The US has approved CRISPR pigs for food
data.author: DocFeind
data.article_summary: 美国批准了一种通过CRISPR基因编辑技术培育的猪，这些猪对猪生殖和呼吸综合征（PRRS）病毒免疫。这种病毒对猪仔是致命的，每年在美国造成约3亿美元的损失。英国公司Genus通过编辑猪胚胎，去除了PRRS病毒用于进入细胞的受体，使猪对该病毒几乎完全免疫。尽管基因编辑动物面临高成本和监管障碍，但这种猪有可能成为首个成功商业化的CRISPR食品，预计明年进入美国市场。不过，Genus还需在墨西哥、加拿大、日本和中国等主要出口市场获得批准。这项技术展示了基因编辑在预防牲畜疾病和提升农业经济效益方面的潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基因编辑猪的科学、伦理和商业影响

不同观点：
• **pazimzadeh**：认为基因编辑猪与之前的CRISPR HIV研究有相似之处，关注删除CCR5受体的长期影响。引用研究表明，基因编辑猪在健康指标和肉质上无显著差异，但有少量数据表明背部脂肪厚度增加。他还提到，实验猪在良好农场条件下无需基因编辑也能抵抗病毒，暗示农场条件的重要性。

• **nerdjon**：认为反对GMO（转基因生物）是反科学的，强调应将科学与不良商业行为区分开。他批评那些声称“非转基因”的产品，认为这些公司不关心可持续性和科学。

• **AzzyHN**：认为基因编辑技术有潜力对社会有益，但担心那些想使用这项技术的人往往不关心动物福利和潜在的人类健康副作用。

• **sinuhe69**：强烈反对将人类基因编辑实验视为“误导”，认为这是犯罪行为，并指出相关科学家因不道德行为被判入狱多年。

• **SoftTalker**：担心基因编辑猪对PRRS病毒的免疫力可能导致罕见亚型病毒成为主导，提出潜在生态风险。

• **comrade1234**：认为基因编辑技术只是为了在工厂化农场中养更多猪，质疑其伦理性和动机。

• **andsoitis**：讽刺未来可能出现“CRISPR Bacon™”，暗示商业化和品牌化的潜在趋势。

• **DesaiAshu**：提出可以停止 breeding 转基因动物，直接合成蛋白质，质疑为何继续使用动物。

• **stavros**：建议不将猪限制在狭小空间，引用视频说明不大幅增加成本也能确保动物福利。

• **walterbell**：关注如何测试零售猪肉中是否存在被编辑的受体，并提出测试流程的复杂性和成本问题。

• **pgryko**：幽默提及基因编辑猪与游戏“The Outer Worlds”中的虚构生物相似。

• **unfitted2545**：表示作为素食者感到高兴，质疑基因编辑动物的伦理问题。

43879288.article_content:
Most pigs in the US are confined to factory farms where they can be afflicted by a nasty respiratory virus that kills piglets. The illness is called porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome, or PRRS.
A few years ago, a British company called Genus
set out to design pigs immune to this germ using CRISPR
gene editing. Not only did they succeed, but its pigs are now poised to enter the food chain following approval of the animals this week by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
The pigs will join a very
short list of gene-modified animals that you can eat.
It’s a short list because such animals are expensive to create, face regulatory barriers, and don’t always pay off. For instance, the US took about 20 years to approve a transgenic salmon with an extra gene that let it grow faster. But by early this year its creator, AquaBounty, had sold off all its fish farms and had only four employees—none of them selling fish.
Regulations have eased since then, especially around gene editing, which tinkers with an animal’s own DNA rather than adding to it from another species, as is the case with the salmon and many GMO crops.
Related Story
Jurassic Patent: How Colossal Biosciences is attempting to own the “woolly mammoth”
The company claiming it can restore lost species also wants to patent them.
What’s certain is that the pig project was technically impressive and scientifically clever. Genus edited pig embryos to remove the receptor that the PRRS virus uses to enter cells. No receptor means no infection.
According to Matt Culbertson, chief operating office of the Pig Improvement Company, a Genus subsidiary, the pigs appear entirely immune to more than 99% of the known versions of the PRRS virus, although there is one rare subtype that may break through the protection.
This project is scientifically similar to the work that led to
the infamous CRISPR babies
born in China in 2018. In that case a scientist named He Jiankui edited twin girls to be resistant to HIV, also by trying to remove a receptor gene when they were just embryos in a dish.
That experiment on humans was widely decried as misguided. But pigs are a different story. The ethical concerns about experimenting are less serious, and the benefits of changing the genomes can be measured in dollars and cents. It’s going to save a lot of money if pigs are immune to the PRRS virus, which spreads quite easily, causing losses of $300 million a year or more in the US alone.
Globally, people get animal protein mostly from chickens, with pigs and cattle in second and third place. A
2023 report
estimated that pigs account for 34% of all meat that’s eaten. Of the billion pigs in the world, about half are in China; the US comes in a distant second, with 80 million.
Recently, there’s been a lot of fairly silly news about genetically modified animals. A company called Colossal Biosciences used gene editing to modify wolves in ways it claimed made them resemble an extinct species, the
dire wolf
. And then there’s the L.A. Project, an effort run by biohackers who say they’ll make
glow-in-the-dark rabbits
and have a stretch goal of creating a horse with a horn—that’s right, a unicorn.
Both those projects are more about showmanship than usefulness. But they’re demonstrations of the growing power scientists have to modify mammals, thanks principally to new gene-editing tools combined with DNA sequencing that lets them peer into animals’ DNA.
Related Story
Gene editing has made pigs immune to a deadly epidemic
A large project is underway to disease-proof pigs using CRISPR to change their DNA. Are people next?
Stopping viruses is a much better use of CRISPR. And research is ongoing to make pigs—as well as other livestock—invulnerable to other infections, including African swine fever and influenza. While PRRS doesn’t infect humans, pig and bird flus can. But if herds and flocks could be changed to resist those infections, that could cut the chances of the type of spillover that can occasionally cause dangerous pandemics.
There’s a chance the Genus pigs could turn out to be the most financially valuable genetically modified animal ever created—the first CRISPR hit product to reach the food system. After the approval, the company’s stock value jumped up by a couple of hundred million dollars on the London Stock Exchange.
But there is still a way to go before gene-edited bacon appears on shelves in the US. Before it makes its sales pitch to pig farms, Genus says, it needs to also gain approval in Mexico, Canada, Japan and China which are big export markets for American pork.
Culbertson says gene-edited pork could appear in the US market sometime next year. He says the company does not think pork chops or other meat will need to carry any label identifying it as bioengineered. "We aren't aware of any labelling requirement," Culbertson says.
This article is from The Checkup,
MIT Technology Review

data.title: Your ViT Is Secretly an Image Segmentation Model
data.author: lamename
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了Vision Transformers（ViTs）在图像分割任务中的潜力，提出无需额外的卷积适配器或像素解码器，仅通过足够大的模型和预训练，ViTs自身可以学习到多尺度特征表示。基于此发现，作者引入了一种仅编码器的掩码Transformer（EoMT），该模型通过简单架构实现了与当前最优方法相当的分割精度，且速度显著提升，如ViT-L可快4倍。实验表明，EoMT在分割精度与预测速度之间达到了较优平衡，证明了扩展ViT本身比增加架构复杂性更有效。

Title:
Your ViT is Secretly an Image Segmentation Model
Authors:
Tommie Kerssies
,
Niccolò Cavagnero
,
Alexander Hermans
,
Narges Norouzi
,
Giuseppe Averta
,
Bastian Leibe
,
Gijs Dubbelman
,
Daan de Geus
View a PDF of the paper titled Your ViT is Secretly an Image Segmentation Model, by Tommie Kerssies and 7 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
Vision Transformers (ViTs) have shown remarkable performance and scalability across various computer vision tasks. To apply single-scale ViTs to image segmentation, existing methods adopt a convolutional adapter to generate multi-scale features, a pixel decoder to fuse these features, and a Transformer decoder that uses the fused features to make predictions. In this paper, we show that the inductive biases introduced by these task-specific components can instead be learned by the ViT itself, given sufficiently large models and extensive pre-training. Based on these findings, we introduce the Encoder-only Mask Transformer (EoMT), which repurposes the plain ViT architecture to conduct image segmentation. With large-scale models and pre-training, EoMT obtains a segmentation accuracy similar to state-of-the-art models that use task-specific components. At the same time, EoMT is significantly faster than these methods due to its architectural simplicity, e.g., up to 4x faster with ViT-L. Across a range of model sizes, EoMT demonstrates an optimal balance between segmentation accuracy and prediction speed, suggesting that compute resources are better spent on scaling the ViT itself rather than adding architectural complexity. data.article_summary: 《Commodore 64的诞生：工程师的故事》讲述了这款历史上最畅销电脑的研发过程。1981年1月，MOS Technology的工程师们开始设计图形和声音芯片，最初目标是用于高级电子游戏。然而，在1982年1月拉斯维加斯的消费电子展上，这些芯片被集成到了一台全新的家用电脑——Commodore 64中，售价仅595美元，远低于市场预期。这台电脑拥有64KB内存，超越了当时16KB或32KB的标准配置。工程师们在极短时间内完成了原型设计和生产，并在展会上获得热烈反响。尽管面临质量控制和缓慢磁盘驱动器的批评，Commodore 64凭借其高性价比和强大的图形、声音性能，成功占据市场主导地位，迫使许多竞争对手退出。

43840057.article_content:
History of Technology
Feature
Creating the Commodore 64: The Engineers’ Story
The daring and design that went into the best-selling computer of all time
Tekla S. Perry
Paul Wallich
01 Mar 1985
31 min read
Evan Amos
In January 1981,
a handful of semiconductor engineers at MOS Technology in West Chester, Pa., a subsidiary of
Commodore International Ltd.
, began designing a graphics chip and a sound chip to sell to whoever wanted to make “the world’s best video game.” In January 1982, a home computer incorporating those chips was introduced at the Winter
Consumer Electronics
Show in
Las Vegas
, Nev. By using in-house integrated-circuit-fabrication facilities for prototyping, the engineers had cut the design time for each chip to less than nine months, and they had designed and built five prototype computers for the show in less than five weeks. What surprised the rest of the home-computer industry most, however, was the introductory price of the
Commodore
64: $595 for a unit incorporating a keyboard, a central processor, the graphics and sound chips, and 64 kilobytes of memory instead of the 16 or 32 that were then considered the norm.
When the chip-development project started, the Commodore 64 was not at all what the designers had in mind. MOS Technology was a merchant semiconductor house. Its LSI Group, headed at that time by Albert Charpentier, had been responsible for some of the chips that went into Commodore’s VIC-20 home computer, but that project was already well into production. “We were fresh out of ideas for whatever chips the rest of the world might want us to do,” said Charpentier, “So we decided to produce state-of-the-art video and sound chips for the world’s next great video game.”
This article was first published as “Design case history: the Commodore 64.” It appeared in the March 1985 issue of
IEEE Spectrum
.
A
PDF version
is available on
IEEE Xplore
. The diagrams and photographs of chips, circuit boards, and screens appeared in the original print version.
Charles Winterble, then director of worldwide engineering for Commodore, gave the go-ahead for the chip effort, and Charpentier’s group worked fairly independently until both chips were finished in mid-November 1981.
At a meeting with Charpentier and Winterble late that month, Jack Tramiel, then president of Commodore, decided not to proceed with the video game. Instead, he decided, the chips would go into a 64-kilobyte home computer to be introduced at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas the second week of January 1982. The computer had yet to be designed, but that was easily remedied.
In two days, the engineers laid out on paper the machine’s basic architecture. Just before the new year, they completed five working prototypes. In the meantime, enough operating-system software was copied and rewritten from the VIC-20 to give passable demonstrations of what the new machine could do. Following its enthusiastic reception at the Consumer Electronics Show, the Commodore 64 was rushed into production; volume shipments began in August 1982 and have continued unabated.
Despite complaints about quality control and the industry’s slowest disk drive, the Commodore 64 has been an unparalleled success, pushing a number of its competitors out of the market. Part of the reason for its success is the price, which keeps falling—from $595 at its introduction to $149 currently, for which the consumer gets graphics and sound equal to or better than that provided by machines that cost five times as much.
Designing the next great chips
In the late 1970s, MOS Technology was a successful semiconductor company; its engineers had designed the popular
6502
microprocessor, and it manufactured several other solidly selling products. Commodore, a West Coast company at the time, took over MOS in 1976—causing many of the MOS engineers to quit when their stock was bought at 10 cents on the dollar—but MOS was allowed to operate fairly autonomously.
In 1979 and 1980, recalls Charpentier, MOS Technology developed the 6510 microprocessor—a minor revision of the 6502 with an additional input-output port, the 6526 peripheral controller, a lot of read-only memory (ROM) chips, and a 4-kilobit random-access memory (RAM) chip. At that time, MOS was supplying equipment to
Atari Inc.
,
General Electric Co
.,
Hewlett-Packard Co
., and a number of other clients, as well as to Commodore.
​Defining terms
Bit map
A display system in which each dot on the screen is controlled by the value of a particular bit in
computer memory
. Multiple bits per dot permit multiple colors and shading.
Character map
A display system in which a group of dots on the screen are defined by a single word in computer memory that points to a miniature bit map containing the values for each dot. Because many patterns are reused on a typical screen, character maps use less memory than bit maps.
Color clock
The frequency of the carrier signal used to transmit color information in the National
Television
Syst

主要讨论点：Rethink DNS的实现方式及其性能表现，以及其他替代方案的讨论

不同观点：
• [对Rethink DNS性能的质疑] maxloh 对Rethink DNS服务器使用JavaScript实现表示怀疑，认为JavaScript作为性能关键的DNS服务器语言不够理想。他通过基准测试发现Rethink DNS的响应时间在400-500ms，而Cloudflare只需要5-10ms，因此选择了AdAway作为替代方案。

• [对Rethink DNS的兴趣与支持] chrisweekly 对Rethink DNS表示了一定的兴趣，特别是将其与Pi-hole进行类比，并提到Bunny.net作为另一个CDN和云服务提供商，具有可编程DNS的功能。

• [提出dnsdist作为替代方案] karel-3d 提供了dnsdist作为另一种选择，指出它是一个高效的DNS负载均衡器，同时也可以作为stub resolver，支持DoH/DoT，并且资源消耗低。他认为dnsdist的这种用途没有被广泛讨论。

• [对Rethink DNS项目活力的担忧] Onavo 对Rethink DNS移动应用多年未发布新版本表示担忧，并在GitHub上询问项目是否仍然活跃。

补充讨论：
• maxloh 提供了具体的基准测试数据来支持其对Rethink DNS性能的质疑，特别是与Cloudflare的对比，显示出显著的性能差异。
• chrisweekly 提到了Bunny.net作为一个新的CDN和服务提供商，扩展了讨论范围，增加了对其他类似服务的兴趣。
• karel-3d 提供了技术细节，强调dnsdist的优点，并指出其作为stub resolver的潜力，尽管其这种用途未被广泛讨论。
• Onavo 提出了对Rethink DNS项目持续发展的关注，质疑其是否仍然在积极维护和开发。

争议焦点：Rethink DNS使用JavaScript实现的性能是否足够好，以及其项目是否仍然活跃。

data.title: AWS Built a Security Tool. It Introduced a Security Risk
data.author: simplesort
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了AWS的一个安全工具“Account Assessment for AWS Organizations”意外引入了跨账户权限提升的风险。该工具旨在审核基于资源的跨账户访问，但由于部署指南不够明确，导致用户在不安全的账户中部署，从而造成安全隐患。具体来说，AWS建议将枢纽角色部署在除管理账户外的任何账户中，这可能让低安全性的账户获得对高敏感账户的访问权限。这种配置可能被攻击者利用，通过开发账户中的角色获取生产和管理工作中的敏感数据和权限。AWS之后修复了该问题，并建议受影响的组织检测和修复不安全的配置。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AWS环境中关于元数据列举是否构成安全风险及其严重性

不同观点：
• yfiapo：承认这是一个安全问题，但认为其严重性中等。信息泄露需要结合其他问题才能提升权限，单独存在并不构成威胁。问题在于AWS文档未明确建议用户遵循最佳实践，而非AWS推荐或自动设置不安全环境。过度炒作小问题无助于解决问题。
   
• placardloop：认为列举元数据不构成安全问题。List* API与Get* API不同，仅提供元数据而不涉及对象本身。如果元数据中包含敏感信息，则是更大的问题。

• abhisek：IAM系统复杂，尤其是联合与跨账户信任。并非每个弱点都是漏洞，未找到此问题构成漏洞的威胁模型。

• dangus：比较AWS与GCP，认为GCP的文件夹和项目系统更灵活，IAM控制更好。AWS的多账户系统需要改进。

• MikeIndyson：是否存储敏感数据在元数据中取决于实现方式，不应将敏感数据存储在元数据中。

• swisniewski：认为文章夸大其词。AWS模型简单，多账户间完全独立，只有明确配置才能跨账户访问。AWS无需提醒用户确保账户安全，称之为重大安全风险是错误的。元数据列举不构成信息泄露漏洞，影响很小。

补充讨论：
• bulatb：批评文章标题简短吸引点击，反映出当前博客的趋势。
• ahoka：讽刺性地提到链接被公司安全套件阻止。

争议焦点：
• 该问题是否构成重大安全风险，或仅仅是小问题被过度炒作。
• 元数据列举是否构成安全问题，特别是在已有开发访问权限的情况下。

43893906.article_content:
Blog
Apr 28, 2025 | 7 min
AWS Built a Security Tool. It Introduced a Security Risk.
Eliav Livneh
Security Researcher
(If you missed the previous parts of this trust policy blog series, we recommend reading parts
one
and
two
first)
In the previous post of this series, we explored four dangerous misconceptions regarding how to securely set up cross-account access in AWS environments.
In this final post of the series, weâll walk through a real-world case where even AWS got it wrong. Their
Account Assessment for AWS Organizations
tool, designed to audit resource-based policies for risky cross-account access, ironically introduced cross-account privilege escalation risks due to flawed deployment instructions. Specifically, customers were effectively encouraged to deploy the tool in lower-sensitivity accounts, creating risky trust paths from insecure environments into highly sensitive ones.
Weâll share how we discovered the issue, the risks it introduced, how AWS fixed it, and what affected organizations should do to detect and remediate it.
How it started
While investigating a critical privilege escalation risk involving an IAM role in a customerâs AWS environment, we discovered a role present in both their production and management accounts, each of which trusted two roles in their development account:
The risky IAM role we investigated
These were the details of the privilege escalation risk (sensitive info redacted):
Examining the permissions of that role in the production and management accounts, we found it had access to several sensitive IAM and data-related API calls, including:
iam:ListRoles
(lists all IAM roles, helping an attacker identify privileged and vulnerable roles)
iam:ListPolicies
(reveals all IAM policies, exposing potential misconfigurations)
secretsmanager:ListSecrets
(lists all stored secret names, identifying potential targets)
s3:ListAllMyBuckets
(enumerates all S3 buckets, exposing potential sensitive data locations)
kms:ListKeys
(lists all encryption keys, indicating what is being encrypted)
kms:GetKeyPolicy
(retrieves key policies, which could reveal weak or misconfigured access controls)
â¦ and more (full policy
here
)
These permissions were granted on all resources (
resource: "*"
), making them particularly dangerous if compromised.
The organization's dev account had weaker security, making this role assumption path a major risk. An attacker compromising a trusted role in dev could immediately gain these permissions in production and management. Combined with other misconfigurations - such as exposed IAM roles, secret names, KMS keys, or public S3 buckets - this could help lead to compromise of the organization's most sensitive accounts.
This was already a serious risk, but what we found next revealed that this misconfiguration was not unique to this organization - it was actually inadvertently encouraged by AWS itself.
Account Assessment for AWS Organizations
The names of these roles were somewhat quirky, and hinted they were part of some automated system. A quick search led us to
Account Assessment for AWS Organizations
, a tool developed by AWS and published in the
AWS Solutions Library
.
According to its official documentation, the tool is designed to âcentrally evaluate and manage AWS accounts within your AWS Organizationsâ, helping users better understand account dependencies. AWS lists its
primary use cases
as mergers and acquisitions, security audits, centralized policy explorer and management account transitions.
So, why was it deployed insecurely?
Given that this tool was built by AWS to audit resource-based cross-account access, we initially assumed the misconfiguration was a deployment error by the customer. However, after reviewing the documentation, we realized that AWSâs deployment instructions unintentionally encouraged insecure setups, making it highly likely that users would deploy the tool in a way that introduced privilege escalation risks.
The tool follows a hub-and-spoke architecture:
A hub role is deployed in a designated hub account.
Spoke roles are deployed in all other accounts to be assessed, trusting the hub role for access.
This design allows the hub role to assume the spoke roles across all accounts, aggregating security data across the organization.
When checking AWS's official deployment guidance, we were surprised to see the following instruction:
"Hub stack - Deploy to any member account in your AWS Organization except the Organizations management account."
This is the root cause of the issue - AWS explicitly recommended not deploying the hub in the management account, without clarifying the security implications of the other possible choices.
Why this is a major security risk
Letâs back up a bit and explain why this instruction, without any clarification, was so problematic.
As we covered in the
previous blog
, allowing a role in a less secure account to assume roles in more sensitive accounts creates a privilege escalation risk.
By d

data.author: qzervaas
data.article_summary: Daft Punk广泛使用多种声乐效果器，包括Roland SVC-350、Auto-Tune、DigiTech Vocalist和Talker，以及Sennheiser VSM201等。根据专辑和歌曲的不同，使用的效果器也有所变化。在《Homework》中，主要使用Roland SVC-350和Ensoniq DP/4+进行音高变换。在《Discovery》中，出现了Auto-Tune和DigiTech Vocalist，而《Human After All》则大量使用DigiTech Talker。在《Random Access Memories》中，Sennheiser VSM201成为主要效果器，同时也有Talk Box和Auto-Tune的应用。Daft Punk的声效可以大致分为Talk Box、声码器和和声器三类，每种技术产生不同的机器人声效果。尽管效果相似，但它们基于不同的技术和设备。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一篇关于Daft Punk音乐设备研究文章的评价及相关设备讨论

不同观点：
• [madeofpalk] 认为文章是一次巨大的努力，包含了大量不为人知的信息。他提到为了撰写文章进行了多年研究，购买了约25件音乐设备，并通过联系Imogen Heap的团队确认了具体设备的使用情况。
• [smjburton] 对文章中的设备进行了具体评价，特别提到Sennheiser VSM201的音质非常干净，喜欢其模拟声音，并认为Digitech Studio Vocalist EX在和声器中音质最佳，同时也喜欢Korg ih Interactive Vocal Harmony的空间声效。
• [jedimastert] 感叹Daft Punk仅凭四张录音室专辑就产生了巨大影响。
• [amelius] 最初以为文章是关于非凡的歌唱技巧，虽然预期不同，但仍认为文章不错。
• [Isamu] 赞赏文章的深度，表示希望能够更多地支持这样高质量的内容。
• [LuciOfStars] 表达了对Daft Punk的简单喜爱，见到相关内容就会支持。

补充讨论：
• [throw_m239339] 指出文章未提及Roland VP 9000，暗示可能有设备遗漏。
• [tecleandor] 对Sennheiser VSM201进行了补充说明，指出其价格昂贵（发布时约25,000美元）且销量极少（不到50台），但认为如果资金充裕可以获得类似效果的 cheaper 设备。

争议焦点：
• 文章是否全面覆盖了所有相关设备，特别是Roland VP 9000的缺失引发了讨论。

43893601.article_content:
The vocal effects of Daft Punk
Daft Punk have used a wide variety of vocal effects in their songs. A May 2001 interview in Remix magazine provided a rare insight from Daft Punk themselves on the topic.
âPeople always ask us what vocoder we use, but every one of our vocal tracks uses a different vocoder effect. We have the old Roland one [an SVC-350], Auto-Tune, and a DigiTech Vocalist.â
The quote delivers some vital clues, but itâs incomplete, covering only their first two albums. Thereâs no mention of using a talk box, despite Around The World almost certainly using one. The quote makes it sound like the DigiTech Vocalist is a vocoder, but itâs not. And for that matter, which DigiTech Vocalist model? Thereâs around 30 pieces of hardware in DigiTechâs Vocalist series, and quite a few of them were around before Discoveryâs release in 2001.
Iâve read comments suggesting the DigiTech Vocalist models with the âEXâ suffix are special, but nobody seems to know why, and nobody has published a direct comparison to prove or disprove the theory. I decided to take on the challenge, and run the tests myself. Hereâs a fraction of the Vocalist units I ended up buying.
Why are there duplicates of the same model? Why is there a Korg ih in that photo? Before this article gets sidetracked with tests and some honestly quite interesting corporate partnerships, mergers, and lawsuits, here is a list of every Daft Punk album song containing robot-like vocal effects, and my guess on which piece of kit was used for the vocals.

Homework notes (20 January 1997)
#
There arenât many robot vocal effects on Homework, but there is a lot of pitch shifting, likely provided by Daft Punkâs Ensoniq DP/4+, a digital multi-effects units that can do a variety of things. I donât believe Daft Punk used the vocoder on the Ensoniq DP/4+ for Homework or any of their other albums. The Remix magazine quote says Ensoniq DP/4, but a
gear list in another interview
says DP/4+. It doesnât matter which model was used, as the pitch shifting and vocoder sound the same on both units.
Discovery notes (12 March 2001)
#
One More Time sounds like Auto-Tune in combination with a Mu-Tron Phasor or Moogerfooger. Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger uses a DigiTech Talker vocoder. Given the DigiTech Talker was used extensively for Human After All, maybe it was one of the last songs recorded for Discovery? The DigiTech Talker wasnât mentioned in the May 2001 interview, despite its use on Discovery.
Human After All notes (14 March 2005)
#
DigiTech Talker and DigiTech Synth Wah are all over the entire album. But, did they use a DigiTech Synth Wah, or DigiTech Bass Synth Wah? Theyâre very similar pedals. The tremolo effect on The Brainwasher could have been done many ways. Maybe it was just an LFO modulating the amplitude on their Roland S-760 sampler? Maybe it was a guitar pedal? Itâs an easy effect that can be achieved many different ways.
Random Access Memories notes (17 May 2013)
#
In Lose Yourself To Dance, the âeverybodyâs dancing on the floorâ vocals sound very crunchy and DigiTech Talker-like. The vocodeded vocals in Touch sound like a Sennheiser VSM201 switched to unvoiced, or using white noise as the vocoderâs carrier. Instant Crush could be Auto-Tune or some other kind of harmoniser. It sounds like Instant Crush constains some Sennheiser VSM201 chord layers in places.
Talk boxes
#
Daft Punkâs vocal effects can be broadly split into three categories: Talk boxes, vocoders, and harmonisers. They all sound vaguely similar and robot-like, and you could be forgiven for confusing them, but theyâre extremely different techniques and technologies.
