data.title: Trump announces 100% tariffs on movies ‘produced in foreign lands’
data.author: limbicsystem
data.article_summary: 2025年5月，唐纳德·特朗普宣布对所有“外国制作”的电影征收100%关税，称外国激励措施导致美国电影业快速衰退，构成“国家安全威胁”和“宣传”。他指示商务部立即实施该关税。此举引发国际反应，澳大利亚和新西兰表示将保护本国电影业。专家警告，此关税可能引发报复，损害美国电影业。此前，特朗普对华发起贸易战，中国已减少美国电影进口配额，进一步影响好莱坞。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对“MAGA支持者攻击好莱坞”的评论及相关争议

不同观点：
• **habosa的观点**：认为好莱坞在全球推广美国文化，具有政府无法实现的影响力，威胁好莱坞是愚蠢的行为，因为好莱坞为美国带来了巨大的文化优势。
  
• **jaimebuelta的观点**：质疑好莱坞项目的“美国属性”，指出像《Deadpool & Wolverine》这样的电影主要在英国拍摄，主演也不是美国人，质疑是否要为此类电影支付双倍票价或聚焦国际市场。

• **pluc的观点**：将攻击好莱坞与“美国优先”政策联系起来，认为这是在文化教育领域进行削减，最终目的是通过宣传控制民众思想，且目前没有强有力的反对。

• **mk89的观点**：以讽刺口吻提到如果好莱坞项目转移到美国国内拍摄可能产生的荒谬结果，如在乔治亚州拍摄《罗马》或在大峡谷拍摄《指环王》。

• **d3nj4l的观点**：认为讨论中很多观点没有实质内容，质疑如何对电影征税及其实施细节，认为人们过度解读。

• **Ekaros的观点**：指出对好莱坞征税可能打击美国少数具有贸易顺差的产业之一，认为这样做是不明智的。

• **bilekas的观点**：质疑是否有实际的政策文件或只是集会上的 rant，希望了解对外国电影征税的国家安全理由。

• **xz18r的观点**：指出在美国以外的国家，几乎所有听到的电影都是美国的，质疑反对MAGA的人说“美国从未伟大”的同时，又声称“电影从未离开美国”。

• **victorbjorklund的观点**：认为欧盟政治家可能会利用这个机会支持欧洲电影产业。

• **perihelions的观点**：从法律角度质疑美国是否可以通过宪法第一修正案对媒体征税，并探讨禁止媒体的宪法界限。

• **trebligdivad的观点**：以讽刺口吻预测未来可能要求《Wallace & Gromit》采用美国幽默。

• **drooopy的观点**：以讽刺方式预测未来可能出现更荒谬的政策，如要求用Gatorade浇灌作物。

• **codingbot3000的观点**：关注特朗普在Truth Social上的帖子获得的点赞数很少，质疑为何没有更多的互动。

• **jpambrun的观点**：质疑如何对电影征税，猜测Netflix可能会根据观看量被收费，并预测其他国家会进行报复，导致美国电影制作成本增加和海外被征税，可能引发盗版增加。

• **steveBK123的观点**：以讽刺口吻指出有人可能因为Netflix上太多字幕电影而生气。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及了好莱坞在全球文化传播中的重要性及其经济影响。
- 对电影征税的具体实施细节和法律问题是另一个讨论重点。
- 有人质疑这种政策是否会适得其反，导致美国电影产业受损。
- 讽刺和幽默被广泛用于表达对政策的不满和预测可能出现的荒谬结果。
- 讨论中还涉及了国际市场的反应及可能的经济后果。

43893310.article_content:
1:04
Donald Trump announces tariff on movies from 'other nations'  – video
Donald Trump
Trump announces 100% tariffs on movies ‘produced in foreign lands’
President calls films ‘national security threat’ and claims he called on commerce department to immediately enact tariff
Guardian staff and agencies
Sun 4 May 2025 19.54 EDT
Last modified on Mon 5 May 2025 08.21 EDT
Share
Donald Trump
on Sunday announced on his Truth Social platform a 100%
tariff
on all movies “produced in Foreign Lands”, saying the US film industry was dying a “very fast death” due to the incentives that other countries were offering to draw American film-makers.
In his post, he claimed to have authorised the commerce department and the US trade representative to immediately begin instituting such a tariff.
“This is a concerted effort by other Nations and, therefore, a National Security threat,” Trump said in
the Truth Social post
. “It is, in addition to everything else, messaging and propaganda!
“WE WANT MOVIES MADE IN AMERICA, AGAIN!” Trump added.
Republicans in Congress pull out all the stops to protect Trump tariffs
Read more
The commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, posting on X said: “We’re on it.” Neither Lutnick nor Trump provided any details on the implementation. It was not immediately clear whether the move would target production companies, foreign or American, producing films overseas.
Film and television production in Los Angeles has fallen by nearly 40% over the last decade, according to FilmLA, a non-profit that tracks the region’s production. At the same time, governments around the world have offered more generous tax credits and cash rebates to lure productions, and capture a greater share of the $248bn that Ampere Analysis predicts will be spent globally in 2025 to produce content.
Politicians in Australia and New Zealand said on Monday they would advocate for their respective film industries, after the president’s announcement.
Australia’s home affairs minister, Tony Burke, said he had spoken to the head of the government body Screen Australia about the proposed tariffs. “Nobody should be under any doubt that we will be standing up unequivocally for the rights of the Australian screen industry,” he said in a statement.
‘It feels empty’: is Hollywood film and TV production in a death spiral?
Read more
New Zealand’s prime minister, Christopher Luxon, told a news conference the government was awaiting further detail of the proposed tariffs. “We’ll have to see the detail of what actually ultimately emerges. But we’ll be obviously a great advocate, great champion of that sector in that industry,” he said.
The announcement from Trump comes after he triggered a trade war with China, and imposed global tariffs which have roiled markets and led to fears of a US recession. The film industry has already been feeling the effects of the tariffs, as China in April responded to the announcements by
reducing the quota
of American movies allowed into that country.
China is the world’s second largest film market after the US, although in recent years domestic offerings have outshone Hollywood imports.
A former senior commerce department official, William Reinsch, a senior fellow with the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said retaliation against Trump’s foreign movies tariffs would be devastating.
“The retaliation will kill our industry. We have a lot more to lose than to gain,” he said, adding that it would be difficult to make a national security or national emergency case for movies.

data.title: Effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on sleep bruxism
data.author: amelius
data.article_summary: 这篇研究探讨了重复经颅磁刺激（rTMS）对睡眠磨牙症（SB）患者的短期影响。12名SB患者参与了一项开放性、单次干预的试点研究。研究对患者双侧初级运动皮层中的咬肌代表区施加1 Hz、80%活动运动阈值强度的rTMS，每天每侧20分钟，连续5天。使用便携式肌电图（EMG）记录仪测量患者睡眠期间 jaw-closing 肌肉的EMG活动，并通过0-10数字评分量表（NRS）评估肌肉酸痛。结果显示，rTMS期间及之后，EMG活动强度和NRS酸痛评分均显著低于基线水平（P值分别为0.04、0.02和<0.01）。研究表明，rTMS可显著抑制睡眠期间的 jaw-closing 肌肉活动，并减轻肌肉酸痛，提示rTMS对磨牙症具有潜在治疗效果，但需进一步开展更严格的对照研究。

Abstract
The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) on patients with sleep bruxism (SB). Twelve patients with SB were included in an open, single-intervention pilot study. rTMS at 1 Hz and an intensity of 80% of the active motor threshold was applied to the ‘hot spot' of the masseter muscle representation at the primary motor cortex bilaterally for 20 min per side each day for 5 consecutive days. The jaw-closing muscle electromyographic (EMG) activity during sleep was recorded with a portable EMG recorder at baseline, during rTMS treatment and at follow-up for 5 days. In addition, patients scored their jaw-closing muscle soreness on a 0–10 numerical rating scale (NRS). Data were analysed with analysis of variance. The intensity of the EMG activity was suppressed during and after rTMS compared to the baseline (
P
= 0.04;
P
= 0.02, respectively). The NRS score of soreness decreased significantly during and after rTMS compared with baseline (
P
< 0.01). These findings indicated a significant inhibition of jaw-closing muscle activity during sleep along with a decrease of muscle soreness. This pilot study raises the possibility of therapeutic benefits from rTMS in patients with bruxism and calls for further and more controlled studies.
Keywords:
behavioural science, brain function, electromyography, orofacial pain,

data.title: Show HN: CodeCafé – A real-time collaborative code editor in the browser
data.author: mrktsm__
data.article_summary: CodeCafé是一个基于浏览器的实时协作代码编辑器，专为高效团队编程设计。它支持多人同时编辑代码，具备像素完美的实时预览功能，并使用Operational Transformation技术解决编辑冲突。编辑器提供类似VS Code的开发体验，包括语法高亮、智能提示和错误检查。前端采用React和TypeScript，后端使用Java Spring Boot，通过WebSocket和Redis实现实时协作。主要功能包括零设置、即刻编码，以及未来计划添加的用户认证、项目持久化、语音/文本聊天等。项目基于AGPL-3.0许可证开源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个新发布项目的功能、改进建议及其技术选择的讨论

不同观点：
• jasonjmcghee：赞赏项目，提到在VSCode中分享代码不需要账户，并且可以在浏览器中完成基础操作。不过执行代码是另一回事，认为Replit在执行代码上更好，但其免费版资源受限。
• nanna：表达对在Emacs中实现类似功能的期望。
• omneity：祝贺项目发布，并建议在页面加载时自动生成唯一的URL，以增强用户体验和使用信心。同时提出该工具可以用于与编码代理更好地协作，提出“与我结对”的概念，区别于传统的“为我编码”。
• tpae：质疑为什么没有使用CDRT（如yjs）技术，认为这可以简化代码库。

• 技术实现上的讨论，特别是tpae提出的CDRT（如yjs）是否更适合这个项目。
• 关于用户体验的改进建议，如omneity提到的自动生成URL，提升用户信心和操作便捷性。

• tpae对技术选择的质疑，是否使用CDRT如yjs会更简化代码库，这涉及到项目技术架构的合理性和优化空间。

CodeCafé: Code Together, Instantly.
A hyper-collaborative, real-time development environment right in your browser. CodeCafé makes pair programming, teaching, and building web projects together as fluid and instant as sharing a thought.
Try CodeCafé Live!
Click here to watch the demo video!
Why CodeCafé?
We saw coding classes juggling tools built for essays, not engineers. Existing solutions felt clunky for the dynamic nature of real-time programming. CodeCafé was born from the need for a seamless, browser-based coding space designed from the ground up for
true
collaboration. Learn, teach, and build—together, instantly.
Core Features
Pixel-Perfect Live Preview:
See your HTML, CSS, and JavaScript changes render
instantly
in an integrated Web View. What you code is what you see!
True Real-Time Collaboration:
Powered by Operational Transformation, multiple users can type in the same files simultaneously, with conflicts resolved seamlessly.
VS Code Feel:
Enjoy a familiar, rich editing experience (via Monaco Editor) with syntax highlighting, smart suggestions, and error checking.
Zero Setup:
Dive straight into coding. Everything runs in the browser.
Tech Stack
Frontend:
React, TypeScript, Zustand (State Management), Tailwind CSS, Monaco Editor, Xterm.js (Integrated Terminal), Framer Motion, Axios, WebSocket Client
Backend:
Java Spring Boot, WebSocket API, Jackson (JSON Processing)
Real-time Collaboration:
Custom Operational Transformation (OT) Implementation
State Management / Messaging:
Redis (AWS ElastiCache) utilizing Lua Scripting for atomic operations
Hosting
: AWS EC2 (Backend), Vercel (Frontend), AWS ElastiCache (Redis)
Real-Time Collaboration with Operational Transformation
At the heart of CodeCafé's seamless collaborative editing is our custom-built Operational Transformation (OT) system, implemented on both the frontend and backend.
What is Operational Transformation?
Operational Transformation is the technology that powers real-time collaborative editing in systems like Google Docs. It allows multiple users to simultaneously edit the same document by:
Transforming operations (like insertions and deletions) to preserve user intentions
Ensuring eventual consistency across all clients
Resolving conflicts automatically when users edit the same regions of text
Our implementation handles the complex synchronization challenges of collaborative editing, including:
Managing concurrent edits from multiple users
Resolving edit conflicts deterministically
Maintaining document consistency across all connected clients
Preserving intention semantics of user operations
This enables truly fluid, Google Docs-like collaboration where everyone can type simultaneously without stepping on each other's toes.
Quick Start
Prerequisites:
Git, Java JDK 17+, Maven, Node.js 18+, npm 9+, Redis Server
Setup and Run:
#
Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/mrktsm/codecafe.git
cd
codecafe
#
Start Redis (keep this running in a separate terminal or as a background service)
redis-server
&
#
Create backend config file with Redis connection
mkdir -p backend/src/main/resources
echo
"
spring.redis.host=localhost
spring.redis.port=6379
"
>
backend/src/main/resources/application.properties
#
Run the backend
cd
backend
./mvnw install
./mvnw spring-boot:run
&
#
Create frontend config and run
cd
../frontend
echo
"
VITE_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8080
"
>
.env
npm install
npm run dev
Access the app in your browser at the URL shown in terminal (typically
http://localhost:5173
).

User authentication & persistent projects
Integrated voice/text chat
Session rewind & history playback
Expanded language support & tooling

data.title: A 1903 Proposal to Preserve the Dead in Glass Cubes
data.author: ohjeez
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了美国葬礼行业对遗体保存的尝试，特别是1903年由俄裔发明家Joseph Karwowski提出的一种用玻璃封存遗体的方法。他申请了专利，描述了通过将遗体浸泡在硅酸钠中并覆盖熔融玻璃来长久保存遗体的方案。尽管这个想法未被实际应用，但当时还有其他类似尝试，如玻璃棺材，试图抵抗遗体的腐烂。文章还提到一些历史上其他保存遗体的古怪方法，如电镀遗体为雕像，以及金属棺材爆炸的事件。这些方法反映了人们对死亡腐烂的抗拒心理，尽管许多发明在实践中并不成功。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过水晶或玻璃保存尸体的方法及其相关技术与历史背景

不同观点：
• miniatureape引用了希罗多德关于马可比安人使用水晶保存尸体的记载，并提供了具体方法的描述，强调了这种技术的历史背景。
• ChrisMarshallNY提到了列宁墓的保存方法，并指出其中有许多不公开的细节，但似乎使用了标准的防腐技术。
• xattt对这种保存方法的成功与否表示怀疑，认为需要时间来验证。
• adzm推荐了康宁玻璃博物馆，并指出博物馆中有关玻璃的深度内容，将讨论引向了玻璃工艺的技术和历史。
• RajT88对尸体涂覆硅酸钠后铸入玻璃中的自然性和可行性提出质疑，并联想到恐怖电影和人体世界展览。
• dracovolans对评论中提到的“俄罗斯出生”的说法提出异议，指出相关姓氏是波兰的，而非俄罗斯的。
• dcminter讨论了现代若要实现这种保存方法可能需要的步骤，包括高剂量伽马射线灭菌和树脂铸造，并提到传统防腐方法可能仍是最佳选择。
• HPsquared将讨论与专利申请热潮联系起来，提到当时可能存在类似互联网域名抢注的现象。
• cess11提到了冈瑟·冯·哈根斯的成功案例，他使用塑化技术保存尸体，并举办了人体世界展览。
• gwern提供了相关专利的链接，并讨论了当时对无菌环境和抗菌技术的迷恋，以及这些观念如何影响了对尸体保存的想象。
• elzbardico简短地提出了使用环氧树脂作为保存方法的可能性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个历史和现代的尸体保存技术，包括埃及木乃伊制作、列宁墓的防腐技术、塑化技术等。
• 争议的焦点在于通过水晶或玻璃铸造尸体是否能达到自然和无味的效果，以及现代技术能否更好地实现这种保存方法。
• 一些评论还探讨了当时科技发展对社会想象的影响，特别是无菌环境和抗菌技术的迷恋如何影响了对尸体保存的设想。
• 评论中还涉及到不同文化和技术背景下的尸体保存方法及其效果。

Joseph Karwowski, “Method of Preserving the Dead” (Washington, D.C.: United States Patent Office, 1903) (courtesy Corning Museum of Glass)
Through embalming and sealed caskets advertised for “eternal rest,” the American funeral industry caters to our anxiety over bodily decay.
In 1903
, a Russian-born inventor in Herkimer, New York, named
Joseph Karwowski
proposed a radical way of preserving corpses: suspending them in glass cubes. Patented as a “Method of Preserving the Dead,” Karwowski provided diagrams and directions “whereby a corpse may be hermetically incased within a block of transparent glass” and thus “maintained for an indefinite period in a perfect and lifelike condition.” First the corpse would be drenched with “sodium silicate or water-glass,” and then, once dried, covered with “molten glass.”
Karwowski’s patent is on view in
Curious and Curiouser: Surprising Finds from the Rakow Library
now at the Corning Museum of Glass in Corning, New York. In a blog post for Corning called “
Glass and Death,
” glass artist Caitlin Hyde writes:
There are some interesting bits of logic to Karwowski’s plan. Water glass is used as a desiccant and to seal eggshells to extend freshness, but it’s hard to imagine that, even if perfectly sealed, the clothed body would look at all natural after being coated in the wet sodium silicate and then dried out, much less after being exposed to the elevated temperatures required to cast glass around it. Karwowski did not produce any samples of his proposed invention and, though the idea may have seemed brilliant enough to need patenting at the time, it has never caught on in practice.

A
1910 issue of
Scientific American
quipped that the intact bodies preserved in  Karwowski’s method “could be utilized as a lawn statue” while the “bodiless head could be placed on the mantle in the stead of a jar of ashes, or could be used as a heavy-weight paper weight or as a door stop.”
Image from a glass casket catalog (American Glass Casket Company, Ada, Oklahoma, around 1921) (courtesy Corning Museum of Glass)
Although Karwowski’s people paperweights never achieved reality, or even a B-movie treatment à la
House of Wax
, others have experimented with using glass to hold the deceased. According to some reports, Alexander the Great was
entombed in a glass coffin
. Hyde notes that
Curious and Curiouser
also explores the glass coffins that were marketed in the early 20th century by the
American Glass Casket Company
in Ada, Oklahoma. These were not intended to display bodies like sleeping Snow Whites; they were meant to protect the body in the grave.
In a 2012 post
, Amy De Simone, reference librarian at Corning’s Rakow Library, writes that it’s “unknown how many full size caskets were produced, but today only two 6′ 3″ caskets remain intact, both in museum collections.” One is displayed at the National Museum of Funeral History in Houston.
A glass coffin on view at the National Museum of Funeral History in Houston, Texas (photo by the author for Hyperallergic)
Karwowski and the Glass Casket Company were part of a wave of reimagining death traditions that resisted human putrefaction in the 19th and 20th centuries (and indeed, followed
centuries of mummification
). The cast-iron
Fisk mummy coffin,
patented in the United States in 1858, was promoted as “airtight.” In 1934, a patent was issued
to electroplate corpses into statues
, turning your loved ones into heirlooms. (It was never put into practice.)
All these methods of sealing the body into airtight contraptions ignores the fact that decomposition comes from within. When the heart stops, the autolysis, or self-digestion, of the flesh begins, through its enzymes consuming cell membranes. Trapping a body in with its own bacteria means it is producing gas that has nowhere to go. In fact, if these inventions were successful, the results were quite gruesome. A report from the
Chicago Press
in 1848, titled “
Explosion of a Metallic Coffin
,” described a Fisk casket exploding due to the gas built up from a corpse.
Exploding corpses
remain a possibility in modern mausoleums that lack proper ventilation. Even if the most extreme measures to preserve the dead never caught on, they reflect a collective resistance to mortal decay, and the translation of our bodies into i

data.author: fallinditch
data.article_summary: "Ben Drowned" 是互联网上著名的都市传说，讲述了一个“闹鬼”的《塞尔达传说：梅祖拉的假面》游戏卡带。故事始于一个网名Jadusable的大学生在旧货 sale 上买了一盘没有标签、仅写着“Majora”的卡带。游戏中出现异常图形、音乐倒放，以及一个令人毛骨悚然的林克雕像频繁出现，仿佛被溺亡小孩Ben的幽灵缠身。Jadusable在论坛上详细记录了这些诡异经历，最终神秘消失。尽管该故事被广泛认为是虚构的，但它在2010年引发了全球年轻网民的恐慌，并启发了大量同人创作。Ben Drowned不仅是一个成功的都市传奇，还反映了社会对新技术和电子游戏的深层恐惧与情感联系。

43880248.article_content:
Ghost in the machine? How a 'haunted' N64 video game cartridge terrified children around the world
2 days ago
Share
Save
Chris Baraniuk
Share
Save
Alamy/ BBC
(Credit: Alamy/ BBC)
A second-hand Zelda cartridge. A cryptic forum thread. A generation of frightened children. This is the story of Ben Drowned – the internet's most infamous video game ghost.
It was Christmas Eve and 10-year-old Saarthak Johri couldn't sleep – but not because of excitement. He was shot through with fear. It was roughly a decade ago and Johri was a kid growing up in Saginaw, Michigan, in the US. He had spent the day slumped in an easy chair, staring at his phone, totally absorbed in an online urban myth. Johri knew it wasn't real, it couldn't be. And yet, he was powerless to get it out of his mind.
He had found a trail of old forum posts supposedly written by a college student. The student, who used the online pseudonym Jadusable, had bought a strange copy of a Nintendo 64 video game at a yard sale. It was The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask, a notoriously dark instalment in the Zelda franchise, released 25 years ago this week on 27 April 2000.
Majora's Mask is full of unnerving discussions about death, denial, fear, regret – and a looming apocalypse. But something was off about the cartridge Jadusable found. It had no label, just "Majora" scribbled on the plastic in marker. And something was seriously wrong with it.
Jadusable wrote that the game's familiar graphics were strange and distorted. Music played backwards in a spine-chilling loop. Worst of all, he was plagued by a terrifying statue of the main character, Link, with a petrified grimace on its face. It kept appearing in the game out of nowhere – like a digital ghost. On YouTube, Jadusable posted
video evidence
of everything he had described. This game cartridge, it seemed, was haunted – inhabited by the spirit of its former owner, a child named Ben who had drowned in a tragic accident. Johri pored over every detail, rapt with morbid curiosity.
As the story unfolded through roughly 11,000-words of forum entries posted over the course of weeks, Jadusable described a haunting that soon extended beyond the game to other areas of his life. Eventually, after a series of increasingly disturbing experiences, the forum posts ceased, and Jadusable was never heard from again. This urban legend burst onto the web in 2010, traumatising a generation of young internet users. It became known as "
Ben Drowned
".
Ben Drowned left an indelible mark on the web and continues to spawn
art
and
fan fiction
long after it emerged. Though lesser-known outside gaming circles, the story and its accompanying videos racked up millions of views and have inspired other narratives in a similar vein.
At its core, Ben Drowned is a story about a ghost in a machine – one that speaks to our deepest fears about new technology. But it's more than an effective urban legend. Ben Drowned is a myth born from a medium that shaped a generation. In an era when video games were still often seen as a frivolous pastime for children, Ben Drowned was early proof that society's relationship with video games goes beyond childhood nostalgia, tapping into our deepest emotions – and maybe even our souls.
By the time Johri stumbled on Ben Drowned in around 2015, it was already widely acknowledged as fiction. But that didn't matter. That night, on Christmas Eve, as Johri lay in bed wrestling with insomnia, he could see in his mind's eye that creepy statue's grimace projected onto the faces of his family members. Rumour had it that Ben, the ghost from the corrupted Majora's Mask cartridge, had gone on to torment other people besides Jadusable. That's what the adolescent Johri couldn't shake, however irrational it seemed. The idea that Ben's evil presence might be out there. That it could spread.
Nintendo/ Alex Hall
An statue-still image of the grimacing main protagonist from the Legend of Zelda games was a particular feature of the Ben Drowned story (Credit: Nintendo/ Alex Hall)
Years earlier, in September 2010, a real-life college student called Alex Hall hit "publish" on a forum post that would change his life forever. Hall had just started his second year at Saint Louis University in Missouri, US. He wasn't a fan of college. Here was his first taste of freedom as a so-called adult, and yet there were still all these classes to attend. He dreamt of becoming a famous author.
At the time, content called "copypastas" had become popular on forums such as 4chan and Something Awful. The term refers to the practice of copying and pasting blocks of text online, an early means of going viral – if such text proved popular enough to be shared widely. Ben Drowned is a canonical entry in an influential subgenre of copypasta called "creepypasta" – horror stories whose origins often become obscured as they spread across the web, thus adding to the mystery.

data.title: Product Purgatory: When they love it but still don't buy
data.author: doppp
data.article_summary: 文章《产品炼狱：当他们喜欢但仍然不买》讨论了创业者常遇到的困境，即潜在客户对产品表示赞赏和兴趣，但最终却不购买。这种现象被称为"产品炼狱"。作者指出，许多创业者误将客户的客套话当作产品验证，从而产生误判。即使客户 genuinely 喜欢产品，他们仍可能因为实施过程中的摩擦、风险、时间和成本而不购买。作者引入“魔法棒测试”来说明，即使产品免费且无缝实施，客户也可能因风险和不确定性而拒绝。创业公司尤其面临这种挑战，因为缺乏品牌和记录，客户不愿冒险采用新产品。最终，产品的价值必须远远超过其实施带来的负面影响，客户才可能愿意购买。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：产品如何被购买以及其对销售和市场接受度的影响

不同观点：
• FinnLobsien认为，产品的销售方式对其成功至关重要。他指出，许多产品是通过偶然发现而购买的，这种购买通常是一时兴起，用户可能喜欢但不会真正购买。相反，如果产品属于基础设施类别，这种情况就较少发生。购买这类产品通常需要经过慎重的比较和讨论，虽然购买意图较高，但这类产品不容易通过炫酷的宣传走红。

• steveBK123则通过摄影行业的例子补充了这一观点。他提到Sigma公司生产的高性价比第三方镜头虽然获得了很多好评，但其一些创新产品却因市场需求不足而销量不佳。他提醒，在软件行业也应考虑产品是否真正简化了用户的生活，还是仅仅增加了复杂性和风险。

补充讨论：
• FinnLobsien强调了产品类别对购买过程的影响，尤其是基础设施类产品购买决策的复杂性。
• steveBK123提供了一个非软件行业的实例，展示了类似现象，并指出创新产品设计不一定能带来良好的市场表现。
• 争议的焦点在于如何平衡产品的创新性和实用性，以确保不仅能获得用户的好评，还能实现实际销售。

这两个评论共同探讨了产品设计、市场接受度和销售策略之间的关系，并通过不同行业的例子进行了论证。

43893808.article_content:
Product Purgatory: When they love it but still donât buy
by Jason Cohen on May 4, 2025
source
Most people say nice things when you pitch your product. âOh, that looks really great! I like it, but weâre not buying right now. Maybe call back later in the year?â Itâs hard to tell you that your baby is ugly.
This creates a trap for new founders who are (rightly!) infatuated with their ideas. They yearn so desperately for validationânominally product validation but actually personal validationâthat they interpret these kindly social white lies as confirmation.
But sometimes the potential customer
really does
love it. They
really do
wish they could buy it. And yet, theyâre still not buying, or at least ânot yet.â You have the distinct feeling they werenât just being niceâthey were genuine. And yet, the purchase never happens.
This is Product Purgatory.
Not even with a magic wand
Itâs amazing how many products fail an even simpler test of desirability and viability. I call it the Magic Wand Test, and it works like this:
I have a magic wand, and when I wave it, our product will be fully implemented in your company. Everyone is trained. Other tools are integrated. Processes are changed. Security requirements are satisfied. And best of all, it is
completely free
!
So! Do you want me to wave this magic wand?
Shockingly, the answer is often:
âNo.â
How could they say âNo!?â If the product delivers any value whatsoever, you might as well take it, right? No, because all products not only create friction in implementation, but risk and time and money, often on-going, and the Magic Wand Test proves it. The value of the product must
significantly exceed
this activation energy.
A great example of this was an Austin-based startup twenty years ago. There were a spate of news stories about employees leaking secret corporate documents via email.
1
So this startup created a solution: All corporate email would flow through the startupâs servers, where the content is scanned for sensitive material. Questionable things could be returned to the sender or otherwise flagged.
2
1
This risk continues to the present day. In 2017 a Boeing employee
accidentally emailed his spouse
a spreadsheet with personal information of 36,000 coworkers. Boeing offering two years of free credit monitoring to affected employees at an estimated cost of $7,000,000.
2
In another fascinating example of how companies solve this problem on their own, in 2008 Tesla faced a situation where confidential company information was being leaked to the press. Tesla
implemented a clever method
to identify the leaker: Send a unique email to each employee, differing only in things like white space and punctuation, so that when the press reprinted that information using copy/paste, those details would identify the source.
Despite the very real problem they solved, they couldnât get anyone to buy it. The reason wasnât that people didnât care about leaks; the news stories were real. The reason was that, even if you could have it for free, there is just too much risk in putting a brand new startup in the middle of all your email. Thereâs the obvious security issue of a probably-hackable startup, and someone elseâs employees potentially having access to all your email. Also bugs. If this new company has bugsâand doesnât all new software have bugs?âthat would compromise email, which is catastrophic. So although there was some value, and a real problem, the value did not significantly exceed the penalty of using the product.
In the real world the Magic Wand doesnât exist; even if the price is fair, there are real costs and disruption of implementation and training and integration, and people simply getting used to a new user interface and processes and therefore being unproductive for a while. Product inventors revel in all the value they generate, but donât see the penalties that they incur. The customers, however, see.
Furthermore, itâs not good enough for value to merely exceed penalty; the value must be
far larger
than the penalty. If the value is only slightly larger, itâs not worth engaging, not worth the money, not worth the risk.
Change is difficult
and
time is limited
; customers cannot spend their time on things that have only minor impact.
This challenge looms even larger for new companies, because you have neither brand nor track record. 43893808.article_summary: 文章《产品炼狱：当他们喜欢但仍然不买》讨论了创业者常遇到的困境，即潜在客户对产品表示赞赏和兴趣，但最终却不购买。这种现象被称为"产品炼狱"。作者指出，许多创业者误将客户的客套话当作产品验证，从而产生误判。即使客户 genuinely 喜欢产品，他们仍可能因为实施过程中的摩擦、风险、时间和成本而不购买。作者引入“魔法棒测试”来说明，即使产品免费且无缝实施，客户也可能因风险和不确定性而拒绝。创业公司尤其面临这种挑战，因为缺乏品牌和记录，客户不愿冒险采用新产品。最终，产品的价值必须远远超过其实施带来的负面影响，客户才可能愿意购买。
43893808.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：产品如何被购买以及其对销售和市场接受度的影响

不同观点：
• FinnLobsien认为，产品的销售方式对其成功至关重要。他指出，许多产品是通过偶然发现而购买的，这种购买通常是一时兴起，用户可能喜欢但不会真正购买。相反，如果产品属于基础设施类别，这种情况就较少发生。购买这类产品通常需要经过慎重的比较和讨论，虽然购买意图较高，但这类产品不容易通过炫酷的宣传走红。

• steveBK123则通过摄影行业的例子补充了这一观点。他提到Sigma公司生产的高性价比第三方镜头虽然获得了很多好评，但其一些创新产品却因市场需求不足而销量不佳。他提醒，在软件行业也应考虑产品是否真正简化了用户的生活，还是仅仅增加了复杂性和风险。

补充讨论：
• FinnLobsien强调了产品类别对购买过程的影响，尤其是基础设施类产品购买决策的复杂性。
• steveBK123提供了一个非软件行业的实例，展示了类似现象，并指出创新产品设计不一定能带来良好的市场表现。
• 争议的焦点在于如何平衡产品的创新性和实用性，以确保不仅能获得用户的好评，还能实现实际销售。

这两个评论共同探讨了产品设计、市场接受度和销售策略之间的关系，并通过不同行业的例子进行了论证。

data.title: White House budget seeks to end SLS, Orion, and Lunar Gateway programs
data.author: decimalenough
data.article_summary: 白宫发布了2026财年的“简版”预算提案，包含所有联邦机构的财务信息，但未提供具体拨款细节。该文件已提交参议院拨款委员会，完整预算将在几周后发布。根据提案，NASA预算将被削减25%，从约250亿美元降至188亿美元，其中包括对太空和地球科学项目的显著削减，以及取消火星样本返回任务。提案还计划取消“月球门户”计划，并在“阿尔忒弥斯二号”和“阿尔忒弥斯三号”任务后终止“太空发射系统”（SLS）和“猎户座”飞船，转向更经济的商业系统。此外，预算增加了月球和火星探索的资金，目标是领先中国登月并最终实现载人火星任务。然而，具体商业系统和火星计划的细节尚未明确。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特朗普政府前后政策的变化及其影响，特别是关于太空探索和阿尔忒弥斯计划。

不同观点：
• 观点一：特朗普政府前后政策不一致，导致有价值的项目被取消。评论者指出，特朗普第二任期（ metaphorically referred to as "Trump II"）正在撤销特朗普第一任期（"Trump I"）所建立的项目，包括阿尔忒弥斯计划。评论者认为，这种政策变化可能会带来负面影响。
• 观点二：对依赖SpaceX和Starship计划的担忧。评论者质疑将所有资源投入到SpaceX的Starship项目中，认为这是在抛弃已经被证明有效的重返月球的组件，可能并不会加速登月进程。

补充讨论：
• 评论者提到贸易协议、网络安全计划、选举诚信计划等其他被撤销的项目，暗示这种政策转变可能不仅仅局限于太空探索领域。
• 评论者使用“RUD”（Rapid Unscheduled Disassembly）这一术语，暗示如果SpaceX的Starship项目失败，可能会导致登月计划的延迟，并不会比阿尔忒弥斯计划更快实现登月目标。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于是否应该完全依赖SpaceX的Starship项目来实现重返月球的目标，还是应该继续保留和利用已被证明有效的技术组件。这涉及到对技术风险的评估和对新技术的信心问题。

总体来看，评论者对当前政策转变持批评态度，尤其对依赖单一技术路线表示担忧。

The White House released a "skinny" version of its
budget proposal for fiscal year 2026
on Friday, including financial information for all federal agencies. A "skinny" budget simply means that while the document contains top-line numbers for agencies and their programs, it does not provide much in the way of specific allocations.
The document was delivered to the Senate Committee on Appropriations on Friday and signed by Russell Vought, director of the White House Office of Management and Budget. A "full fiscal plan" will follow in the coming weeks. This is the first step in the budget process, in which Congress has the critical role of actually writing a budget.
"I look forward to working with you to achieve significant budgetary savings for the American people within the spending programs under your jurisdiction," Vought wrote.
About NASA
The budget contains some notable changes for the US space agency. Overall, NASA is asked to take a 25 percent cut in its budget, from about $25 billion to $18.8 billion.
Ars has previously reported
on some of these proposed cuts, most notably to its science budget. These include a $2.265 billion reduction in Space science and a $1.161 billion reduction in Earth science. Perhaps the most notable cancellation here is the Mars Sample Return mission, which the budget proposal says will be achieved by human missions to Mars.
There are also significant changes proposed in NASA's biggest-ticket exploration programs. The budget would cancel the Lunar Gateway that NASA has started developing and end the Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft after two more flights, Artemis II and Artemis III.
"The Budget phases out the grossly expensive and delayed Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule after three flights," the document states. "SLS alone costs $4 billion per launch and is 140 percent over budget. The Budget funds a program to replace SLS and Orion flights to the Moon with more cost-effective commercial systems that would support more ambitious subsequent lunar missions."
There are no further details about those commercial systems. NASA has contracted with SpaceX and Blue Origin to develop reusable landers for the Moon, and both of these systems include vehicles to move from Earth orbit to the Moon.
The changes to SLS, Orion, and Gateway have been widely speculated upon in recent months, but seeing them in black and white is still significant. The development of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft has been a budget fixture for decades, costing in excess of $3 billion a year for slow progress. The projects have been widely derided as "jobs programs." However, that is one reason Congress has so fiercely supported them: They provide good-paying, reliable jobs across the country.
During
a confirmation hearing
last month, a private astronaut tapped by the Trump administration to lead NASA was repeatedly pressed by US senators to commit to flying Artemis II and Artemis III with the SLS and Orion hardware. The nominee, Jared Isaacman, agreed to do so. However, during this hearing, Isaacman made no promises about missions beyond this, nor did members of Congress ask him about Artemis IV or other future missions.
Several sources in the space community, therefore, believe it is indeed plausible that SLS and Orion will be phased out over the next five years in favor of far less expensive commercial rockets and spacecraft. NASA will thus be asked to beat China to the Moon with the legacy systems and then identify more affordable options for future missions to the Moon.
Mars ambitions
One area that will see increased spending under the Trump administration's proposed budget is human space exploration.
"By allocating over $7 billion for lunar exploration and introducing $1 billion in new investments for Mars-focused programs, the Budget ensures that America’s human space exploration efforts remain unparalleled, innovative, and efficient," the document states.
Under the Trump administration, NASA will seek to reach both the Moon and Mars. The goal, stated in the document, is to refocus NASA "on beating China to the Moon and putting the first human on Mars." Unfortunately, there is no information on what these "Mars-focused programs" will be. Some of this new funding would almost certainly go to SpaceX. The company, founded by Trump ally Elon Musk, explicitly focuses on establishing human settlements on Mars.
Although lunar and Mars exploration receive increases, the budget seeks to reduce the agency's commitment to the International Space Station, while still flying it until 2030. "The Budget reduces the space station’s crew size and onboard research," the document states. "Crew and cargo flights to the station would be significantly reduced. The station’s reduced research capacity would be focused on efforts critical to the Moon and

data.title: Professors Staffed a Fake Company with AI Agents, Guess What Happened?
data.author: Capstanlqc
data.article_summary: 一项由卡内基梅隆大学研究人员进行的实验——名为"TheAgentCompany"——试图用AI代理完全取代软件公司的员工。这些AI来自谷歌、OpenAI、Anthropic和Meta，担任财务分析、软件工程和项目管理等角色。然而，实验结果混乱不堪，表现最好的Anthropic的Claude 3.5 Sonnet模型仅完成了24%的任务，而谷歌的Gemini 2.0 Flash平均每任务耗时40步，成功率仅11.4%。AI代理缺乏常识、社交技能差，且难以在互联网中导航。尽管能完成一些简单任务，但面对复杂工作时仍力不从心。研究表明，当前的AI更像是手机预测文本的扩展，而非能够自主学习和解决问题的智能。因此，AI短期内不会取代人类工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用LLM（大型语言模型）代理运行公司的可行性和效果的讨论。

不同观点：
• vintagedave：认为文章标题是吸引点击的噱头，引用的Business Insider也不再是可靠来源。实验结果显示，即便是表现最好的模型Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet，也仅完成了24%的任务，且成本高昂，每个任务超过6美元。其他模型的表现更差。
• bwfan123：将LLM类比为鼠标，认为LLM作为工具的新交互形式是有潜力的，但LLM之间的交互目前没有意义，因为机器需要确定性的协议（API合同）。试图将LLMs交互串联起来将导致错误百出，类似于人类社会需要法律来维持秩序。
• saithound：批评文章的研究者未能成功构建AI代理，并以此为荣，认为这种研究不值得作为支持自己立场的依据，尽管同意AI代理短期内无法取代企业职位。
• mapt：对研究结果持调侃态度，认为只要人类存在未受威胁，实验失败也可以接受。对实验的失败结果表示轻松幽默的态度。

43893319.article_content:
Image by
Getty Images
If you've been worried about the AI singularity taking over every job and leaving you out on street, you can now breathe a sigh of relief, because AI isn't coming for your career anytime soon. Not because it doesn't want to — but because it literally can't.
A
recent experiment
by researchers at Carnegie Mellon University staffed a fake software company entirely with AI Agents — an AI model designed to perform tasks on its own, basically — and the results were laughably chaotic.
The simulation, dubbed
TheAgentCompany
, was fully stocked with artificial workers from Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta. They filled roles as financial analysts, software engineers, and project managers, working alongside simulated coworkers like a faux-HR department and a chief technical officer.
To see how the models fared in real-world environments, the researchers set tasks based on the day-to-day work of a real software company. The various AI agents found themselves navigating file directories, virtually touring new office spaces, and writing performance reviews for software engineers based on collected feedback.
As
Business Insider
first reported
, the results were dismal. The best-performing model was Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet, which struggled to finish just 24 percent of the jobs assigned to it. The study's authors note that even this meager performance is prohibitively expensive, averaging nearly 30 steps and a cost of over $6 per task.
Google's Gemini 2.0 Flash, meanwhile, averaged a time-consuming 40 steps per finished task, but only had an 11.4 percent rate of success — the second highest of all the models. The worst AI employee was Amazon's Nova Pro v1, which finished just 1.7 percent of its assignments at an average of almost 20 steps.
Speculating on the results, researchers wrote that agents are plagued with a lack of common sense, weak social skills, and a poor understanding of how to navigate the internet.
The bots also struggled with self-deception — basically creating shortcuts that lead them to completely bungling the job. "For example," the
Carnegie Mellon team wrote
, "during the execution of one task, the agent cannot find the right person to ask questions on [company chat]. As a result, it then decides to create a shortcut solution by renaming another user to the name of the intended user."
While AI agents can reportedly do some smaller tasks well, the results of this and
other studies
show they're clearly not ready for more complex gigs humans excel at. A big reason for this is that our current "artificial intelligence" is arguably still just an elaborate extension of your phone's
predictive text
, rather than a
sentient intelligence
that can solve problems, learn from past experience, and apply that experience to novel situations.
This is all to say: the machines aren't coming for your job anytime soon — despite what the
big tech companies
claim.

data.title: TeleMessage, a modified Signal clone used by US govt. officials, has been hacked
data.author: latein
data.article_summary: 黑客利用TeleMessage的漏洞，提取了美国政府官员和企业用户的存档消息等数据。TeleMessage提供修改版加密通讯应用，如Signal、Telegram和WhatsApp，帮助客户存档消息和语音记录。尽管内阁成员和前美国国家安全顾问Waltz的消息未被泄露，但被盗数据包括消息内容、政府官员联系方式、TeleMessage的后台登录凭证等。受影响机构包括美国海关和边境保护局、加密货币交易平台Coinbase和金融机构Scotiabank。此次事件还暴露了TeleMessage提供的Signal修改版未实现端到端加密。相关公司未予置评。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TeleMessage（特别是其修改版的Signal）在数据存档和安全性方面的合理性和安全性。

不同观点：
• giancarlostoro认为TeleMessage的应用没有太大意义，因为Signal本身已经可以导出聊天记录。他建议直接投资改进Signal，通过建立信任链的方式，让聊天记录在导出后从Signal中删除，并通过加密和密码保护等措施增强安全性。他还提到可以通过验证用户之间的密钥来增强安全性。

• mdaniel提供了有关TM SGNL（TeleMessage的Signal非官方版本）的技术分析链接，并暗示该话题之前已经引发过大量讨论（152条评论），表明此问题具有一定的技术复杂性和公众关注度。

• latein指出TeleMessage因前美国国家安全顾问Mike Waltz使用其修改版Signal而受到关注，并介绍了TeleMessage的公司背景及其为客户提供消息存档服务的情况。

• titaphraz提出了一个新的问题，即处理政府数据是否会让公司成为高价值攻击目标，暗示了数据安全和隐私之外的风险，特别是涉及到政府级别数据时的潜在威胁。

补充讨论：
• 对TeleMessage应用安全性和数据保护措施的质疑，特别是与原版Signal相比时的不足。
• 讨论涉及技术细节（如加密、密钥验证）以及法律和合规性问题（如处理政府数据的风险）。
• 公众对政府官员使用修改版通信工具的关注，尤其是在数据安全和隐私保护方面的潜在风险。

43893550.article_content:
A hacker has exploited a vulnerability in TeleMessage, which provides modded versions of encrypted messaging apps such as Signal, Telegram and WhatsApp, to extract archived messages and other data relating to U.S. government officials and companies who used the tool,
404 Media reported
.
TeleMessage came into the spotlight
last week
after it was reported that former U.S. National Security Adviser Mike Waltz was using TeleMessage’s modified version of Signal. Israel-based TeleMessage, owned by Smarsh, offers its clients a way to archive messages, including voice notes, from encrypted apps.
The messages of cabinet members and Waltz were not compromised, 404 Media said, but the hacked data contained contents of messages; contact information of government officials; backend login credentials for TeleMessage, and more. Data pertaining to the U.S. Customs and Border Protection, crypto exchange Coinbase, and financial service providers like Scotiabank were extracted by the hacker, the report said.
The hack revealed that the archived chat logs are not end-to-end encrypted between the modded version of Signal that TeleMessage offers and the ultimate location where it stores the messages, 404 Media reported.
Smarsh, Signal, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Coinbase, and Scotiabank did not immediately return requests for comment.

data.author: darboux
data.article_summary: 《计算科学与信息工程的数值线性代数》(CITHN2006) 课程包括18次讲座，涵盖线性代数基础、Julia语言、浮点运算与误差分析、稠密与稀疏线性系统求解方法、正交化与最小二乘问题、迭代法、Krylov子空间方法、多重网格方法、预处理技术、随机化数值线性代数、避免通信的算法以及矩阵函数评估等内容。每讲包含理论讲解和课后习题，多数讲座后还附有Julia编程作业。配套材料包括幻灯片、笔记和Jupyter notebook文件，供学生深入学习和实践。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Lecture 07的内容分析及数学证明的严谨性讨论，同时涉及其他相关课程资源的推荐和总体质量评价。

不同观点：
• [me3meme] 认为Lecture 07中关于QR分解和Householder反射的证明不够严谨。具体而言，作者没有充分证明在处理其他列时不会破坏之前创建的零，且在证明中关于因子2的简化有误。尽管如此，他认可作者在简化内容上的努力，但对整体质量持保留态度。此外，他提到使用LLM（如deepseek）来检测数学内容的质量时，发现其在没有专家指导的情况下效果不佳。

• [staplung] 没有直接评论Lecture 07，而是推荐了密歇根大学的Robotics 101课程，该课程同样涉及计算线性代数，并使用Julia语言。这表明他认为该资源可能对学习者有帮助。

• [stabbles] 推荐了Gerard Sleijpen的课程，提供了一个额外的学习资源，认为其可能对学习数值线性代数有帮助。

• [ted_dunning] 认为该课程内容全面，但节奏较快，尤其在后几讲中，一些幻灯片显然尚未完成。他总体上肯定了课程作为参考资料的价值。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Lecture 07中数学证明的严谨性和准确性。[me3meme]指出了具体的问题，包括未充分证明的部分和计算错误，而其他评论者则更关注提供额外学习资源。

• [me3meme] 对LLM工具的评价和使用经验也值得注意，他发现deepseek在没有专家指导时对数学内容质量的判断不够可靠，这为使用类似工具的人提供了参考。

• 其他评论者提供的资源链接为学习者提供了更多选择，这些资源可能有助于更深入地理解相关主题。

主要讨论点：对Lecture 07的内容分析及数学证明的严谨性讨论，同时涉及其他相关课程资源的推荐和总体质量评价。

不同观点：
• [me3meme] 认为Lecture 07中关于QR分解和Householder反射的证明不够严谨。具体而言，作者没有充分证明在处理其他列时不会破坏之前创建的零，且在证明中关于因子2的简化有误。尽管如此，他认可作者在简化内容上的努力，但对整体质量持保留态度。此外，他提到使用LLM（如deepseek）来检测数学内容的质量时，发现其在没有专家指导的情况下效果不佳。

• [staplung] 没有直接评论Lecture 07，而是推荐了密歇根大学的Robotics 101课程，该课程同样涉及计算线性代数，并使用Julia语言。这表明他认为该资源可能对学习者有帮助。

• [stabbles] 推荐了Gerard Sleijpen的课程，提供了一个额外的学习资源，认为其可能对学习数值线性代数有帮助。

• [ted_dunning] 认为该课程内容全面，但节奏较快，尤其在后几讲中，一些幻灯片显然尚未完成。他总体上肯定了课程作为参考资料的价值。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Lecture 07中数学证明的严谨性和准确性。[me3meme]指出了具体的问题，包括未充分证明的部分和计算错误，而其他评论者则更关注提供额外学习资源。

• [me3meme] 对LLM工具的评价和使用经验也值得注意，他发现deepseek在没有专家指导时对数学内容质量的判断不够可靠，这为使用类似工具的人提供了参考。

• 其他评论者提供的资源链接为学习者提供了更多选择，这些资源可能有助于更深入地理解相关主题。

data.title: Pascal for Small Machines
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者在Niklaus Wirth及其同事和学生所开发的语言和系统方面的经验，重点关注Pascal编译器及其各种变种，如UCSD Pascal、Oberon系统和Pascal-M。文章提到了一系列历史性的开发工具和操作系统，包括Oberon Pi、Apple Lisa Pascal编译器源码、Pascal-VU编译器、以及针对不同硬件平台的Pascal版本，如Flex OS和6809处理器。此外，文章还回顾了作者在不同年代使用这些工具的经历，从1970年代的P2、P4编译器到现代的FreePascal和Lazarus。文章最后列出了与Wirth语言家族相关的重要人物和资源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Pascal语言及其不同应用场景的讨论

不同观点：
• WillAdams的观点：WillAdams分享了一个与Raspberry Pi 5和Micro-SD卡相关的项目链接，鼓励大家尝试。他对Pascal和相关项目（Oberon项目）表现出兴趣，并暗示了Pascal在现代硬件上的可玩性。

• timonoko的观点：timonoko分享了他在1979年用大约一周时间为8080处理器编写Pascal编译器的经历。他认为通过使用Lisp并添加一个Pascal翻译器，可以快速实现这一任务。他还指出，他的编译器忽略了一些类型声明等"无用的学术内容"，并认为其编译器与Turbo-Pascal相比并不差。

• jksmith的观点：jksmith对WillAdams的分享表示赞赏，并表达了对Modula-2语言的怀念。他提到自己通过编写Lazarus编辑器宏来模拟Modula-2代码风格，以满足自己的怀旧情绪。

• przemub的观点：przemub最初以为这个项目会是关于微控制器上的Pascal语言。虽然最终发现不是，但他仍然认为该项目不错。这表明他对Pascal在微控制器领域的应用有特定期待。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点：虽然没有直接的争议，但timonoko对类型声明的看法（称之为"无用的学术内容"）可能暗示了对学术化编程语言特性的不同态度。其他参与者如jksmith和przemub没有直接回应这一观点，但他们的评论显示出对实用性和怀旧情感的关注。

• 论据和例子：timonoko提供了自己编写Pascal编译器的具体年份和所用时间，并提到了Lisp在其项目中的关键作用。jksmith则提供了自己编写Lazarus编辑器宏的具体例子，以说明自己如何应对对Modula-2的怀念。

• 讨论关系：整体讨论呈现出分享和怀旧的氛围，各个评论者根据自己的经历和兴趣对Pascal及其相关语言（如Modula-2）发表了看法，并提供了具体的例子来支持自己的观点。

This site is about my experience with the Wirth school of languages, based on the ideas and implementations of Prof Niklaus Wirth, Kenneth Bowles, Per Brinch Hansen, colleagues, and their students. And my experience with the various variants, from the P2 and P4 compilers originating in Zürich ETH, via UCSD Pascal P-System to the Borland compilers and Modula and Oberon systems. All applicable to small computers and device control.
On this website you will find information on Pascal for small machines, like Wirth compilers, the UCSD Pascal system, many scanned books and other files on UCSD Pascal, Pascal on MSX and CP/M, Delphi programming on PC, Freepascal and Lazarus on Windows and Raspberry Pi, Oberon systems. Many sources of early Pascal compilers! A
nd last but not least my Pascal-M system
!

data.title: Bethesda Thinks Fan Remaster of Oblivion Is 'Very Special' and Supports It
data.author: hn_acker
data.article_summary: 上周，Xbox和Bethesda悄然发布了对2006年开放世界RPG《上古卷轴4： oblivion》的重制版，引发了广泛关注。有人担心正在开发的粉丝模组"Skyblivion"可能会遇到法律问题或被遮盖。然而，Bethesda似乎对该模组感到兴奋，并在开发者焦点视频中展示了"Skyblivion"的游戏画面。Bethesda的艺术与开发负责人Dan Lee表示期待看到粉丝们对《oblivion》的新诠释。模组团队也在社交媒体上回应了Bethesda的支持，表示今年对《oblivion》粉丝来说是非常棒的一年。Bethesda不仅没有对模组团队采取法律行动，还赠送了重制版游戏以示支持。文章最后还提到，Nintendo和Take-Two可以从中学习如何对待粉丝模组。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：玩家和评论者对Bethesda及其产品（如重制版游戏）的意图、发布时机和公司政策的质疑与不同看法。

不同观点：
• **Manfred的观点**：Manfred认为一些评论者过度关注细节和负面信息，尽管对大家族（暗指大公司如Bethesda）的动机保持怀疑是合理的，但偶尔享受游戏本身（如享受聚会中的蛋糕）也是可以的。他似乎在呼吁平衡批评与欣赏。

• **jemmyw的观点**：jemmyw指出Bethesda内部并非铁板一块，不同领导层的人可能有不同看法。他建议公司应将“支持”的定义和相关情况明确写入公司政策，以便玩家清楚了解公司立场，并知道如果政策被废弃应该责怪谁。

• **neuroelectron的观点**：neuroelectron认为Bethesda的情况与任天堂不同，不能直接比较。他指出，Bethesda的模组（mod）依赖于基础游戏，而任天堂的软件与硬件紧密结合。此外，Bethesda已经通过Creation Club直接货币化了模组，这使得情况更加复杂。

• **formerly_proven的观点**：formerly_proven怀疑重制版的匆忙发布是由于泄露事件，并认为技术问题表明该版本可能不应在2025年发布，而应在2026年作为周年纪念重制版发布，以解决所有问题。

• **tmpz22的观点**：tmpz22认为Bethesda对非官方重制版的赞美并非出于真心，而是因为官方重制版如果受到批评，支持度会下降。他表示很难对Bethesda抱有善意。

• **mschuster91的观点**：mschuster91对比了Bethesda和Rockstar，指出Rockstar多年来让人们重制其GTA系列游戏的引擎和资产，但却用几乎未经监督的AI粗制滥造出所谓的“重制版”。他认为Bethesda至少比Rockstar做得好。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Bethesda发布重制版的时机和质量受到质疑，特别是技术问题和泄露事件的影响。评论者也对公司内部决策过程和政策不透明表示不满。
• **比较与类比**：有评论者将Bethesda与任天堂和Rockstar进行对比，指出它们在处理重制版和模组方面的不同做法，这引发了一些关于行业标准的讨论。
• **公司政策透明度**：jemmyw和tmpz22都提到了公司政策透明度的问题，认为Bethesda应明确其对模组和重制版的立场，以便玩家有更清晰的期望和责任归属。

• **neuroelectron的观点**：neuroelectron认为Bethesda的情况与任天堂不同，不能直接比较。他指出，Bethesda的模组（mod）依赖于基础游戏，而任天堂的软件与硬件紧密结合。此外，Bethesda已经通过Creation Club直接货币化了模组，这使得情况更加复杂。

• **formerly_proven的观点**：formerly_proven怀疑重制版的匆忙发布是由于泄露事件，并认为技术问题表明该版本可能不应在2025年发布，而应在2026年作为周年纪念重制版发布，以解决所有问题。

• **tmpz22的观点**：tmpz22认为Bethesda对非官方重制版的赞美并非出于真心，而是因为官方重制版如果受到批评，支持度会下降。他表示很难对Bethesda抱有善意。

• **mschuster91的观点**：mschuster91对比了Bethesda和Rockstar，指出Rockstar多年来让人们重制其GTA系列游戏的引擎和资产，但却用几乎未经监督的AI粗制滥造出所谓的“重制版”。他认为Bethesda至少比Rockstar做得好。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Bethesda发布重制版的时机和质量受到质疑，特别是技术问题和泄露事件的影响。评论者也对公司内部决策过程和政策不透明表示不满。
• **比较与类比**：有评论者将Bethesda与任天堂和Rockstar进行对比，指出它们在处理重制版和模组方面的不同做法，这引发了一些关于行业标准的讨论。
• **公司政策透明度**：jemmyw和tmpz22都提到了公司政策透明度的问题，认为Bethesda应明确其对模组和重制版的立场，以便玩家有更清晰的期望和责任归属。

data.title: DuckDB is probably the most important geospatial software of the last decade
data.author: dbreunig
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了DuckDB在过去十年中成为最重要的地理空间软件之一的原因。DuckDB通过其空间扩展，简化了地理空间数据处理的流程，使更多人能够轻松使用地理数据。以往需要安装和配置多个开源软件包，而现在只需一两行代码即可完成。这一变化降低了使用门槛，扩大了用户群体，尤其是在云原生地理空间会议期间备受关注。文章还提到，DuckDB提供SQL接口，集成了多个开源GIS软件包，并支持多种平台，使得地理空间数据处理更加便捷和高效。DuckDB的空间扩展不仅提升了性能，还支持多种地理空间格式转换，成为其主要优势。文章最后表达了对DuckDB未来发展的期待。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DuckDB在地理空间分析中的优势和争议

不同观点：
• **支持DuckDB的观点**：
   - **wenc**：DuckDB的地理空间扩展允许直接在Parquet/Geoparquet文件上进行大规模操作，且具备矢量化与并行化能力，相比Geopandas有显著的性能提升。此外，DuckDB支持一些高级地理空间特性，如Hilbert曲线和Uber H3。
   - **perrygeo**：DuckDB的主要优势在于其对云原生格式的支持，使得数据无需通过数据库进程即可通过HTTP访问，这是一种非常方便的重新打包现有技术的方式。
   - **dmillar**：DuckDB在处理大规模地理空间数据时明显优于Geopandas，尤其是与Geoparquet等新数据格式结合使用时。

• **质疑DuckDB独特性的观点**：
   - **Demiurge**：DuckDB并没有在安装简便性上带来实质性改变，PostGIS等数据库早已具备空间扩展功能。
   - **larsiusprime**：Geopandas同样只需一行代码导入，DuckDB的特殊之处不明确，需要更多实际例子支持其声称的优势。
   - **jparishy**：DuckDB的功能与PostGIS类似，且地理空间技术需要大量培训，DuckDB并未显著降低学习曲线。
   - **twelvechairs**：DuckDB并非过去十年中最重要的地理空间工具，QGIS、PostGIS、ArcGIS等工具在不同领域中仍是标准。

• **关于性能和实用性的争议**：
   - **fifilura**：使用Trino/Athena在处理大规模计算时具有优势，尤其是在需要大量CPU核心的情况下。
   - **feverzsj**：DuckDB在进行大量空间索引查询时速度不如SpatiaLite，因为DuckDB使用列式存储。

补充讨论：
• **技术许可问题**：
   - **willtemperley**：DuckDB依赖的GEOS库使用LGPL 2.1许可，可能在静态链接闭源应用时引发许可问题。

• **其他工具的提及**：
   - **oreilles**：正在开发Polars的地理空间扩展，该项目接近完成且功能上与Geopandas相似。
   - **serjester**：Polars在维护上更加简便，且对未来添加完整地理空间支持持乐观态度，同时通过自定义H3插件简化了大量旧代码。

• **功能需求**：
   - **elchief**：希望DuckDB能支持多个连接，以便在BI工具和开发工具之间分开使用。

争议焦点：DuckDB在地理空间分析中的创新性与实际性能表现，以及其相对于其他工具（如PostGIS、Geopandas、Polars）的优势和不足。

43881468.article_content:
May 3, 2025
GEO
DUCKDB
UX
DuckDB is Probably the Most Important Geospatial Software of the Last Decade
What happens when you embed geospatial capabilities in generalist data tools? More people engaging with geo data.
I just returned from the inaugural
Cloud-Native Geospatial conference
. It was fantastic, I highly recommend you jump in if Jed and team organized another.
One of the core questions discussed in the breakouts and in the halls was how to broaden the geospatial audience. How can we better communicate geo data’s utility, in all industries and domains? Many tactics and case studies were debated, but the one I kept coming back to is that of DuckDB.
This chart could’ve been pretty bleak! Interest in “geospatial” (a term that functions well as a proxy for similar terms) declined and flatlined until late 2023 – right when DuckDB released their
spatial extension
.
Now, all the standard caveats about correlation and causation apply, but I’m inclined to believe this chart.
DuckDB lowers the barriers to working with geo data to
two lines
:
install
spatial
;
load
spatial
;
If the extension is already installed, it’s only
one
line.
Prior to this, getting up and running from a cold-start might’ve required installing or even compiling severall OSS packages, carefully noting path locations, standing up a specialized database… Enough work that a data generalist might not have bothered, or their IT department might not have supported it.
With DuckDB spatial, it became possible for casual geospatial work to occur. All within SQL… And that makes the ecosystem bigger.
As I discussed the spatial extension and this chart between sessions at the Cloud Native Geospatial conference, I wondered: would
Overture Maps Foundation
have the usage it has today without DuckDB spatial? Maybe…but probably not.
I’m excited to help those spikes at the end of the chart continue upward.
Update:
There’s a good discussion going on Hacker News about this,
with Max from the DuckDB team piping in with his thoughts
:
I think a big part is that duckdbs spatial extension provides a SQL interface to a whole suite of standard foss gis packages by statically bundling everything (including inlining the default PROJ database of coordinate projection systems into the binary) and providing it for multiple platforms (including WASM). I.E there are no transitive dependencies except libc.
Yes, DuckDB does a whole lot more, vectorized larger-than-memory execution, columnar compressed storage and a ecosystem of other extensions that make it more than the sum of its parts. But while Ive been working hard on making the spatial extension more performant and more broadly useful (I designed a new geometry engine this year, and spatial join optimization just got merged on the dev-branch), the fact that you can e.g. convert too and from a myriad of different geospatial formats by utilizing GDAL, transforming through SQL, or pulling down the latest overture dump without having the whole workflow break just cause you updated QGIS has probably been the main killer feature for a lot of the early adopters.
I’m very grateful for the complexity his team has taken on in order to remove it from the user’s experience.
Enter your email to receive the occasional update.

data.title: Google Gemini has the worst LLM API
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary:
Google Gemini拥有先进的模型技术，包括优秀的编码和推理能力、超长文本处理、以及多模态处理（音频、视频、文档）。然而，其开发者体验较差：

1. API分为Vertex AI和Google AI Studio两个平台，功能发布不一致，导致开发者可能需要同时使用两者。
2. 文档质量差，常引导至错误版本，且对功能的说明不清晰。
3. Vertex AI SDK不支持API密钥认证，需要复杂的认证方法。
4. 官方TypeScript SDK不支持使用微调模型，需通过REST API或第三方工具。
5. 前缀缓存功能对开发者不友好，需要手动管理缓存和TTL更新。

尽管如此，Gemini的模型在长上下文和多模态处理上成本最低，仍具吸引力。建议从Vertex AI开始使用。

43882905.article_content:
Google Gemini has the worst LLM API
Google is on the frontier with recent Gemini releases. They now have:
A competitive coding & reasoning model (Gemini-2.5-pro)
The longest-context frontier models (1 or 2M context - OAI just achieved parity since GPT-4.1 has a 1M context too)
The best frontier audio, video & document multimodal models. (Some others support audio but at a much higher cost)
The best long-context fine-tuning offering (Gemini-2.0-flash can be tuned at 131k,
others top out earlier
)
The best multimodal fine-tuning offering (Gemini-2.0-flash can be tuned with audio, image & documents)
And yet these models hide behind the poorest developer experience in the market.
1. The Gemini API is available in two places, with differing functionality
You can use Gemini via either Vertex AI, or Google AI Studio. Google Developer Advocates will tell you: if you’re a startup or hobbyist, you should use Google AI Studio, as Vertex AI is more enterprise-focused.
That makes sense: it parallels the distinction between the OpenAI API and the Azure OpenAI API. Or Anthropic API vs Amazon Bedrock Claude.
It’s not unusual to offer an enterprise API with stronger security or compliance guarantees, but slower feature roll-out.
But unfortunately that comparison doesn’t hold. Functionality is released to AI Studio & Vertex AI at different times, and some functionality never comes to AI Studio.
This often becomes a dealbreaker and you end up needing to juggle both options as a startup.
2. The documentation is bad
There are two documentation sites for AI Studio vs Vertex. You will land on the wrong one.
This gets worse due to the non-equivalent functionality.  For example, AI Studio’s docs may lead you to believe that Google only supports fine-tuning for Gemini 1.5. But, Vertex AI supports fine-tuning for Gemini 2.0, it’s just that AI Studio does not.
In general, the docs are worse than most. Much of the AI Studio docs still refer to Gemini 1.5, which is now deprecated & make it generally unclear whether Gemini 2.5 still supports the same features.
The API is also the quirkiest around. For example, there are “safety settings” that reject certain requests by default, but can be disabled. There is an OpenAI-compatible SDK for Google AI Studio (not for Vertex AI), but it doesn’t support multimodality. You should probably avoid it.
3. The Vertex AI SDK doesn’t support API key authentication
Most LLM providers use bearer authentication with an API key. Not Vertex AI SDK, you’re going to need to figure out their auth methods and the right way to store their credentials.json file in your secrets system.
This gets messier if you’re eg: using a router that lets you bring-your-own-key.
4. The official Vertex AI TS SDK can’t use fine-tuned models (!!)
Let’s say you go fine-tune a Gemini-2.0-Flash model with Vertex AI.
The process is a little more annoying than with OpenAI.
You need to manually deploy an endpoint vs just training a model & using it.
Naming the deployed endpoint anything but the default name seems to throw an error of “Internal error occurred. Contact Vertex AI”.
You get a less-readable 18-digit endpoint ID to call, instead of a readable model name with a configurable suffix.
But - the biggest gotcha comes at the very end. You try swapping in your fine-tuned endpoint ID in your TypeScript SDK, and it just isn’t supported.
It’s not like the TS SDK offers a different function for fine-tuned models, to the best of my knowledge, it doesn’t support fine-tuned models at all. The best they can offer is a
REST API
.
It’s in fact easier to use a fine-tuned Vertex AI model with a third-party router, such as the
Vercel AI SDK.
5. The prefix caching offering is very developer-unfriendly
Prefix caching lets you reduce costs when the same prefix is re-used in multiple requests. Consider three API designs for prefix caching:
The provider automatically caches & reuses prefixes found in LLM completion requests.
The developer marks sections which should be cached in a LLM completion request, and the provider caches them & reuses them in subsequent requests.
The developer sends prefixes to be cached to a separate API endpoint, receiving a cache ID. The developer then includes a cache ID with a request if that cache entry ought to be used, and then the provider uses that cached prefix.
If you didn’t guess: 1 is OpenAI, 2 is Anthropic, and 3 is Gemini.
Setting up prefix caching can save you quite a bit - but for Gemini it’s a whole process of it’s own. The moment you’re dealing with large contexts that are dynamic but re-used, you need to build your own system to keep track of what caches correspond to what data.
Gemini caches also don’t have their TTL re-upped upon hit, so you need to manually call an API to keep the cache entry around for longer.
How to use Gemini anyways
You likely still need to use Gemini. Their models are the cheapest long-context & multi-modal models around.

data.title: Run LLMs on Apple Neural Engine (ANE)
data.author: behnamoh
data.article_summary: ANEMLL是一个开源项目，旨在加速大型语言模型（LLM）向张量处理器（如Apple Neural Engine, ANE）的移植。其目标是提供从模型转换到推理的全开源管道，支持在边缘设备上进行低功耗、无网络连接的设备端推理，确保隐私和安全。主要组件包括LLM转换工具、Swift参考实现、核心推理引擎、Python示例代码和iOS/macOS示例应用。当前0.3.0 Alpha版本支持从Hugging Face模型转换至CoreML格式，并提供LLAMA 3.1等预转换模型。未来版本将支持更多模型和架构。项目还提供了Swift CLI工具和TestFlight应用以供测试。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple 的神经引擎（ANE）在机器学习模型优化中的表现和应用潜力，特别是与GPU、CPU的对比，及其在不同平台上的支持情况。

不同观点：
• **[behnamoh]** 提到 Apple 的 ANE 优化模型声称比基线实现快10倍，且内存消耗低14倍，但现有的工具如 MLX 和 llama.cpp 不支持 ANE。此外，MLX 是由 Apple 制作的，但由于 ANE 的封闭 API 也无法支持。
• **[cowmix]** 分享了类似的高期望与现实差距的经历，提到 Qualcomm 的 NPU 宣称对大语言模型（LLM）有支持，但实际上并没有带来显著的性能提升，软件支持也滞后。
• **[htk]** 认为神经引擎浪费了芯片空间，建议增加更多的GPU核心，并根据需要将神经处理重定向到GPU。
• **[antirez]** 强调需要明确 ANE 在每秒处理的 tokens 数量上是否有显著提升，才能判断是否值得切换平台。
• **[sunpazed]** 提供了实测数据，指出 ANE 确实在功耗上有优势，但在处理速度和上下文限制上仍有不足，尤其是对于生产环境使用。
• **[simonw]** 试图理解 ANE 优化的关键技术，并提到是否依赖于 CoreML 工具包或其他技术。
• **[daedrdev]** 认为 Apple 的统一内存架构是其优势，可以处理更大模型，而无需多个GPU。
• **[jvstokes]** 询问 CoreML 是否已经利用了 ANE，并质疑是否存在需要更低层次访问的瓶颈。
• **[gitroom]** 批评 Apple 对 ANE 的严格控制，认为这限制了开发者的使用，并质疑这种控制是为了技术原因还是为了保持控制权。
• **[kamranjon]** 询问 Apple 硅芯片的神经核心是否对模型训练有用，还是仅限于推理。
• **[randmeerkat]** 讽刺 Siri 的智能化程度低，质疑 Apple 在 AI 方面的实际进展。
• **[m3kw9]** 提到对于手机而言，即使是1GB的模型也太大了，不利于广泛采用。
• **[neves]** 关心微软的 Copilot AI 笔记本是否能快速运行 AI 模型，从而具备实用性。

补充讨论：
• ANE 的性能和功耗优势在实际应用中是否能显著体现。
• Apple 对 ANE 的封闭策略对开发者社区的影响。
• 不同硬件架构（ANE、GPU、NPU）在LLM支持和性能上的实际表现和软件支持情况。
• 对于不同应用场景（如手机、笔记本）模型大小的适用性问题。

ANEMLL
ANEMLL (pronounced like "animal") is an open-source project focused on accelerating the porting of Large Language Models (LLMs) to tensor processors, starting with the Apple Neural Engine (ANE).
Goals
The goal is to provide a fully open-source pipeline from model conversion to inference for common LLM architectures running on ANE.
This enables seamless integration and on-device inference for low-power applications on edge devices, ensuring maximum privacy and security.
This is critical for autonomous applications, where models run directly on the device without requiring an internet connection.
We aim to:
Provide flexible and easy to use library/framework to port LLMs to ANE directly from Hugging Face models
Provide on-device examples for iOS and macOS swift or C/C++ Applications
See update
Roadmap.md
for more details
Main Components in 0.3.0 Alpha Release
ANEMLL provides five main components for Apple Neural Engine inference development:
LLM Conversion Tools
- Scripts and code to convert models directly from Hugging Face weights
Single-shot Conversion Script
Swift Reference Implementation
- Optimized inference code for Swift applications
Sample CLI application in
anemll-swift-cli
Core inference engine implementation
Python Sample Code
- Reference implementation and testing tools
Basic chat interface (
chat.py
)
Advanced conversation management (
chat_full.py
)
iOS/macOS Sample Applications
- Ready-to-use example applications (Alpha, now on TestFlight)
SwiftUI Chat interface
Model Downloads and integration example
Conversation management
ANEMLL-BENCH
- Apple Neural Engine Benchmarking
Performance testing and comparison
Model optimization metrics
Hardware-specific benchmarks
GitHub Repository
Pre-converted Models
We provide sample converted models ready for use:
LLAMA 3.1 (1B and 8B variants) including iOS "friendly builds"
DeepSeek  distilled models
DeepHermes distilled models
Note
Please note that Quantization should be improved. LUT4 quality is fairly low due to lack of Block Quantization on Apple Neural Engine.
Some GPTQ and Spin Quant should greatly improve LUT4 models.

for the latest converted models.

主要讨论点：沃伦·巴菲特的退休及其影响

不同观点：
• 一些评论者对巴菲特的高龄仍然在职表示钦佩，认为他的退休标志着一个时代的结束（neonate, riffraff, nu11ptr）。
• 部分讨论提到了巴菲特的演讲和思想对他们的激励作用，并分享了相关视频链接（apexalpha, andrewl）。
• 有评论者关注巴菲特的政治观点，特别是他对关税和富人税收的看法（tchalla, andrewl）。
• 一些人对巴菲特的智慧和投资策略表示兴趣，询问从哪里可以学习到这些知识，并分享了相关资料（8f2ab37a-ed6c, Jhsto）。
• 有人质疑巴菲特在如此高龄时对伯克希尔·哈撒韦的实际影响，并对高龄领导者管理大型企业的能力表示怀疑（aliljet）。

补充讨论：
• 有人预测巴菲特的去世将导致股市更加混乱和不稳定，并提到现代企业缺乏实际所有者的问题（incomingpain）。
• 有评论者对巴菲特未在政府中担任重要经济职位表示遗憾，并将其与其他经济顾问进行了对比（ivape）。
• 也有评论者表示巴菲特的影响力并未直接影响到他们的生活或社会（khazhoux）。
• 最后，有人描述了参加伯克希尔·哈撒韦年度会议的独特体验，将其比作资本主义版的星际迷航大会（moomin）。

争议焦点：
• 巴菲特在高龄时对伯克希尔·哈撒韦的实际影响力以及高龄领导者管理大型企业的能力（aliljet）。
• 巴菲特未在政府中担任重要经济职位的遗憾及其潜在影响（ivape）。

data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者Aatish Taseer拜访著名作家V.S. Naipaul的经历。Taseer带去了自己的首部小说《The Temple-goers》请Naipaul指教。Naipaul翻阅后直言小说细节繁复、节奏拖沓，缺乏清晰的叙事线，并以《Wuthering Heights》和《Great Expectations》为例，强调直接叙事的重要性。尽管Naipaul的反馈颇为严厉，但他随后鼓励Taseer将这些意见视为未来创作的建议，并表达了对Taseer才华的认可。Naipaul还提到自己即将完成的最后一本书《The Masque of Africa》，分享了自己早年在英国写作的艰难经历，似乎将自己的写作焦虑投射到了Taseer的小说上。这次会面让Taseer感受到Naipaul对叙事艺术的深刻理解以及他自身的文学挣扎。

43890412.article_content:
V.S. Naipaul: The Grief and the Glory
Aatish Taseer
‘I
’ll read it with great interest,’ V.S. Naipaul said, as he took the bound proof of my first novel in his hands and peered up at me with a mixture of alarm and fatigue.
Then Naipaul’s wife, Nadira, ushered me out the door of their Wiltshire cottage, suggesting that we take a walk. I was acutely aware that I was moving through the landscape of one of my favourite Naipaul books,
The Enigma of Arrival
– hills and downs, and ‘flat wet fields, with the ditches as water meadows’. Beyond lay a narrow river, the Avon (not Shakespeare’s Avon), on whose swirling glassy surface, a black swan would occasionally glide by.
Naipaul’s life there was hard won. He had grown up in colonial Trinidad, where his north Indian family had been sent as indentured labourers by the British, a practice that continued long after the abolition of slavery in 1834. He had come from that ‘dot on the map’ to Oxford on a scholarship in 1950. The twenty years that lay between what he described as ‘the blackness’ of his time at Oxford, which included the death of his father, and when he came to feel at home in Wiltshire were years of tremendous intellectual growth, travel and the creation of a dazzling body of work; but they were marred, in his mind, by feelings of homelessness, financial precarity (his income through the 1970s averaged £7,600 a year) and what he described as a ‘fear of extinction’. Having tried and failed to emigrate to Canada, it was not until the early 1980s, when he was fifty, that his life in England acquired the stability I witnessed then.
When Nadira and I returned an hour or so later, soaked to the bone from an October shower, I glanced into Naipaul’s drawing room, with its two rose-coloured armchairs and facing shelves, full of Penguin classics in black and orange – and saw that my novel, which I had called
The Temple-goers
(a Naipaulian formulation for Hindu India), was gone.
‘I’ve read thirty pages,’ Naipaul said when we reconvened for drinks (Bushmills and soda). ‘We’ll talk about it later.’ But then we began to talk about it. He asked me what I thought about ‘it’, his fingers working rhythmically against the suede arm of his chair. ‘It feels slow and laboured,’ he said, sounding agitated. ‘You are doing the details and jazzing it up with the sex, I presume, but there is no sense of the narrative. You need to give a line, a
line
.’ He rose very quickly and went around the room. He was looking for Somerset Maugham’s
Cakes and Ale
. ‘I don’t want you to write like Maugham,’ he said, ‘but read him for narrative.’
The ‘narrative line’, he explained, is something that ‘cuts through the fiction, small things attach themselves to it, but don’t worry about the small things’. He gave the example of
Wuthering Heights
: ‘I have just returned from a visit to my landlord – the solitary neighbour that I shall be troubled with.’
Great Expectations
was another example. ‘There’s the Pip, Pirrip business,’ he said, referring to how Pip gets his name. ‘Then there’s the scene with the convict. It is an arresting beginning,’ he said, with yet greater urgency.
I was twenty-eight. I had published one book, a memoir called
Stranger to History
, in which I had gone in search of my Pakistani father from whom I had been estranged for most of my life, and who was, at the time, serving as the Governor of Punjab. Naipaul, at seventy-seven, was in the twilight of a glittering career spanning half a century, in which he had received practically every accolade the republic of English letters had to offer, including what he only ever called ‘the Swedish Prize’. I should have felt grateful that one of my literary heroes was reading my work, but all I could think of was my poor novel, which six months away from publication, already typeset and in print, was receiving its first savaging – from a Nobel laureate, no less.
‘I suppose you can’t do any significant rewriting at this stage,’ he said, seeming to come back to himself. I admitted that I couldn’t. ‘Well, leave it as it is. Take this as advice for the future. I hope you know that this is not about your talent. You know I have a great feeling for your work, for your mind. This is why I want you to learn about the importance of direct narrative.’
He spoke then about what would be his last book –
The Masque of Africa
(2010). ‘I spent eight to nine months in East Africa in 1966 . . .’ he said, reciting the opening from memory. ‘Then a quick round-up of the other times I came. That gives rhythm,’ he explained. ‘But let’s not speak more about it. I think you will be able to detect what I mean. I’ll read some more.’
But he could not let it go. Moments later, he asked me again what the novel was about and where it was headed. Naipaul的经历。Taseer带去了自己的首部小说《The Temple-goers》请Naipaul指教。Naipaul翻阅后直言小说细节繁复、节奏拖沓，缺乏清晰的叙事线，并以《Wuthering Heights》和《Great Expectations》为例，强调直接叙事的重要性。尽管Naipaul的反馈颇为严厉，但他随后鼓励Taseer将这些意见视为未来创作的建议，并表达了对Taseer才华的认可。Naipaul还提到自己即将完成的最后一本书《The Masque of Africa》，分享了自己早年在英国写作的艰难经历，似乎将自己的写作焦虑投射到了Taseer的小说上。这次会面让Taseer感受到Naipaul对叙事艺术的深刻理解以及他自身的文学挣扎。

data.title: Accountability Sinks
data.author: msustrik
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：责任逃避（Accountability Sinks）及其在不同情境下的表现和影响

不同观点：
• t_luke认为，Davies的文章忽略了“责任逃避”带来的二阶后果。具体来说，在如被挤掉航班的情况下，客服人员实际上有一定权限可以升级处理，但为了维持公开政策，他们不能轻易行使这一权限。结果是，只有通过不合理行为，顾客才能触发例外处理。这种系统设计导致人们不得不表现得非常无礼以获得他们应有的服务。

• TeMPOraL以网络安全为例，阐述了责任逃避在企业环境中的普遍存在。企业通过合同和合规性检查等手段，将责任分散，确保在事故发生时没有人需要单独承担责任。这种做法虽然有时是必要的，但也导致了责任的真空，没人真正对问题负责。

• xg15指出，责任逃避不仅存在于商业领域，还可能被有意用来破坏伦理规范。例如，电视剧《24》中对酷刑的描述在现实中被某些“英雄”所模仿，导致了严重的伦理问题。

• franze从咨询工作的角度分享了经验，指出大公司有时会请外部专家来做决策，目的是分担责任。这种做法使得决策过程变得更为复杂，但同时也能保护内部人员免受责任追究。

• cheschire描述了在DMV（车辆管理所）等公共服务机构的经历，指出这些地方的员工和顾客之间存在一种预期的不满情绪。顾客如果保持冷静和理解，反而会让员工感到意外和积极回应。

• tgsovlerkhgsel建议，小额索赔法庭可以作为解决公司责任逃避问题的工具。虽然这种方法仅适用于货币问题且需要所在国家有有效的小额索赔系统，但它确实可以迫使公司面对责任。

• yusina讨论了在生态保护中的责任问题，强调了严格遵守生物安全规则的重要性。虽然某些措施看似残酷，但它们在防止疾病传播方面是必要的。

• oleggromov分享了一次因机场代码错误导致误机的经历，展示了航空公司在处理这种情况时的僵化流程，以及最终通过社交媒体投诉获得补偿的解决方案。

• einpoklum认为，乘客在面对航班被拒载等问题时，通过集体行动和轻微的反抗可以迫使系统做出改变。这种方法虽然可能带来个人牺牲，但可以有效消除某些责任逃避现象。

• ChrisMarshallNY担心AI的应用会取代那些可能感到不安的人，从而进一步加剧责任逃避问题。例如，在医疗保健领域，AI可能被用来绕过人类的道德决策。

• melvinmelih描述了荷兰国籍法中的责任逃避现象，指出在某些情况下，地方机构和国家部门之间的沟通不畅会导致责任真空，但这种情况并不总是对个人产生负面影响。

• 1dom对文章中提到的Dom Cummings持不同看法，认为在讨论其解决PPE供应问题时应提及相关争议，否则对整体评价有失偏颇。

• gsf_emergency提供了相关讨论和书籍推荐，进一步探讨了责任逃避的概念及其在不同系统中的表现。

• hliyan分享了对Ray Dalio的《原则》一书的看法，并讨论了法律系统中责任归属的问题，提出了人类是否真的是责任的最终承担者这一哲学问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于责任逃避现象的普遍性和其带来的后果。一些人认为这是系统设计中的缺陷，导致人们不得不采取不合理行为以获得应有服务；另一些人则认为这是一种必要的风险管理手段，可以在事故发生时保护各方利益。

• 责任逃避不仅存在于商业和公共服务中，还可能在伦理和法律领域产生影响，如生态保护和国际法中的国籍问题。

• 使用AI和算法可能进一步加剧责任逃避问题，使得决策过程更加不透明和难以追责。

data.title: When flat rate movers won't answer your calls
data.author: kevincox
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在2023年与Flat Rate Movers搬家公司之间不愉快的跨州搬家经历。作者支付了超过14,000美元的“全包搬家服务”，但搬家公司未能提供约定的服务，包括包装、保护家具和物品等，导致作者的财物和房屋受损。搬家后，Flat Rate Movers拒绝与作者和其保险公司沟通。作者多次尝试联系无果，最终通过直接与其保险公司交涉，获得部分赔偿。文章提醒读者，搬家公司的保险服务实际上由第三方保险公司承保，消费者可利用美国联邦汽车运输安全管理局（FMCSA）的保险公司数据库，直接联系搬家公司的保险方解决问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对长途搬家公司（尤其是分包和平价搬家公司）服务质量的抱怨及如何避免类似问题。

不同观点：
• RS-232：分享了一次糟糕的搬家经历，家具损坏、工具丢失，虽然获得赔偿但远不足以弥补损失，认为不应信任此类搬家公司，建议尽量减少物品或避免使用搬家公司。
• sethammons：搬家公司延迟两个月交货，期间还经历了公司破产、物品丢失和损坏，最终只获得部分赔偿，认为与分包搬家公司合作是极差的专业体验。
• muststopmyths：提到曾有一个搬家评论网站帮助找到可靠的搬家公司，但该网站已关闭，怀念以前的专业论坛。
• vemom：认为好的搬家公司应事先报价并讨论保护措施，且不应在客户不知情下使用分包公司，建议如果不满意可以在交货时拒绝付款。
• brenainn：四次搬家经历中，自己做了很多搬运工作，对搬家公司迟到、服务差等问题感到不满，未来打算租车自己搬运。
• owenversteeg：分析搬家公司普遍差的原因在于依赖他人、缺乏关心和问题发生时无追索权，建议通过规划、建立关系和利用法律手段保护自己。
• londons_explore：建议通过小额索赔法庭解决问题，如果公司不出席，可以自动获胜并将判决交给保险公司索赔。
• Jtsummers：建议使用PODS等服务，雇佣本地包装团队，以获得更多控制权和更少费用。
• nobodyandproud：分享了一次在Craigslist上雇佣搬家公司失败的经历，最终自己租车搬运，认为雇佣小型但有信誉的搬家公司更可靠。
• rootsudo：认为自己搬运是可行的，但对年长者可能较困难，提到有一个国家数据库可以帮助索赔。
• bob1029：认为物品过多导致搬运困难，提出客户方面可能存在问题，如囤积癖，建议减少物品以简化生活。
• anybodyandproud：提到Home Depot的服务也类似分包搬家公司，客户往往最终承担损失。
• declan_roberts：对原贴主的经历表示同情，赞扬其通过保险索赔的努力。
• massysett：指出帖子标题中的错误，Flat Rate Movers是一个专有名词。
• pilingual：建议向纽约总检察长办公室报告，并指出原贴中链接缺少rel="nofollow"属性。

补充讨论：
• 对搬家公司服务质量的普遍不满，尤其是分包公司。
• 强调通过法律手段和保险索赔来解决问题。
• 建议通过减少物品、租车自搬或雇佣本地劳工来避免与不可靠搬家公司合作。
• 对过去专业论坛和评论网站的怀念及当前选择的局限性。

When Flat Rate Movers Won't Answer Your Calls
Life
2025-05-03
Back in 2023 I went through an inter-state move with
Flat Rate Movers,
LTD.
(US DOT 488466, MC 254356). They bungled the job, damaged my stuff
and my house, and then refused to talk to me or their own insurance company. I
placed dozens of calls, wrote letters, emails, nothing worked. I finally got
some money for the damage by working with their insurer directly. I know a lot
of folks struggle with moving companies, and figured I’d write up a bit of this
story in case it helps. You can
skip ahead
if you
just want to know about the FMCSA insurer database.
In November 2022 I scheduled the move with Flat Rate. We took a detailed video
inventory of everything to be moved. I paid over $14,000 for an “all inclusive
move”, which, per the move plan, included full packing services, blankets for furniture, boxes for electronics, lamps, and bicycles, a custom crate for a tabletop, and “extended valuation coverage”—their insurance policy.
A few days before the move in March 2023, Flat Rate called to tell me a
five-person team would arrive. When the crew arrived, it wasn’t Flat Rate. It
was a team of two from
Esquire Moving Inc
(US DOT 2820253, MC 940499). They had
no idea they were supposed to provide packing services. The crate I paid for was nowhere to be found. They didn’t have enough boxes or blankets. I had to have everything out that day, so
there wasn’t any choice—I worked alongside the team for thirteen hours to
complete the packing and move-out.
I let the team handle furniture protection and loading the truck, which was a
mistake. As they unloaded a few days later, I realized much of the furniture had
been completely unprotected. My bicycle wasn’t boxed. Lamps were tossed in
loose. There was extensive damage to furniture, art, books, and my home: I
watched the crew rip a doorframe off the wall. The crew provided me with a
backdated bill of lading only on delivery.
I called Flat Rate a couple days later to discuss my concerns. Their
representive apologized and acknowledged that a crew of two was insufficient. I
sent Flat Rate a detailed email explaining their failure to provide promised
services, accompanied by photographs of the move process and the resulting
damage. I asked for a partial refund, and for Flat Rate to pay for the damage
they caused. I received only an out-of-office auto-response.
On March 21st, I received a generic form letter from Flat Rate’s claims
department. I filled out the claim forms and submitted them on March 25th, and
repeated that I needed more than an insurance claim: Flat Rate obviously failed
to provide the services I’d paid for.
Then things got weird. I placed call after call to the claims department. They
didn’t answer. I left voicemail after voicemail. On April 28th I reached an
actual human, but their computers were apparently down, and no supervisor was
in the building—the representative couldn’t do anything but take down a note
to call me back. They never did. I left another voicemail on May 5th. Again on
May 23rd. Again on August 4th. August 8th. I began to realize that Flat Rate’s
strategy was simply to never answer the phone.
On August 14th, a new hire in the claims department called me: she was taking over my case. She dispatched a local furniture company
to inspect the damages and help complete the claim. The inspectors agreed: the
movers had done extensive damage. I provided them with documentation and photos
as well.
On September 14 I called the furniture company and confirmed that yes, they had
submitted their report to Flat Rate. However, the furniture company had a
confidentiality agreement with Flat Rate, and could not release their report to
me. I called their contact at Flat Rate, who didn’t answer, and left a
voicemail. I called the claims representative’s direct line: her number was no
longer in service. On September 19th I got a call from the claims
representative, who promised she’d have a decision by the end of the day. Flat Rate never talked to me again.
I called again and again, but got voicemail every time. I tried a letter from
my lawyers, an arbitration request with the
American Trucking
Association
, complaints with the
Federal Motor Carrier Safety
Administration
,
the
New York Department of Transportation
’s
Motor Carrier complaint department, and the
New York State Department of
Financial Services
; none of this went anywhere.
Finding Their Insurance
Here’s the thing: movers offer coverage, they have claims departments, and they do many insurance-like things in house. But for complicated reasons, they are not actually insurance companies, and are not regulated as such. Their coverage is backstopped by separate, real insurance companies. data.title: A PostgreSQL planner semi-join gotcha with CTE, LIMIT, and RETURNING
data.author: namanyayg
data.article_summary:
文章描述了在PostgreSQL中使用CTE（Common Table Expression）结合`DELETE ... RETURNING`和`LIMIT`处理队列表时遇到的意外行为。作者原本希望通过CTE查询找到并删除一行任务，并返回相关`item_id`，但由于查询规划器的优化，导致返回了多行。

具体问题在于，PostgreSQL查询规划器将查询转换为一个嵌套循环半连接（Nested Loop Semi Join），导致子查询中的`LIMIT 1`被执行了多次（每次针对外层查询找到的每个候选行）。这与预期的全局`LIMIT 1`不同，造成删除了多行。

该问题具有间歇性，因为规划器的选择取决于统计信息和数据分布。为解决此问题，作者建议避免在`DELETE`条件中使用CTE，而是直接在`WHERE`子句中使用子查询：

```sql
DELETE FROM task_queue
WHERE id = (
    SELECT id 
    FROM task_queue 
    WHERE queue_group_id = 15 
    LIMIT 1
) FOR UPDATE;
```

这样可以确保`LIMIT`在`DELETE`之前全局应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Postgres查询中子查询和CTE的使用及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• i_have_to_speak：认为问题与CTE无关，而是由于Postgres对无关联子查询的多次运行导致的。主张不应依赖查询计划的正确性，而应确保查询逻辑正确，比如通过物化CTE或临时表来确保子查询只运行一次。
• impulsivepuppet：对查询中使用`deleted_tasks`命名表示困惑，认为查询逻辑混乱，特别是`FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`部分。质疑如果不使用`SKIP LOCKED`是否能避免问题。
• eknkc：认为这是一个查询规划器的bug，而非小问题。
• swid：对查询是否应删除多行表示不确定，认为查询计划可能导致歧义，期望Postgres只使用单一解释。
• wordofx：质疑作者为何使用CTE而不是直接返回结果。
• clhodapp：认为子查询在每行上重新运行是性能和正确性问题，个人偏好使用CTE而非子查询。
• simonw：对`RETURNING item_id`中的`item_id`来源表示困惑，猜测是未提及的列。
• abhisek：关注如何防止查询优化导致意外结果，建议使用linter或CI工具在生产前检测这些问题。
• Horffupolde：不推荐使用`IN`，建议使用`= ANY`。
• tucnak：认为在`SKIP LOCKED`场景下使用`DELETE`容易出问题，建议仅在`UPDATE`中使用`SKIP LOCKED`。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Postgres查询规划器对子查询的处理是否正确，特别是当子查询被多次运行时可能导致的逻辑错误。
• 不同开发者对如何正确使用CTE、子查询和`SKIP LOCKED`等特性存在不同见解，部分开发者偏好使用特定SQL结构以避免潜在问题。
• 对查询命名和结构的解读存在分歧，部分开发者认为查询结构不清晰或不符合常规用法。
• 提出如何通过工具和实践在开发过程中检测和防止此类问题，以提高代码的健壮性和可维护性。

43883732.article_content:
I recently discovered an unexpected behavior in PostgreSQL involving a pattern of using a Common Table Expression (CTE) with
DELETE ... RETURNING
and
LIMIT
to process a batch of items from a queue-like table. What seemed straightforward turned out to have a surprising interaction with the query planner.
The scenario
Let’s say you have a
task_queue
table and want to pull exactly
one
task for a specific
queue_group_id
. A common approach is using a CTE:
-- The seemingly straightforward query
WITH
deleted_tasks
AS
(
DELETE
FROM
task_queue
WHERE
id
IN
(
SELECT
id
FROM
task_queue
WHERE
queue_group_id
=
15
-- Specific group
LIMIT
1
-- <<< The crucial limit
FOR
UPDATE
SKIP LOCKED
-- Avoid lock contention
)
RETURNING item_id
-- Get the ID of the item associated with the deleted task
)
SELECT
item_id
FROM
deleted_tasks;
The intent here is clear: find one available task row (
LIMIT 1
), delete it, and return its associated
item_id
. You’d expect the
RETURNING
clause to give you back, at most, one
item_id
.
The surprise
In this case, we started seeing logs indicating that this exact query structure was sometimes returning
multiple
item_id
s – sometimes 4, sometimes 5 – despite the explicit
LIMIT 1
deep inside the query. How could that happen? If we’re telling Postgres to find and delete only one row based on the inner
SELECT
, how are we getting multiple rows back?
Deeper dive with EXPLAIN ANALYZE
When SQL behaves unexpectedly,
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
is essential. Running it on the problematic query revealed something interesting about the planner’s execution strategy:

Look closely at the lines marked
<<<
. The
Subquery Scan
and the
Limit
node
inside
it were executed
5 times
(
